## Phase 6c slice PT: player-placed tracking (C32) (FROZEN 2026-10-13 after Steward's review)

API: the next free minor at merge (house rule; placeholder `PT` below), mod to match, `KIT_VERSION` next minor. Steward ask
C32 (steward-mc docs/ARCHITECT-ASKS.md), approved by Noah 2026-10-13 and refined by him the same day: PT is about **builds**,
not every block. It replaces the dropped draft above. The PLAN "Keep open: zones" rule holds: no id is built from an owner
string, and nothing persisted assumes an owner never changes.

- **Branch:** `slice/PT`, worktree `../architect-mc-PT`. **Spend:** $0. Builds after T2, in parallel with P0.
- **Scope:** record every block a player places (the foundation), group those blocks into **builds**, keep builds from every
  Architect write path unless the caller explicitly names them, and offer builds to plans as features. Claim and release.
- **Not in scope:** adopting a build as a site (slice **PT2**, outlined at the end); blocks placed by commands, dispensers or
  other mods' tools (§2); zones and transfers (Keep open).
- **Depends on:** C31 (v0.24.1), B (`Destruction`), P0 (`plan/0`, frozen 2026-10-12: changes here are additive only).

### Answers to Steward's three questions (C32), in the light of builds

1. **Cost.** On disk, about **3 bytes per tracked block** while a section holds at most 256 (2-byte position, 1-byte palette
   index) and a 512-byte mask plus at most 2 bytes per block above that; about **24 bytes per touched section** and **16 bytes
   per distinct placer per chunk**, saved inside the chunk itself (chunk NBT is compressed on top). In memory, O(1) lookups:
   sparse sections about 8 bytes per block, dense ones 4.6 KB. The hot path (every block change) adds one attachment lookup.
   Builds add one index record per build (about 200 bytes plus its footprint).
2. **Blocks placed before PT.** Unknown, and never guessed as a player's. They are treated as natural unless the voxel table
   classes them non-natural (planks, glass, doors: today's cell-level protection, unchanged), they are journal-owned, or they lie
   in a C17 area. **The gap:** natural-looking blocks (logs, dirt, stone, sand) a player placed before PT, and builds made
   only of them, are not builds. Mitigation: "claim my build" (§8) marks a box as a build; an inferred scan is an open question.
3. **Named refusals.** Yes, by build: a refusal names each blocking build (id, kind, blocking count) and its first 8 blocking
   cells with their block ids, plus the total; region and stroke findings carry the same list. Incidental blocks never refuse.

### 0. Facts (v0.24.1)

- "Natural" has two readers: the kit's voxel table (`VoxelTable`, a block not listed is `PLAYER`; every vanilla log is `LOG`)
  and 4e's `TerrainFit.flags` / `CellCond.natural` (natural ground, plants, trees, air, water). Neither knows who placed a block.
- `site/TileCheck` (regions and strokes): stage 0 skips `others` (another owner's journal cells) and failed conditions; C31's
  `trees()` flood stops at the claim, `others`, the owner's C17 areas and non-LOG logs, as `tree_kept.<reason>`.
- `PlayerBlocks.scan` (1.9.0, `Reason.PLAYER_BLOCKS`) refuses a LAYER lot on a region pad over non-natural, non-BE, unowned
  blocks. Every other placement overwrites such blocks (journaled, given back on remove).
- B's `Destruction.PLAYER_BLOCKS` clears unowned non-natural cells for an online actor at permission 2 (N-B-1).
- Undo and remove restore only cells still holding the entry's `after` (StillOurs), so a player's later block is kept.
- `LevelChunkMixin` already hooks `LevelChunk.setBlockState` (ChangeTracker, WriteCounter). `placement/Occupancy` is entities
  only and is unchanged by PT.
- Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3 bundles `fabric-data-attachment-api-v1` 2.2.30 with chunk targets (`SerializableChunkDataMixin`).

### 1. Data: the per-chunk set

- **Where.** A Fabric data attachment `architect_mc:placed` on `LevelChunk`, persistent (a Codec), never synced to clients.
  It is written into the chunk's own NBT, so the set and the blocks it describes save together; a side file under
  `<world>/architect/` could disagree with the blocks after a crash. Every change calls `markUnsaved` on the chunk.
- **Per chunk:** `placers`: a palette of UUIDs (at most 254; the 255th distinct placer in one chunk records as unknown, 0xFF);
  `builds`: a palette of build ids (§4); `sections`: the touched sections by Y.
- **Per section, on disk (JournalNbt v2's own rule):** at most 256 cells: `p` (2 bytes per cell, the 12-bit local position,
  ascending); more: `m` (a 4096-bit mask, 64 longs). Then, in the same order, `o` (1 byte per cell, the placer index; omitted
  when the chunk has one placer) and `b` (1 byte per cell, the build index, 0 = incidental; omitted when uniform).
- **Cost.** Sparse 2-4 bytes per block; dense 512 bytes plus 0-2 per block; about 24 bytes of NBT per section and 16 per placer.
  A 9x7x9 log cabin (about 330 blocks, two sections, one placer): about 1.1 KB before the region file's compression.
- **In memory.** Sparse sections: an open-addressed `short -> short` map (placer, build), about 8 bytes per block at its load
  factor; at 257 cells a section turns dense: a `long[64]` bitset plus a `short[4096]` (4.6 KB). Lookup: the chunk (callers
  hold it), the section by Y, a bit or map probe: O(1). Chunks with no attachment cost nothing.
- **Mod removed.** Unknown attachments should stay in the chunk NBT untouched; a gate item checks it (§11 item 12) instead of
  this draft asserting it.

### 2. Events: what records a block

- **A player places it.** Hooks on `ServerPlayerGameMode.useItemOn` and `useItem` open a scope (the acting player, the clicked
  position); inside it the chunk hook records every cell that goes from air, a fluid or a replaceable block to a block:
  - `BlockItem` placements, every cell they set (both halves of a door, bed or tall plant; signs; seeds and crops; lily pads);
  - buckets: the placed fluid source (water, lava) and powder snow; flowing fluid is never recorded;
  - tool conversions on a cell within 1 of the click: hoe (farmland), shovel (path), axe (stripped log, scraped copper) record
    the converted cell (a farm's farmland and a path count);
  - **not recorded:** bone meal growth, fire, spawn eggs, and anything farther than 2 cells from the click.
- **Survival and creative alike.** Commands (`/setblock`, `/fill`, `/clone`) are not recorded (N-PT-7).
- **Pistons.** `PistonBaseBlock.moveBlocks` reads each moved cell's record into the `MovingPistonBlockEntity` (an NBT key
  `architect_mc:placed` with the placer UUID and build id, so a chunk saved mid-move keeps it); when the moving block settles,
  the destination is recorded with it. A block the piston destroys is cleared. A falling block (sand, gravel, concrete powder)
  carries its record on the `FallingBlockEntity` the same way.
- **Ownerless placements are not recorded:** dispensers, endermen, snow golems, other mods' machines. A mod's fake player that
  goes through `useItemOn` is recorded under its UUID. Claims by the console record the nil UUID ("unknown placer", §8).
- **Architect's writes never record**, even inside a player scope (an Architect tool used by a player): the writer's scope
  (UpdateMask's style) turns recording off.

### 3. Events: what clears a block

- **The rule:** a record is cleared when its cell becomes **air or a fluid**, when **another placement replaces** it (then
  re-recorded for the new placer), or when **Architect writes** the cell. Breaking (any tool, any player), explosions, fire,
  fluids washing a torch away and pistons all reach the first case through the same `setBlockState` hook.
- **Kept through in-place changes:** a cell that stays a block keeps its record: copper weathering and waxing, grass spreading
  onto placed dirt and farmland drying back, concrete powder setting, crops growing, a log stripped, waterlogging. A rule of
  "the block changed, so clear" would untrack every copper roof and dirt-floored cabin.
- **Architect's journaled writes.** A write (region tile, stroke, site, road, cells, delta) captures each cell's record into
  the journal before it writes (§5) and clears the record with the write. Remove and undo restore the record exactly.

### 4. Builds

The raw set is the foundation; **enforcement applies to builds**. A tracked cell that is not in a build is **incidental**.

- **Structural cells.** Voxel class can't decide builds (C32's case is an all-log cabin: natural by class). A tracked cell
  is **fill** when it is natural-looking and lies at or below the surrounding untracked ground (the median surface of the
  untracked columns within 3); every other tracked cell is **structural**. Farmland, crops and bucket sources count as
  structural even when flush (farms). A patched hole or a levelled patch of dirt is fill, so it stays incidental.
- **Components.** Structural cells joined when within 2 of each other (Chebyshev; a one-block gap, a door, a fence line).
  The flood is bounded at 65,536 cells and runs over loaded chunks only; a build reaching unloaded chunks keeps its stored ids
  there and is merged when they load.
- **Promote** a component to a build when it has at least **40 structural cells** (**24** when at least half of them are
  non-natural by class) and spans at least 3 in two axes, and one of: an entrance (a door, fence gate or trapdoor at its
  ground); an enclosure (at least 8 air cells with a structural cell above within 6 and walls on 3 of 4 sides within 8); at least
  16 farmland or crop cells; or at least 96 structural cells.
- **Demote** (hysteresis) only when it falls below **20** structural cells, or below 48 with no qualifier left, on two
  evaluations 60 s apart. A claimed build (§8) never demotes. Classification runs 5 s after the last change in a component
  (debounce), so a house under construction or a creeper hole doesn't flicker.
- **Ids.** `build-<n>` from a per-world counter in `<world>/architect/builds.json` (temp file, then rename), never from
  geometry or an owner string. A component takes the id of the build it shares most cells with. **Merge:** the oldest id
  survives, the others are kept as aliases (`mergedInto`). **Split:** the largest part keeps the id, the others take new ids.
- **The index** (`builds.json`, per dimension): id, dimension, bounds, footprint (column runs per z), entrances, kind and
  confidence, structural count, placers (UUID and cell count), state (`ACTIVE`, `CLAIMED`, `RELEASED`), aliases, first and last
  change times, and a revision bumped on every change. The per-cell build index (§1 `b`) makes "which build is this cell in" O(1).
- **Entrances:** each door, fence gate and ground trapdoor in the build, with its position (lower half) and facing; the
  apron is the 3 cells outside it.
- **Kind guess** (append-only enum): `HOUSE` (an entrance and an enclosure, or a bed), `BARN` (an enclosure over 200 floor
  cells), `FARM` (farmland and crops are the majority of the footprint), `WALL` (at most 2 thick, at least 8 long, no roof),
  `TOWER` (height at least twice the footprint's longer side), `PATH` (path blocks are the majority), `OTHER`; plus a
  confidence 0-1. The share of non-natural blocks feeds the guess and the lower promote bar, not a hard rule.

### 5. Undo restores tracking exactly

- `JournalNbt` sections gain an optional `pt` member: the indexes (into the section's cell order) of cells that were tracked
  before the write, with their placer and build index into file-level `ptu` (UUIDs) and `ptb` (build ids) lists.
- **A file that holds `pt` is written as `JournalNbt.VERSION` 3; every other file stays 2.** An older mod refuses a v3 file
  (4e's downgrade rule) instead of rewriting it without `pt` and losing the flags silently. Reads of v1 and v2 are unchanged.
- Undo and remove write `before`, then restore its record (placer, build id; an alias resolves to its survivor; a build gone
  meanwhile leaves the cell incidental and the component is re-classified). Cells StillOurs keeps (the player changed them
  since) keep their current record. Exact means: the tracked set, each placer and each build id equal the pre-write state.
- Cost: only cells tracked before the write carry `pt` (about 2 bytes each), so terrain-only writes add nothing.

### 6. Placers and owners

- Records hold placer UUIDs only. Settlement owners (`<modid>:<thing>`) never enter the set, the index or an id, so a later
  `transferOwner` (Keep open) moves nothing here.
- **The caller-supplied rule.** Steward decides which builds belong to which settlement. A request that should touch a build
  carries `BuildConsent(Set<String> buildIds, @Nullable UUID actor)`: only builds it names explicitly, and for each named build
  the actor must be one of its placers (at least 10% of its cells) or hold permission level 2. Unnamed builds still refuse.
- A build's **primary placer** (most cells) is what Steward shows ("Alex's house"); per-placer counts are in the index.

### 7. Enforcement: every write path consults it

| Path | Rule (a build cell = tracked and in a build; incidental cells are natural) |
|---|---|
| `TileCheck` stage 0 (regions, strokes) | a build cell is skipped as `build` (beside `owned`), counted `player_build` and `player_build.<id>` |
| `TileCheck.trees()` (felling) | the flood stops at a build cell: `why = "build"`, counted `tree_kept.build`; an incidental log may be felled |
| `TileCheck.leaves()` | a leaf in a build is never held or written |
| `TileCheck.dependents()` and supports | a natural cell that holds up a build cell (a torch, door, ladder, rail, crop, sign, or a gravity block above) is kept as `player_build.support` |
| Region plan (kit) | builds in the claim are hard keep-outs for lots, forms and connectors, with a 1-cell margin and each door's apron |
| Brush strokes | `NATURAL_ONLY` skips build cells; `PLAYER_BLOCKS` clears only builds named in its consent, by a placer or an op (N-PT-5) |
| `Sites` place/check, batch building and move | the snapshot box (approach, foundation) holding build cells refuses `PLAYER_BUILD` for every caller, LAYER or not |
| `placeRoad` / `checkRoad` | a road cell on a build refuses; with `partial` it is a skipped span naming the build |
| `placeCells` / `checkCells` (`naturalOnly`, `CellsCheck`, `InfraPlace`) | build cells are skipped (`naturalOnly`) or refuse `PLAYER_BUILD` |
| `fitToLot`, `minLotSize` | a lot holding build cells is not a fit (`PLAYER_BUILD`, the builds named); the recommended rect avoids them |
| Approaches | an approach stops before the first row on a build cell, as at a road (4e) |
| `applyDelta` / `checkDelta` | `KEEP` as today; `OVERWRITE` writes incidental player edits as today, but build cells need consent, else `PLAYER_BUILD` |
| Remove, undo, `undoStage` | unchanged (StillOurs), plus §5's restore |

- **Incidental cells are natural**, whatever their voxel class (a torch, a cobble block, a filled hole): `IF_NATURAL`, fits
  and `naturalOnly` may write them without refusal; they are journaled and come back, with their records, on undo. Block
  entities keep their own rules (BLOCK_ENTITIES, B's journaled NBT); an incidental chest is never cleared silently.
- **Untracked non-natural blocks** (pre-PT, other mods) keep today's cell-level rules; 1.9.0's `PLAYER_BLOCKS` keeps its meaning.
- **`force` does not override a build.** Only consent does. A behaviour change, listed (N-PT-6).
- **One predicate.** `Placed.build(level, chunk, pos)` is the single test every row above calls; a JVM test lists the paths.

### 8. Claim and release

- **Claim:** `/architect build claim <x0 y0 z0 x1 y1 z1>` and `Sites.claimBuild(...)`: marks every non-air, unowned cell in the
  box that isn't another placer's (journal-owned cells are never marked) as the claimer's, and makes them one build in state
  `CLAIMED` (no promote bar, no demotion). For builds placed before PT, made of logs, dirt or stone.
  - Non-op players: a box of at most 32x32x32, within 64 blocks of them, at most 8 claims each; ops: any box up to 4,096x4,096
    columns (C17's bound), sliced at 2 ms a tick. Console claims record the nil placer.
- **Release:** `/architect build release <id>` and `Sites.releaseBuild(id, actor)`, by a placer or an op: the build becomes
  `RELEASED`; its cells stay tracked but incidental, and they are not promoted again unless claimed or grown by 25% since.

### 9. API (next free minor; additive and binary compatible)

```java
// Sites; each default throws "needs Architect API <PT>"
Optional<PlacedBy> playerPlaced(ResourceKey<Level> dim, BlockPos pos);           // empty: not tracked (or not loaded)
PlacedBox playerPlaced(ResourceKey<Level> dim, BoundingBox box);                  // loaded chunks only; counts, builds hit
List<Build> builds(@Nullable ResourceKey<Level> dim, @Nullable BoundingBox within);
Optional<Build> build(String id);                                                  // aliases resolve to the survivor
Build claimBuild(ResourceKey<Level> dim, BoundingBox box, @Nullable ServerPlayer actor);
Build releaseBuild(String id, @Nullable ServerPlayer actor);
record PlacedBy(UUID placer, @Nullable String buildId) {}                        // placer nil: unknown (a console claim)
record PlacedBox(int tracked, int incidental, Map<UUID, Integer> byPlacer, List<BuildHit> builds) {}
record Build(String id, ResourceKey<Level> dimension, BoundingBox bounds, int[] footprint, List<Entrance> entrances,
             BuildKind kind, float confidence, int cells, Map<UUID, Integer> placers, BuildState state, long revision) {}
record Entrance(BlockPos pos, Direction facing, String blockId) {}
record BuildHit(String buildId, BuildKind kind, int blocking, List<BlockHit> first) {}  // first: at most 8
record BlockHit(BlockPos pos, String blockId) {}
record BuildConsent(Set<String> buildIds, @Nullable UUID actor) {}
enum BuildKind { HOUSE, BARN, FARM, WALL, TOWER, PATH, OTHER }    // append-only
enum BuildState { ACTIVE, CLAIMED, RELEASED }                     // append-only; PT2 appends ADOPTED
```

- **Reason** (appended): `PLAYER_BUILD`. Not a widened `PLAYER_BLOCKS` (S-PT-2).
- **Refusal** gains trailing `List<BuildHit> builds` (old constructor: empty); `ArchitectRefused.builds()` defaults to empty.
  The message reads "the player's build build-12 (house, 41 blocks in the way: -120 64 33 minecraft:oak_log; ...; and 33 more)".
- **Consent:** trailing `@Nullable BuildConsent consent` on `PlaceRequest`, `RoadRequest`, `CellsRequest`, `DeltaRequest`,
  `RealiseRequest`, `BrushRequest` and `FitOptions` (old constructors: null). Batch items carry their request's.
- **Findings:** `RegionView` gains trailing `List<BuildHit> buildHits` (at most 8 builds); `cellsSkipped` gains `player_build`,
  `player_build.<id>`, `player_build.support` and `tree_kept.build`.
- **Events:** `SiteEvents.BUILD_CHANGED` (appended): a build found, changed (revision), merged, split, claimed, released or gone.
- **Features:** `playerPlaced` (tracking on), `builds` (classification and enforcement), `plan.feature.build` (the kit's).
  A world rule `architect.playerTracking` (default on); off: nothing is recorded, enforcement off, the data kept.

### 10. Builds in plans (`plan/0`, additive)

- `$defs/feature` gains `{build: {id?, kind?, pick?: largest|nearest, to?: anchor}}` (id or kind; `feature.pick`'s ties).
  Catalogue entry **`feature.build`** (supported, sinceApi PT). `near {feature: {build}}` works with it.
- `$defs/target` gains `{build: id}`, so `inside` and `adjacent {to: {build}}` work. R5 has no `target.*` family: a `{build}`
  target answers under `feature.build` (one idea, one block id, as R4c), so no new family.
- `$defs/endpoint` gains `{build: id, port?: door | door_<n>}`: a road ends on the door's apron. Catalogue **`endpoint.build`**.
- **Around a build** uses `locator.around`, reserved until FL: it answers unsupported `{block: locator.around}` until then.
  A district round a build waits for `program.districts` (D1).
- **Ids in plans are the persisted build ids.** The plan check reads the index for the claim; the plan artifact records each
  build it used with its revision. A build that changes after planning is still kept at realise (§7); its cells are skipped
  and reported, never a DRIFTED refusal.

### 11. Gate (slice tier, $0)

Headless steps place blocks through a **fake ServerPlayer's `useItemOn` / `useItem`** (never `setBlock`, which would skip the
recording hook). Driver `tools/gate6cpt.mjs`, evidence `artifacts/gate6c-pt/`. Timing and memory bars are recorded, not judged.

| # | Check | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Recording | 200 placements (blocks, a door, a bed, buckets, seeds, a hoe, a shovel, an axe): exactly the expected cells; 20 bone meal uses and a region realise of 50k cells record 0 |
| 2 | Clearing | 50 breaks, 4 TNT at a wall, water over 10 torches: the records equal the remaining blocks; grass spread on placed dirt and copper weathering keep theirs |
| 3 | Pistons | 12 tracked blocks pushed and pulled: destinations recorded, sources cleared; a save mid-move keeps them |
| 4 | Save and reload | the set's hash and the index equal after `/save` and a restart, and after chunk unload and reload |
| 5 | Builds | an all-log 9x7x9 cabin with a door: `HOUSE`; a cobble wall and a dirt wall 16x3x1: `WALL`; a 9x9 farm: `FARM`; 20 torches, a filled 5x5x2 hole and a levelled 7x7 dirt patch: 0 builds |
| 6 | Hysteresis and ids | a 40-cell build cut to 21 stays; cut to 19, incidental after the debounce; regrown to 30 stays incidental; the id survives +50 blocks, a merge (oldest wins) and a reload |
| 7 | Village | an S3 copy with the cabin and a cobble wall 2 cells from its lots: plan keeps out, realise loses **0** of their blocks (hash equal), findings recorded |
| 8 | Brush | raise, lower, smooth and melt strokes at and over the cabin, `NATURAL_ONLY` and `PLAYER_BLOCKS` without consent: **0** lost |
| 9 | Felling | the cabin's wall touching a tree: the flood stops at its logs (`tree_kept.build` at least 1), the cabin's hash unchanged, the rest felled |
| 10 | Undo exact | with consent, a stroke clears 40 of a build's cells and 20 incidental ones; one undo: blocks E-flat 0, and the tracked set, placers and build ids 0 mismatches |
| 11 | Named refusals | a building placed over the cabin: `PLAYER_BUILD` naming build id, kind, count and the first 8 positions with block ids, all equal to the world; a `partial` road names its skipped span's build |
| 12 | Incidental and removal | a realise over the 20 torches and the dirt patch writes them with no refusal and its undo restores them and their records; the chunk NBT keeps `architect_mc:placed` after a start without the mod |
| 13 | Claim, release, supports | a pre-PT log cabin claimed: a build, kept by a stroke; released: cleared by the next stroke; a torch on natural ground beside a lowered column stays |
| 14 | Plan features | `near {build kind house}`, `adjacent {to {build}}`, `endpoint {build, port door}`: supported answers, the road ends on the apron; `around`: unsupported `locator.around` |
| 15 | Cost (recorded) | bytes per tracked block and per section on disk and in heap; `setBlockState` added ns (median of 1M, tracked and untracked chunks); classification own CPU per tick max (budget 1 ms) |
| 16 | API, spend | api-compat clean against the archived jars; apitest through the public API; $0.00 |

**Tier:** slice: units, apijars and api-compat, the impact steps (`site/**`, `region/**`, `journal/**`, mixins), PT's own
items. **gate-verifier** re-runs items 7, 8 and 10 (undo, journal, removal) per the 2026-10-12 policy.

### 12. Performance

- **Hot path:** every block change pays one attachment lookup when the chunk has none, plus a scope check. Recording is O(1)
  plus a dirty mark; no per-tick work except the classifier.
- **Classifier:** debounced 5 s, sliced at 1 ms own CPU a tick, 65,536 cells per flood; dirty components queue by age.
- **Queries:** every enforcement check is O(1) per cell; box queries walk only touched sections.

### 13. Build order

1. Archive the apitest jar. 2. The attachment, recording and clearing hooks, pistons and falling blocks. 3. The journal `pt`
member and v3. 4. The classifier and the index. 5. Enforcement path by path behind the single predicate. 6. Claim and release,
commands. 7. plan/0 additions and the kit's keep-outs. 8. Fixtures and gate.

### Slice PT2 outline: adopting a build as a site (later, after PT)

Not small, so a separate slice: it needs a site with no blueprint behind it.
- `Sites.adopt(buildId, owner, BuildConsent)`: the build stays standing; its cells (and the air inside its outline) are
  captured as **version 1** of a new site under the settlement's owner, with a blueprint taken from the world (block entities
  included) and a frame (front, entrance) guessed from its main door. `BuildState` appends `ADOPTED`; the site id is new.
- **The adoption entry's before equals its after.** Undoing or removing the adoption only un-adopts (the site record goes, the
  build returns to `ACTIVE` with its records): it never removes the house.
- Then updates, `versionOf`, change requests, `revert` (to v1 works as on any site) and undo work as on any building; the
  cells Architect writes in later versions are its own, and the player's later blocks are tracked again (KEEP as today).
- Open for PT2: a build spanning unloaded chunks; a build with another owner's journal cells in it.

### Changes from Steward's review of PT (2026-10-13; these win)

- **S-PT-2:** a new `Reason.PLAYER_BUILD` (its meaning differs from PLAYER_BLOCKS).
- **S-PT-3:** per-request consent by build ids is enough for v0; Steward's change requests carry the asking player as actor.
- **S-PT-4:** builds are hard keep-outs in every plan by default, door clearance included, **except** a build named in the
  request's consent (an adopted build, "replace my shed").
- **S-PT-5:** `builds()` and `BUILD_CHANGED`, plus **`builds(box)`** (query by area) and the build's **placer UUID(s)** on
  its view.
- **S-PT-6 (PT2):** the adopted site carries the caller's `ext`; a player's later hand edits on an adopted build stay player
  edits (kept by updates as today).
- **Addition: PATH builds don't block roads.** A road may cross or join a `PATH` build without consent, provided it removes
  none of the path's cells (it may only write cells the path does not occupy, and may treat path cells as walk surface).
  Gate item: a road routed across a player's path joins it with 0 path cells changed.

### Coordinator decisions on PT's Noah questions (2026-10-13; from Noah's stated intent, he may override)

- **N-PT-1:** yes, incidental non-natural blocks (a torch, a few scattered blocks) count as natural.
- **N-PT-2:** yes, a grace period: a component of 24+ structural cells changed by a player within the last 10 minutes is a
  **provisional build** (kept like a build, shown as provisional) so a half-built house isn't cleared mid-build.
- **N-PT-3:** the drafted promote/demote numbers are accepted as defaults (world-rule tunable); revisit with play data.
- **N-PT-4:** no inferred scan by default (it would mark generated villages as builds). "Claim my build" is the tool; an
  op-only scan command may come later.
- **N-PT-5:** yes: a build's own placer (or an op) may consent to `PLAYER_BLOCKS` on that build. Noah's rule is "unless its
  owner asks", so B's op-only rule (N-B-1) stays for everyone else's blocks.
- **N-PT-6:** yes, `force` never overrides a build.
- **N-PT-7:** accepted: commands, WorldEdit and other mods' tools are not recorded; claim covers them.
- **N-PT-8:** the drafted non-op claim limits are accepted.
- **N-PT-9:** next free minor at merge.
- **Item 12 ruling (2026-10-13, after the measurement):** accept and document: a start without the mod that loads a chunk
  drops its records (Fabric API); item 12's no-mod half asserts that limit, a clean reload after the reinstall with the blocks
  untracked, and "claim my build" restoring protection. No side-file mirror.

| § | As built |
|---|---|
| §1 data | Fabric data attachment `architect_mc:placed` on `LevelChunk` (Fabric API 0.161: persistent, `CompoundTag.CODEC` mapped, not synced; `markUnsaved` on every change). `placed/PlacedChunk`: a placer palette (254 UUIDs, then UNKNOWN) and a build palette (index 0 = incidental) per chunk; sections sparse (`Short2ShortOpenHashMap`) up to 256 cells, dense (`long[64]` bitset + `short[4096]`) from 257, sparse again at 128 or fewer; a cell is `(placer << 8) \| build`. NBT `{v, placers, builds, sections[{y, p \| m, o?, b \| bu}]}`, palettes compacted on write. |
| §2 recording | Mixins on `ServerPlayerGameMode.useItemOn`/`useItem` open a **use scope** (placer, kind BLOCK/BUCKET/TOOL, click, face); `LevelChunk.setBlockState` calls `Placed.changed`, which records only what the scope's rule allows (`placed/PlacedRules`, pure: a block within 2 of the click from empty or replaceable, a stacked count or double slab; a bucket's source fluid within 2; a tool's block-to-block change within 1). Pistons (`PistonBaseBlock.moveBlocks`, `MovingPistonBlock.newMovingBlockEntity`, `PistonMovingBlockEntity` tick/finalTick/save/load) carry each record on the moving block entity (NBT `architect_mc:placed`), so a save mid-move keeps it; falling blocks (`FallingBlockEntity` fall/tick/save/read) likewise. Bone meal, growth, commands, dispensers and other mods record nothing (N-PT-7). Off the server thread a change only clears. |
| §3 clearing | A cell that becomes empty (air or a fluid) loses its record; a block-to-block change keeps it (grass spread, weathering, waxing). A use scope that changes a cell outside its rule leaves it as it was. Leaked scopes are reset at the end of each tick. |
| §4 builds | `placed/Builds`: per-section debounce (5 s), a flood of tracked cells within Chebyshev 2, structural vs natural by the **median surface of the untracked columns** within 3, then 6, then 12 (farmland, dirt paths, crops, stems and fluid sources always structural); promote 40 (24 with a non-natural block), demote below 20 after a 60 s second look (48 without a qualifier), provisional 24 (N-PT-2: grace 10 min, rescheduled at load and on a rule change). Merges keep the oldest id, a split keeps the id on the largest part; aliases resolve. Kinds HOUSE (enclosure plus a door), WALL, FARM, PATH, TOWER, BARN, OTHER. Index `<world>/architect/builds.json`, written by an async writer thread (waited on at save). Sliced at 1 ms own CPU per level per tick. Rules are world rules (`/architect build rule`). **Finding:** a 16x3x1 wall is WALL only while PROVISIONAL (48 cells, no qualifier: below the no-qualifier bar once the grace ends); item 5 runs with the grace, item 6 with `graceMs 0`. |
| §5 undo | `journal/Pt` on each journal cell (`Cell.pt`, `HandDown.wasPt/nowPt`, `Write.pt`), captured at `Txn.create` (entries are committed before their writes). File version **3 only for files that hold `pt`** (palettes `ptu`/`ptb`, section member `pt {k,u,b}`); every other file and every head stays version 2; a 0.25.0 reader refuses a v3 file. Hand-downs carry the record with the before; reactivate gives it back. Every Architect write goes through `Placed.set` or a writer scope (`beginWrites` for template placements and restores, the restore scope for `SiteJournal`, `RestoreJob`, `DeltaJob`): inside it a cell takes the record the undo's restore map names, else is cleared. `PredicatePathsTest` fails on a new raw `setBlock` outside its allowlist. |
| §6 placers | Records hold placer UUIDs; builds hold `placers` (UUID to count) and `primaryPlacer()`. No id is built from an owner or a name. |
| §7 enforcement | One predicate `Placed.build(level, chunk, x, y, z)`; a consent (build ids) is checked per request on the server thread and kept with batch items, regions and strokes. Sites: `checkSite` refuses `PLAYER_BUILD` (first 8 cells with ids, counts per build) and `force` never overrides it (N-PT-6); the terrain fit sees build cells as fixed; approaches stop short of them. Roads: a segment over a build is refused `PLAYER_BUILD` (a `partial` road skips it as a named span); a PATH build is walk surface, joined with 0 path cells changed. Cells, deltas, stockpiles: refused or skipped per the request's mode. Regions and brushes: `TileCheck` skips build cells (`player_build`, `player_build.<id>`, `player_build.support` for a lowered column's neighbour support), felling stops at build logs (`tree_kept.build`), the region plan's keep-outs are each kept build's bounds plus 1 and both door aprons (S-PT-4: a consented build is no keep-out). PLAYER_BLOCKS on a build: an op, or the build's own placer with consent (N-PT-5). Incidental cells count as natural (N-PT-1). |
| §1 limit (item 12) | The set lives in the chunk NBT only. A start **without the mod** that loads a chunk drops its records (Fabric API skips the unknown attachment and the chunk is saved again); a never-loaded chunk keeps them. After the reinstall those blocks are untracked (natural by class, the pre-tracking rule) and `/architect build claim` restores protection. Accepted by the coordinator (2026-10-13); no side-file mirror (it would go stale while the mod is absent). |
| §8 claim | `/architect build claim <from> <to>`, `release <id>`, `list`, `at <pos>`, `rule` (op); claim limits 32x32x32 and reach 64, 8 claims per player, ops 4096 columns; claims over 1M cells are sliced at 2 ms a tick. A claimed build is CLAIMED and never demoted; a released one is RELEASED and its cells incidental. **Finding:** a released or never-claimed log cabin is felled whole by a stroke at its base (C31's LOG rule: its walls are logs). |

## Phase 6c slice PT2: adopt a build as a site (FROZEN 2026-10-13 after Steward's review)

API: the next free minor at merge (house rule; placeholder `PT2` below), mod to match, `KIT_VERSION` next minor. Outlined at
the end of PT and shaped by Steward's S-PT-6: the adopted site carries the caller's `ext`, and a player's later hand edits on
an adopted build stay player edits, kept by updates as today. The PLAN "Keep open: zones" rule holds: records hold UUIDs and
the ids below, and no id is built from an owner string, so a later `transferOwner` moves nothing new here.

- **Branch:** `slice/PT2`, worktree `../architect-mc-PT2`. **Spend:** $0 (the `versionOf` step runs on the sim).
- **Scope:** `Sites.adopt`: a standing player build becomes a site with a library entry at version 1, **without writing a
  block**, so updates (5b), `versionOf` (C13), `revert`, undo and `outdated` work on a player's house.
- **Not in scope:** several builds in one site; adopting a box that is not a build (claim it first, PT §8); entities (item
  frames, paintings, armour stands, pets: not captured); placing an adopted entry elsewhere (refused, N-PT2-2); polish of an
  adopted entry; `transferOwner`; Hardcore's difference; the `.schem` export of an adopted site (SCH's `exportSiteSchematic`
  works on it unchanged).
- **Depends on:** PT (v0.27.0), 0b C13 `versionOf`, 5b deltas, Y (stockpile). No kit plan changes (`plan/0` untouched).

### 0. Facts (v0.27.0)

- A site is a library entry at a pinned version plus a journal `site` entry whose `after` is the cells it wrote; `checkDelta`
  and `applyDelta` compare the world with the site's top `after` (StillOurs, with the volatile list of Steward's S2) to find
  kept cells, and a revert undoes the suffix of delta entries (5b).
- `versionOf` needs a parametric source: polish's `bundled`, `no_source` and `massing` refusals are inherited (0b §5). An
  imported `.nbt` entry has none, so an adopted entry needs a **captured source** (§3).
- PT builds are index records plus per-cell placer and build ids in the chunk attachment. Architect's writes clear a cell's
  record; undo restores it exactly (PT §5). `Build` has no site link. `BuildState` is `ACTIVE, CLAIMED, RELEASED, PROVISIONAL`.
- Survival deltas are construction deltas: added and changed cells are queued and built from the owner's stockpile (Y); a
  removed or changed cell refunds only when it is paid and still ours; a revert in survival is a forward delta (5b).
- The template cap is 96x64x96. `Reason.FIELD_LIMIT` and `FieldLimits` bound `ext` (4096 characters as JSON, namespaced keys).

### 1. API (additive and binary compatible)

```java
// Sites; the default throws "needs Architect API PT2"
CompletableFuture<AdoptResult> adopt(String buildId, @Nullable String owner, BuildConsent consent, JsonObject ext);
Optional<String> adoptedSite(String buildId);                       // the site standing on a build, if any
record AdoptResult(String siteId, String entryId, int version /* 1 */, String buildId, BoundingBox box, int cells,
                   int airCells, int blockEntities, int skipped, Direction front, boolean frameGuessed) {}
// appended: BuildState.ADOPTED; Reason.ADOPT_REFUSED (detail below); SiteEvents.ADOPTED (siteId, buildId, entryId)
// Build gains trailing @Nullable String siteId (old constructor kept: null); SiteView gains no field (its ext carries the link)
```

- **Features:** `adopt`. A client without it sees the default throw. `adopt` needs no mode and no `INSTANT` permission: it writes
  nothing, so it cannot be a free build (§7).
- **Ids.** The alias of a merged build resolves to the survivor. The **site id** is new (the house counter, as any site); the
  **entry id** is `adopted-<8 hex of a random UUID>` (the library is per game folder, not per world, so no world counter);
  neither uses the owner, the build number or a player name. The entry name reads "Adopted <kind> <buildId>".
- **`ext`.** Validated like a lot list's (`FieldLimits.lotExt`): over 4096 characters or a key without `namespace:name` refuses
  `FIELD_LIMIT` with the path (`ext`). The site carries the caller's keys; the mod then sets `architect_mc:adopted =
  {build, entry, at}` last, and it wins. The entry's own `ext` stays `Library.setExt`'s: the caller's keys are not copied there.
  Survives save, reload, `versionOf`, undo and redo as the lot ext does (C19).
- **Owner.** Free string on the site, nullable as in `place`; stockpile and `outdated(owner)` key on it as for any site.

### 2. What adoption does (one atomic step, no world writes)

1. **Check** (server thread, loaded chunks only), in this order, first refusal wins (§5): the build and its state, the consent,
   the chunks, the cells' owners, the size, `ext`.
2. **Capture** the build's cells (§3). Up to 50,000 cells in one tick; above that sliced with change tracking (4e's capture): a
   cell that changes before the commit is re-read, and a capture that cannot settle in 3 passes fails `SITE_BUSY` (temporary).
3. **Create** the library entry (version 1: structure `.nbt`, blueprint JSON with `frame`, captured source, `ext`) and the
   site (state BUILT, `kind` building, rotation NONE, `box` = the cells' bounds, no approach, no crate, every cell **unpaid**).
4. **Journal** one entry `kind: "adopt"`, `site: S`, BOX policy, cells = the captured cells with **`before` == `after`** (the
   world as captured), `meta {build, priorState, entry}`. No `pt` member: nothing is written, so no record changes.
5. **Mark** the build `ADOPTED` with `siteId`; revision +1; `BUILD_CHANGED` and `SiteEvents.ADOPTED` fire.

If any step fails, nothing remains: the entry is trashed, no site, no journal entry, the build unchanged.

### 3. The capture: what becomes version 1

- **Cells.** Every tracked cell of the build (all its structural cells and the incidental ones inside it), plus **column fill**:
  for each footprint column, the air cells between the column's lowest and highest build cell (rooms under roofs, stairwells).
  Natural cells, fluids, other players' incidental blocks and open courtyard columns (no build cell) are `structure_void`: not
  the site's, never written, never refunded. This is the PT footprint, not a bounding box.
- **Block entities** keep their id and non-inventory NBT (sign text, banner patterns, bed colour). Inventories (`Items`,
  `Item`, `RecordItem`, a lectern's book) are **dropped from the blueprint** so a copy can never duplicate items; the world's
  chest keeps its items. A delta that would write a container cell refuses `BLOCK_ENTITIES` as today (5b).
- **Frame.** `front` = the facing of the **main entrance**: of the build's `entrances`, the one lowest in the build and nearest
  its footprint edge (ties by position). The entrance feet row is that door's lower half. With no entrance the front is the
  longest footprint side facing the open side, `frameGuessed: true` (SQ-PT2-1: refuse instead?).
- **Captured source.** The kit gets `kit/lib/adopt.mjs`: the structure as a generated blueprint of run-length boxes per layer,
  one part `adopted` (v0; SQ-PT2-3), with `front`/`frame` set. It reads as a normal `.mjs` blueprint, so `versionOf`'s
  designer, renders and the frame guard work unchanged; `source: "captured"` lifts `no_source` for these entries only.
- **Limits.** Bounds at most 96x64x96 (`TOO_LARGE`) and at most 262,144 captured cells (`TOO_LARGE`, N-PT2-5). A PT build is
  bounded at 65,536 structural cells, so the second cap bites only on huge column fills.
- **Skipped** cells (void by the rules above) are counted in `AdoptResult.skipped`.

### 4. The build stays a PT build: `ADOPTED`

**Decision: the build stays in the PT index, state `ADOPTED`, linked to its site, and keeps the `PLAYER_BUILD` protection.**

- **Why.** (1) The cells are still the player's: their records, placers and the build id are what Steward shows ("Alex's
  house"), and hand edits after adoption must keep being recorded and kept (S-PT-6) by the same hook. (2) Every write path
  already asks the one predicate `Placed.build`; leaving the build in place means roads, strokes, felling, region plans, fits
  and approaches keep the house without a new rule, where a plain site would protect it only where a path honours journal
  ownership. (3) S-PT-4 already says a build named in the request's consent is the one exception, so "replace my shed" works
  on an adopted build with no new concept. (4) Un-adopting is a state change, nothing is rebuilt.
- **Never demotes** (as CLAIMED). **Merges:** an `ADOPTED` build is the survivor of a merge with an `ACTIVE` or `PROVISIONAL`
  one (and keeps its id); two `ADOPTED` builds, or `ADOPTED` and `CLAIMED`, are **not** merged (cells within 2 stay assigned to
  their own build). **Split:** the largest part keeps the id, `ADOPTED` and `siteId`; the others are new `ACTIVE` builds.
- **Growth.** Blocks the player adds beside the house within 2 of its cells join the build (same id). They are outside the
  site's cells: PT protects them, the site does not own them.
- **Release** of an `ADOPTED` build refuses `ADOPT_REFUSED` (`adopted`); remove or undo the site first.
- **The site's own operations are implicitly consented** for cells **inside its own cell set**: `applyDelta`, `revert`,
  `checkDelta` and `remove` on site S need no `BuildConsent` to touch S's cells, `OVERWRITE` of a player edit included (the
  caller already chose it). **Growth cells outside S's cells** that hold tracked cells of the adopted build refuse
  `PLAYER_BUILD` as any build's, unless the request's consent names the build. Every other caller still needs consent.
- **Records under Architect's writes.** A delta's written cell loses its record (PT §3) and is the site's; the build's tracked
  count falls. Undo and revert give the records back exactly (PT §5). A cell the player later edits is recorded again and is
  the player's, inside the build.

### 5. Refusals

`Reason.ADOPT_REFUSED` (appended), `ArchitectRefused.detail()`; reused reasons keep their meaning.

| Condition | Refusal |
|---|---|
| unknown id, or a `RELEASED` build | `ADOPT_REFUSED` `not_a_build` (the message says "claim it first" for a box) |
| `PROVISIONAL` | `ADOPT_REFUSED` `provisional` (SQ-PT2-4: a half-built house is a moving target; wait for the promotion, or `claim` it, which makes it CLAIMED) |
| consent null, not naming the build, `actor` null, or the actor neither a placer (10% of its cells) nor permission 2 | `ADOPT_REFUSED` `consent` (names what is missing) |
| `ADOPTED` already | `ADOPT_REFUSED` `already_adopted`, message "adopted as site-N": a caller that lost the response recovers from it or `adoptedSite` |
| a chunk of the build unloaded | `NOT_LOADED` naming the chunks |
| a tracked cell of the build is owned by a journal entry (a site, region or road) | `OVERLAP` listing the sites and counts; an owned **air or fill** cell is void, not a refusal |
| bounds or cell cap | `TOO_LARGE` (the dimensions and count) |
| `ext` out of limits | `FIELD_LIMIT` |
| journal unreadable, world stopping | `JOURNAL_UNAVAILABLE`, `WORLD_STOPPED` |
| the placement toggle (`architect.playerTracking`) off | `ADOPT_REFUSED` `tracking_off` |

Also: **`place`/`check` of an adopted entry anywhere** refuses `ADOPT_REFUSED` `placed_elsewhere` (N-PT2-2); `polish` of an
adopted entry refuses `VERSION_REFUSED` `adopted_polish` (`versionOf` works, §3). A stand-alone `remove` of the entry's
library file while the site stands is the existing pinned-version refusal.

### 6. What works afterwards

- **Updates (delta).** `checkDelta`/`applyDelta` from v1 to a later version, per 5b: growth cells meet the world under the
  usual refusals (`OVERLAP`, `PLAYER_BUILD` as §4), `FRAME_CHANGED` if `front` or the entrance row moves.
- **`versionOf`** (C13): `DesignRequest.versionOf(entryId, siteId)` on the adopted entry installs v2 (`by: design`). Its
  context has the head's captured source and renders, `site-now.nbt` (the restore box as it stands) and `site-edits.json`
  (the KEEP set), so "add a floor" is told which cells the player has changed. The sim changes the head as it does for C13.
- **`outdated(owner)`** lists the site once v2 exists (`version` 1, `headVersion` 2); `ENTRY_VERSIONED` fires.
- **`revert(siteId, 1, actor)`** returns to v1 as 5b's revert: creative by journal undo of the delta suffix, survival as a
  forward construction delta. Reverting to v1 is a normal revert; there is no v0.
- **Undo, and `remove`, of the adoption un-adopt only.** The journal `adopt` entry has `before == after`, so undoing it writes
  nothing: the site record goes, the build returns to its `priorState` (`ACTIVE` or `CLAIMED`) with `siteId` null and its
  records untouched, `BUILD_CHANGED` and `SITE_REMOVED` fire, **the house stays**. `remove(siteId)` on an updated site first
  undoes its delta group (5b: back to the adopted state), then un-adopts. The entry goes to the library trash when it has one
  version; it **stays** when it has two or more (a paid design history, SQ-PT2-5). The slice never removes the house.
- **Redo.** `adopt` again after an un-adopt makes a new site and, if the old entry stayed, a new entry (no reuse in v0).

### 7. Player hand edits after adoption

- Edits are ordinary player edits: recorded by PT (the cell is the player's, in the build), and **kept** by `applyDelta` and
  `revert` under 5b's rules: a Δ cell whose world value is not the site's top `after` is `KEEP` (not written, in
  `kept {pos, found, planned}`, counted in `deviations`), `OVERWRITE` writes it (the entry's `before` records the player's
  block), `REFUSE` refuses `PLAYER_EDITS`. Cells outside Δ are never written. Opening a door, copper weathering and other
  volatile changes are not edits (S2's list).
- **A block the player puts into a cell the delta wants** stays until they remove it or `OVERWRITE` runs; the next delta
  compares plan against plan, as 5b's "later deltas" rule says.
- **Survival:** a mined adopted block is a player edit: kept, not refunded (phase 3's no-dupe rule).

### 8. Survival: adoption is free

- Adopting needs no items, no crate, no stockpile, no `INSTANT` permission. No block is written, so there is nothing to refund.
  Every adopted cell is **unpaid** (the `free` bitset is full): a later delta that removes or swaps an adopted block gives **no
  refund** (N-PT2-1: the safe default), and a `remove` of the site refunds nothing for them, so adopt then remove gains and
  loses 0 items (gate item 6).
- **Later changes construct from the stockpile** (Y): `applyDelta` of an update is a construction delta; the owner's
  stockpile feeds the added and changed cells (credit key `delta:<entry>:<site>`); cells it adds are paid and refund on
  revert and remove as 5b says. An owner with no stockpile gets a delta crate as today.
- The identity "items in = items out" holds across adopt, update, revert and un-adopt (checked by the gate's ledger).

### 9. Saved state and compatibility

- The site record is the ordinary one plus `ext["architect_mc:adopted"]`; the journal entry kind `adopt` is a free string
  (`kind` is a free string, 5b's kind-compatibility note). Whether a 0.27.0 reader keeps or refuses an `adopt` entry is
  unmeasured: the gate (item 13) records it, and if it would drop the entry the file version is bumped as 4e's downgrade rule
  requires, only for files that hold one.
- `builds.json` gains `siteId` and the `ADOPTED` state; an older reader drops the unknown state to `ACTIVE` and the site link,
  which the plan accepts: the house is still a build there (SQ-PT2-6).
- The library entry's blueprint JSON gains `source: "captured"` and `adopted {build, at}`; an older mod shows it as a plain
  imported entry (no `versionOf`).

### 10. Gate (slice tier, $0)

Headless steps place every block through a **fake ServerPlayer's `useItemOn`** (never `setBlock`), as PT. Driver
`tools/gate6cpt2.mjs`, evidence `artifacts/gate6c-pt2/`. The cabin is PT's 9x7x9 log cabin with a door, a chest (with items), a
bed and a sign, built by the fake player, `HOUSE`.

| # | Check | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Refusals | each §5 row: unknown, released, provisional, no consent, a stranger actor, an op actor (passes), already adopted (the message names the site), an unloaded chunk, an owned tracked cell, 97 wide, 300k column fill, a bad `ext`, tracking off; every one leaves the world, the index and the library unchanged |
| 2 | Adopt | the cabin is adopted: `AdoptResult` (version 1, frame from the door), world hash **equal** before and after, 0 blocks written (the change counter), `BuildState.ADOPTED` and `siteId`, the tracked set and each record **unchanged**, `ext` carries the caller's keys and `architect_mc:adopted` |
| 3 | Capture | the entry's structure equals the world's footprint cells (and the column-filled air), the chest's `Items` are absent from the entry while the world's chest keeps them, the chest cell is a block entity; `skipped` counts the void |
| 4 | A floor | `versionOf` (sim) "add a floor" installs v2 (`by: design`), `outdated` lists the site 1 -> 2, `checkDelta` reports the growth, 0 kept; the frame guard passes |
| 5 | Hand edits kept | the player breaks a wall block, places a block in a cell the delta changes and another outside it; `checkDelta`/`applyDelta` (KEEP): the changed-cell edit is kept and reported (`found`, `planned`), the outside edit is untouched, `deviations` counts the kept cell; the floor is built; the edits stay the player's (records), the build's placers are unchanged |
| 6 | Survival | a survival world, the same flow with a stockpile: adopt costs 0 and writes 0; the update builds from the stockpile; the ledger, the crate and the player's inventory balance (items in = out) across adopt, update, revert and un-adopt; no refund for an adopted block |
| 7 | Revert to v1 | `revert(site, 1)`: the floor is gone, the hand edits outside Δ stand, the cabin's hash equals the adopted state plus the edits; `history` shows it |
| 8 | Undo of the adoption | **run A** (adopt, undo): the cabin's hash equals the pre-adoption hash, the tracked set, placers and build ids **0 mismatches**, the build `ACTIVE` with `siteId` null, the entry trashed. **Run B** (items 4-7 first, then `remove`): the deltas go, the cabin stands with the hand edits, its hash equals the hash taken just before the removal, the PT records equal the ones then (0 mismatches), the entry stays (two versions) |
| 9 | Save and reload | after `/save` and a restart (and a chunk unload and reload): the site, its version and `ext`, the entry, the `ADOPTED` state and `siteId`, the records, `kept` cells and `outdated` are identical; `applyDelta` and `revert` still work; undo after the reload still only un-adopts |
| 10 | Protection stays | with the cabin adopted: a stroke, a road across it, felling at its wall and a region plan keep it (`PLAYER_BUILD`), a consent naming the build lets a `PLAYER_BLOCKS` stroke clear it; growth cells over the player's lean-to refuse `PLAYER_BUILD` unless consent names the build |
| 11 | Build states | adopted builds do not demote under 20 cells; a merge with an `ACTIVE` build keeps the id; two adopted builds do not merge; a split keeps the id on the largest part; `releaseBuild` refuses |
| 12 | Elsewhere | `place` of the adopted entry refuses `placed_elsewhere`; `polish` refuses; the entry's library delete while the site stands refuses |
| 13 | API, spend | api-compat clean against the archived 0.27.0 jars, apitest through the public API, an old reader opens a world without `adopt` entries, and what a 0.27.0 jar does with one that has them is recorded; $0.00 |

**Tier:** slice: units, apijars and api-compat, the impact steps (`site/**`, `delta/**`, `journal/**`, `placed/**`,
`library/**`), PT2's own items. **gate-verifier** re-runs items 5, 6, 7 and 8 (undo, journal, removal, accounting) per the
2026-10-12 policy.

### 11. Build order

1. Archive the 0.27.0 apitest jar. 2. `Build.siteId`, `BuildState.ADOPTED`, the classifier rules (§4). 3. The capture and
`kit/lib/adopt.mjs`. 4. The `adopt` journal entry, the site and entry creation, un-adopt on undo and remove. 5. The implicit
consent in `applyDelta`/`revert`/`checkDelta`. 6. Refusals and `placed_elsewhere`. 7. `versionOf` for captured sources. 8. Fixtures
and gate.

### Open questions for Steward

- **SQ-PT2-1.** A build with no entrance (a wall, a farm, an open barn): adopt with a guessed `front` (`frameGuessed`, the
  draft), or refuse `no_entrance`? A wrong frame only matters to the frame guard and an approach.
- **SQ-PT2-2.** Do you need `adopt` to take a name for the entry, or a box beyond the build (a garden, a fence), or is
  "claim first, then adopt" enough?
- **SQ-PT2-3.** The captured blueprint has one part. Do your change requests need parts (walls, roof) for the scoped
  `versionOf` ("local edits within 3 existing plus 2 new parts")? One part makes any edit a whole-house edit for the scoping call.
- **SQ-PT2-4.** `PROVISIONAL` refused (the draft), or allowed once its cells have not changed for some minutes?
- **SQ-PT2-5.** Un-adopt keeps the entry when it has two or more versions: right, or always trash it?
- **SQ-PT2-6.** The `ADOPTED` build stays a keep-out in your plans (the draft). Do you also want `builds()` to flag
  `siteId` so the settlement view shows "Alex's house (site-14)"? (It does in this draft.)
- **SQ-PT2-7.** A site's own cells are implicitly consented; growth over the player's extension needs your consent. Right?

### Open questions for Noah

- **N-PT2-1.** In survival, demolishing a player's adopted block through an update gives **no refund** (the block was never
  paid to Architect, and an item back would risk a dupe on revert). Or refund the item to the crate and charge it back on revert?
- **N-PT2-2.** An adopted entry cannot be placed anywhere else (it would copy a player's house as a design). Allow it as a
  copy for the owner or an op?
- **N-PT2-3.** Containers' contents are never captured, and a chest in a cell an update changes refuses `BLOCK_ENTITIES`.
  Fine, or may an update move a chest's items?
- **N-PT2-4.** A player may adopt only a build they placed (10% of its cells) or an op may adopt any. Same rule as consent (PT §6).
- **N-PT2-5.** The caps: 96x64x96 and 262,144 captured cells.
- **N-PT2-6.** Entities (item frames, paintings, armour stands) are not captured; a wall change may pop a painting as an item (vanilla).
- **N-PT2-7.** API version: the next free minor at merge (the house rule).

(`artifacts/gate6c-pt2/spend.json`). Ports 8924-8929. Evidence: `artifacts/gate6c-pt2/` (one JSON per `tools/gate6cpt2.mjs` step,
REPORT.md, api-compat.txt, old027.txt; `v0270/` the 0.27.0 tag build with its `tools/`), the runs under `artifacts/gate-runs-PT2/`
(and `gate-runs-PT2b/` for a parallel survival run). The version numbers are the coordinator's placeholders.

**The draft's unverified assumptions, checked against the Java:**
- **A 0.27.0 reader and an `adopt` entry:** it would keep it (the index's kind is a free string) but misread it: `SiteJournal.main()`
  takes it as the site's main entry, `Sites.reconcile` would rebuild a lost record of a non-`site` main entry as an Infra, and a 0.27.0
  remove runs the BOX undo, writing every `before` over the player's later edits and clearing their PT records. So the entry's files
  (region and head) are **journal file version 4** (`JournalNbt.VERSION_ADOPT`), which 0.27.0's `known()` (1-3) refuses (4e's
  downgrade rule, as PT's v3); every other file and the index are unchanged. Measured (item 13): 0.27.0's own `JournalNbt` and
  `JournalStore` refuse each adopt file, read every other file, and keep the adopt row of the index.
- **The 3-pass capture:** built (`Adopt.Job`: 50,000 cells a tick under a `ChangeTracker`, the changed cells re-read; a re-read that
  fits a tick commits in that tick, else another pass; past 3, SITE_BUSY). Unit-tested (`AdoptTest.settleRule`); no gate fixture is
  that large.
- **The `free` bitset:** not needed. An adopted site has no construction record, `Builder.paidCells` of such a site is empty, and a
  survival delta's queue holds only its own cells, so adopted cells are never paid (item 6: no refund for an adopted block).
- **before == after:** harmless on disk, wrong on undo (a BOX undo writes its befores). The adopt entry is **never undone**: a remove
  undoes the site's other entries (deltas, their crates, held leaves) as any site's, then **releases** the adopt entry. Its cells hold
  block states only (no block-entity data: inventories stay the world's), no `pt`.

| §1 API | `Sites.adopt(buildId, owner, consent, ext)` (a `CompletableFuture<AdoptResult>`) and `Sites.adoptedSite(buildId)`: defaults that throw "needs Architect API 1.28.0". `AdoptResult` as drafted. `BuildState.ADOPTED`, `Reason.ADOPT_REFUSED` appended; `SiteEvents.ADOPTED (siteId, buildId, entryId)`; `Build` gains trailing `siteId` (the 11-argument constructor kept; equals/hashCode include it). Feature `adopt`. |
| §2 adoption | `site/Adopt.java`. Checks in order: the world and the journal, tracking, the build and its state, the consent (names it, an actor, the actor a placer of 10% or an op: `BuildViews.consent`), the chunks, the owners, the size, `ext` (`FieldLimits.adoptExt`, the lot ext rule). Then the capture, the entry (written to a temp folder, renamed, the library reloaded), the record, one journal commit, the build marked. A failure after the entry is written trashes it. |
| §3 capture | Per footprint column of the build, its tracked cells, the incidental tracked cells of its placers, and the air between the column's lowest and highest build cell; everything else in those spans is void (`skipped`). Block entities keep their data without `Items`, `Item`, `RecordItem`, `Book` and the position. The front: of the build's entrances the lowest, then the nearest the footprint edge; its side is the one whose neighbour column is outside the footprint (a door's own facing follows the placer's look, so it is not used); none: the longer axis's more open side, `frameGuessed`. `groundY` = the door's lower half (0 when guessed). Implicit consent: `SiteDeltas.buildRefusal` lets an adopted site write a build cell its own journal holds on top (`SiteJournal.isOwnedBy`); growth cells still need consent (item 10). |
| §5 refusals | As drafted. `place`/`check` of an adopted entry: ADOPT_REFUSED with the message starting `placed_elsewhere:` (`Refusal` has no detail field). `polish`: VERSION_REFUSED `adopted_polish` (the sidecar, before the login check). `Library.delete` of an adopted entry whose site stands returns false (the client's Library and the headless bridge too): no such pinned-version refusal existed for a library delete, so it is added for adopted entries only. |
| §6 afterwards | `SiteCells`, `beforeMap` and `reconcile` take the adopt entry as the site's base. Remove (and undo): no other entries: the record and the adopt entry released at once (`Sites.forget`), nothing written; with deltas: the API's and the removal's blockers and the player-in-box check cover only the deltas' cells, the deltas undone (survival: refunds over the deltas' cells only, and a paid block the undo writes back unchanged is not refunded), then the adopt entry released. Then the build returns to its prior state and a one-version entry goes to the library trash (two or more: kept). `adopted` is carried to every version by the sidecar's versionOf install. The versionOf context's KEEP list compares an adopted site's cells as still ours (its journal holds block states only). Start-time repair: an ADOPTED build whose site is gone is un-adopted; a site whose build is not linked is linked again. |
| §8 survival | Adopting writes and costs nothing; deltas are construction deltas fed by the stockpile. **Finding:** an un-adopt hands the paid blocks its undo leaves standing to the player with the house (the survival revert's rebuilt hatch log: neither refunded nor taken away); the gate's ledger counts them as handed over. |
| §9 saved state | `builds.json`: an adopted build is written with the state it had before (ACTIVE or CLAIMED) plus `adopted {site, prior}`: 0.27.0's `BuildState.valueOf` would throw on ADOPTED and drop the rest of the index; this reader reads it back ADOPTED (`BuildsAdoptTest`). |

The checker treats a captured source as an import (the design rules are warnings), allows groundY 0 (the floor row is the ground under it) and checks it with its own empty profile. Column fill is per column, as drafted: a floorless cabin's room under a flat roof is not captured (each interior column's lowest build cell is the roof), so a stroke may still raise terrain into that open air (as for any build). A consented PLAYER_BLOCKS stroke does not clear the site's own cells while the build is adopted (a region never writes a site's cells, 6a); once un-adopted it clears the build (item 10). ### C34 as built (Steward's patch ask; mod 0.29.1, API unchanged at 1.26.0; recorded 2026-10-13)

| Part | As built |
|---|---|
| The report | A hollow plank hut made with `/fill` and `/setblock` (an oak door in its south wall) and claimed with `Sites.claimBuild` came back kind `OTHER` with no entrances. Steward suspected the claim path or a door in the floor row. |
| Root cause | The door in the floor row, cut by the box. Steward's "claim my build" claims from the player's feet up (`Actions.build_claim`: `y .. y + min(31, 2r)`), and a player stands on the floor, so a door whose lower half is in the floor row has only its **upper** half inside the box. `ClaimJob` marked the upper half; `Builds.Comp.stats` counts a door's **lower** half as the entrance (`entranceBlock`), so the build had an enclosure, no entrance and no bed, which `Builds.kind` tells `OTHER`. Not the kind rules and not detection: the same hut with its door a row higher, a smaller hut, a margin claim, a console claim and the hut placed by use all gave HOUSE with one entrance. |
| Fix | `PlacedRules.partner(state, pos)` names the other half of a door (lower or upper) or a bed (head or foot). `ClaimJob.step` takes that partner too when it falls outside the box and holds the same block, with the claim's usual rules (another placer's cell and a journal-owned cell are never taken). The claim then holds both halves and the entrance is found. Claims inside the box, placement by use and the classifier are unchanged. `Build.cells` of such a claim is one higher. |
| Gate | `tools/gate6cpt.mjs` step `claimhut` (inside `pt-ingame`; `GATE6CPT_STEPS=claimhut` runs it alone): 11 huts made with commands (door above and in the floor row, 5x4x5 and 5x3x5, a claim with 2 around and 2 under, the floor in the ground, the console, and **Steward's feet-up box** in three forms) each claimed: HOUSE, CLAIMED, one entrance, still HOUSE after the classifier ran; the same hut placed by use is HOUSE with one entrance. Failed before the fix (feet-up box, door in the floor row: OTHER, 0 entrances, twice), passes after. Unit `ClaimPartnerTest` (the partner of each half of a door and a bed, none for other blocks, `Builds.kind` HOUSE with an entrance and an enclosure, OTHER without). |
| Left as is | A claim box that cuts a door's lower half is the only case fixed; a claim that holds only a build's roof or one wall still classifies by what it holds. A two-block build the box cuts elsewhere (a bed's partner in an unloaded chunk) is skipped. |

### C34b as built (Steward: "C34 still reproduces"; mod 0.29.2, API unchanged at 1.26.0; recorded 2026-10-13)

| Part | As built |
|---|---|
| The report | After 0.29.1, Steward's free e2e (`steward-mc tools/e2e.mjs` `playerBuilds`) still got CLAIMED, 170 cells, `OTHER`, no entrances for its command-built hut, and its box starts in the floor row, so 0.29.1's cut-door diagnosis did not fit. |
| Root cause | **The hut stands in the air, and §4's entrance rule judged its door against the natural ground.** The fixture takes `y` from the player's `Pos` after `/tp @p x 100 z` and `/tp @p x ~ z`; earlier steps switch spectator -> creative, which keeps flight on, so the player hovers at 100 and the hut is built at y 100..104 over flat ground (Steward's own `builds.json`: build-1..build-11 all have bounds y 100). `Builds.Comp.stats` took a door as an entrance only when its lower half was within 2 of the median ground surface round it (`y <= g + 2`), so a door ~160 above the ground was no entrance; with an enclosure, no entrance and no bed, `Builds.kind` says `OTHER`. The adopt then guessed the front (`frameGuessed`). |
| Ruled out (with evidence) | **Classification after the claim returns:** no. `BuildViews.claim` marks boxes up to 1,000,000 cells in the call and `finishClaim` runs `stats`, the enclosure and `kind` before it returns; the gate reads the claim's return, `Sites.builds` at once (no drain) and again after the 5 s debounce: the same kind every time (OTHER/0 before the fix, HOUSE/1 after). Only a box over 1M cells is marked over ticks: its returned view has no cells yet, and `BUILD_CHANGED` "claimed" fires when marking ends (unchanged, as built in PT). **The door breaking under the separate `/setblock`s:** no. `BlockInput.place` keeps the given state when the neighbour-shape update would make it air, and the upper half's placement completes the pair; both halves stand (`/execute if block` on both cells, each case), and 170 = the full 7x7x5 shell with both door cells non-empty (a broken door would leave 168). **Facing, air outside or inside the door:** not part of the rule. **Claimed vs tracked cells:** both go through the same `Comp.stats` and `kind`. **Why 0.29.1's gate passed:** its huts all stood on the ground; Steward's order (lower first) on the ground gives HOUSE on 0.29.1 too. |
| Fix | `Builds.entranceAt(y, g, minY)`: a door, gate or trapdoor is at its ground when within 2 of the median ground surface (as before), **or**, for a build lifted off the ground (its lowest cell more than 2 above that surface), within 2 of the build's own lowest row. Read §4's "at its ground" for a lifted build as its own base. Builds on the ground are judged exactly as before (no upper-storey door becomes an entrance, no apron moves). One rule for claimed and tracked builds. |
| Side effects | A lifted build that is tracked (not claimed) may now promote through `qualifier()` (an entrance). Its entrance's apron, and a road endpoint to it, is in the air. Anything hanging below a lifted floor (a lantern, a ladder) lowers its lowest row and can put the door out of reach again. Claimed builds already in the index keep their kind until a change in them reclassifies them (a release and re-claim does it at once). |
| Gate | `tools/gate6cpt.mjs` step `claimhut` (inside `pt-ingame`) adds Steward's exact repro: `/fill ... hollow`, the door's lower half `/setblock` first, then the upper, both halves checked with `/execute if block`, the box (x0-1, y, z0-1)..(x0+7, y+8, z0+7), the claim's return read at once, `Sites.builds` at once and after 6 s; on the ground, at y 100 (Steward's height) and 40 above the ground: each CLAIMED, 170 cells, HOUSE with one entrance at every read. **On v0.29.1** (`artifacts/gate-runs-c34b/20261013-224436-slice`, head caa9b399, `GATE6CPT_STEPS=claimhut`): on the ground HOUSE/1, both lifted cases OTHER/0 at every read with both door halves standing: Steward's result exactly. **After the fix** (`artifacts/gate-runs-c34b/20261013-224654-slice`, head 518003b0, ports 8932/8933): unit-mod 665/0, pt-unit 4/0, pt-ingame 103/0 plus item 15's recorded bar (classifier max 1.08 ms, not judged): all three C34b huts HOUSE/1 at every read, the 11 C34 huts and the hut placed by use unchanged. Unit `EntranceGroundTest`. |
| For Steward | If the fixture meant a hut on the ground, its `y` needs the ground (e.g. `/gamemode survival` before the tp, or a heightmap read); that is Steward's to change. With 0.29.2 its lifted hut is HOUSE with one entrance either way. |

### C35 as built (Steward: versionOf of an adopted hut with a bible; mod 0.29.3, API unchanged at 1.26.0; recorded 2026-10-13)

Branch `fix/c35-captured-palette` (worktree `../architect-mc-c35`). $0: sim only.

| Part | As built |
|---|---|
| The report | Steward's stub e2e on 0.29.2: an "add a floor" `versionOf` of an adopted hut, sent with the settlement's bible (`withBible`), failed in the sim: `design adopted_d04f0165 threw: Error: kit/designs/adopted_d04f0165.mjs ignores the palette it is given (pass ... to the Blueprint) at loadDesign (kit/build.mjs:81)`. Without a bible it passes (Steward's re-run: capturedChanged 1 of 245). |
| Root cause | `kit/lib/adopt.mjs` `adopted()` builds its Blueprint with no palette, and the source the mod generates (`Adopt.source()`: `build({ floors = 0 })`) never takes or forwards one. With a bible on the request the sidecar runs the kit with `--bible bible/bible.json` (plus `--restraint`), `loadDesign` resolves a palette and passes it, and its guard (`bp.p !== p`, meant for a design that forgets its palette) throws. |
| Why PT2's gate missed it | Every PT2 `versionOf` (the kit test, the sidecar test, the in-game `flow` step's `addFloor`) ran without a bible, so `loadDesign` got no palette and the guard never ran. |
| Behaviour (Noah: "the player's house as built is theirs") | A captured source **opts out** of the palette: `adopted()` sets `bp.captured` (as PT2 did, for `sourceKind`), and `loadDesign` treats it as declared-exempt instead of throwing. A palette or bible supplied is ignored, never an error, and recorded three ways: `paletteIgnored` in the build's sidecar JSON (`{ bible: { id, version } }`, `{ preset }` or the inputs), so the installed version carries it; a check warning `palette ignored: <id> is a captured source ...`; and, first in the versionOf design's step (cut at 120 characters), `bible <id> v<n> ignored (captured: the player's blocks kept)` (`paletteIgnoredNote`, sidecar `installVersionOf`, both backends). A captured build records no `palette` or `bible` of its own, so an adopted version never reads as bible-driven. Any other design that drops its palette still throws. |
| New cells (Steward's decision, 2026-10-13) | Captured cells keep their blocks. An added storey takes its materials from the captured mix by role (`storeyMaterials`): **wall** `cap.wall` (the mod's most used non-air state), **frame** (the storey ring's corners) the most used full block in the footprint's corner columns below the top layer, **roof** the most used full block of the top captured layer; each falls back to the wall; ties go to the capture palette's lower index. The floor is the old top layer, which stays. Before C35 every storey cell was `cap.wall`. |
| Limits | A bible is never used for new cells in v0, even when the change asks for other materials: the generated source does not forward a palette, and changing `Adopt.source()` would not reach entries already adopted. The sim never asks; a Claude designer can still write other materials into the source by hand (the exemption no longer throws). Roles are wall, frame and roof only (no trim or accent role from the mix). A v2 built by 0.29.0-0.29.2 has storey frame and roof of `cap.wall`; a later versionOf rebuilt from its source under 0.29.3 gives those storey cells the derived materials (v1's captured cells are unaffected, so `capturedChanged` is too). `KIT_VERSION` unchanged (a patch). |
