## Phase 6c slice CU: copper weathering and undo (FROZEN 2026-10-20, Steward reviewed)

Weathered, waxed and scraped copper stays ours. Undo, site removal, deltas, the survival build's "still built" test and the
refund all treat a copper block at any stage of its own chain as the block we wrote. PLAN "Queued (coordinator, 2026-10-19):
Copper weathering and undo"; VOC §10 ("Queued, not built here"). Over HY (and KC, which shares no file with it).

- **Branch:** `slice/CU`, worktree `../architect-mc-CU`. **Spend:** $0.
- **Scope:** the copper equivalence in `StillOurs` (§2); every block-only "still ours" test (§3); the refund (§4); which other
  drift kinds count as ours (§5); the gate (§8).
- **Not in scope:** changing the E-normal classifier (no new world class); leaf decay, sapling growth, snow and ice (§5, kept as
  today); `palette()` over generated families (VOC §10's second item).
- **Touches removal and survival accounting:** the verifier re-runs undo and accounting, and **Steward's pre-release check**
  comes before release (GATES policies 3 and 4).

### 0. Facts (main 0d665136; HY changes none of these files except RegionFluids, which only calls `WorldJournal.holds`)

**"Still ours"** is `journal/StillOurs.holds(now, nowNbt, after, afterNbt)` (StillOurs.java:76-102):
- `fluidHolds` (a water source or ice cap holds any water, ice, frosted ice or air; lava likewise), fluid in cleared air;
- the `spread` set (dirt, grass_block, mycelium, podzol) is interchangeable;
- otherwise the **same block**, every property equal except the volatile ones (`open`, `powered`, `lit`, `waterlogged`, `age`,
  `moisture`, `distance`, ...; connections on walls, fences and bars; `shape` on stairs and rails; `level` on composters and
  cauldrons), the block entity's presence equal, an empty container still empty.
- **No copper rule anywhere in mod/.** A weathering step (`copper_block` -> `exposed_copper`), waxing (`waxed_copper_block`) and
  scraping are block-id changes, so each fails "same block".

**Who asks it:**
- `Journal.planUndo` (Journal.java:258-389): a **BOX** entry on top always restores (`ours = true`, :324); a **CELL** entry
  restores only when `world.holds` / `match.same` (:329), else the cell is counted `Stats.changed` and reported `kept`.
- **Region tiles are CELL entries** (`InfraPlace`, `RegionKinds`: `architect:terrain`, `architect:path`); **lots are BOX sites**
  (RegionsImpl.java:1430-1452). So copper written by a region part (a wall's trim, a copper lantern or lamp, a bridge's rail,
  a prop, a grate) that weathers is left standing by `Regions.remove`. A lot's building restores its box exactly whatever the
  copper did.
- Deltas: `DeltaPlanner.outcome` and its shape-neighbour test via `WorldJournal.same`: a weathered site cell becomes an "edited"
  Kept cell (`Edits.KEEP`) and can trip `PLAYER_EDITS`.
- PT2's adopted-site edit count (SiteDeltas.java:399), the startup settle's revert and lost-write votes (SiteDeltas.java:1625,
  1699), `Sites.foreignBlockEntities` (:833) and the removal blockers' `journalOwn` (:1741): a weathered **copper chest** or
  **copper golem statue** (block entities) fails `journalOwn` today.
- **Block-only tests that bypass StillOurs:** `Builder.Run.matches` (Builder.java:404-409; rescan's `built`, finish, the swap's
  `holdsOld`, deconstruct's `asPlaced`), `RoadBuilder.refundOf` (via `matches`), `Sites.evidence` (:2482-2485).
- PT (`Placed.java:341, 600-603`): a cell that stays a block keeps its player-placed record through weathering; an undo
  restores the record only for cells it writes.

**The survival refund** (`survival/Refunds.classify`, Refunds.java:33-41, with `asPlaced = r.matches(now, qi)`):
- `REFUND` pays the queued target's cost (`r.cost.get(qi)`: the plan's block);
- `PLAYER_DROP` pays `Cells.cost(now)` (the current block) as a drop at the site, never to the stockpile;
- `NONE` for air, the snapshot's block, or `Refunds.natural` (water, lava, fire, snow, ice, short grass, leaves, soil to soil).
- **Today a weathered copper cell fails `matches`, so it is a `PLAYER_DROP`:** the player's own copper comes back as a drop of
  the weathered item, never credited to the stockpile, and the BOX restore then removes the block anyway.
- VOC item 11 binds the principle: "the survival deconstruct refund equals the items of the blocks standing" (C29: "refunded
  what actually stood").

**The table.** `kit/tools/VocabDump.java` reads vanilla's `WeatheringCopper.NEXT_BY_BLOCK` and `HoneycombItem.WAXABLES` into
`blocks.mjs`'s `wx {next?, waxed?}`: 60 rows, 15 forms x 4 stages (block, chiseled, cut, cut slab, cut stairs, bars, bulb, chain,
chest, door, golem statue, grate, lantern, trapdoor, lightning rod), all waxable. The `copper` family is 120 blocks (VOC-a).
`copper_ore`, `raw_copper_block` and `copper_torch` are outside the chain.

**What VOC's probe measured** (voc-natural item 9, `tools/lib/gate6cvoc-b.mjs:404-489`, recorded, never judged): 157 of 157
unwaxed copper cells of `voc_copper_hall` weathered under `dev.vocab.tick`; after `Regions.remove`, 134-148 cells inside the
hall's lot box + 1 differed from the snapshot, **all classed `growth`** (VOCb2: kept 134, `{growth 134, live 1}`; VOCb-verify
138; another run 0 and 157 growth; another 148). **Reading:** the hall is a lot, so its box is a BOX entry and is restored
exactly; `growth` is RegionHash's plants and grass spread, never a copper block. The figure the PLAN quotes is most likely
grass regrowing on the restored pad, not copper left standing. The driver kept only counts, not the cell list. **The real
exposure is the CELL paths and block-only tests above**, which no probe has measured yet (§8 item 1 measures them first).

### 1. The rule

**A copper block is ours while it stays in its own chain.** Two states are the same "copper" when they have the same **form**
(block, cut, stairs, slab, door, ...) at any weathering stage, waxed or not. Shape-defining properties still compare as today
(`facing`, `half`, `type`, `axis`); volatile ones stay volatile. A player record wins (§2.3).

### 2. `StillOurs` (Java)

**2.1 The canonical form.** `Copper.canonical(Block) -> Block`: unwax (`HoneycombItem.WAX_OFF_BY_BLOCK`), then the chain's first
stage (`WeatheringCopper.getFirst`). Read from vanilla at class load, never a hand table, so a new copper form in a later
Minecraft version joins by itself. A unit test pins the 60 rows against `blocks.mjs`'s `wx` table (the kit's own dump), so the
two never disagree silently.

**2.2 `holds`.** Before "same block": if `canonical(now) == canonical(after)` and both are in the chain, compare as the same block
(the properties of the two states, the block entity's presence, the empty-container rule for the copper chest). Everything
else is unchanged.

**2.3 Player records first.** `holds` itself stays pure (no PT lookup). Every caller that already consults PT's records keeps
doing so first: a cell PT records as player-placed after our entry is the player's, whatever its block. A player who mined our
copper and placed their own oxidized block there is not ours. A player who waxed or scraped our block in place is (no
placement is recorded: the block is still the one we wrote).

**2.4 `WorldJournal.same` and `holds`** (the wrappers, WorldJournal.java:393-410) apply the same canonical rule in their block
pre-filter, so every StillOurs caller in §0 gets it at once.

### 3. The block-only tests

Each gets the canonical comparison, so a weathered cell counts exactly as StillOurs counts it:
- `Builder.Run.matches` (rescan's `built`, finish, the swap's `holdsOld`, deconstruct's `asPlaced`): **without this a survival
  build that weathers while it waits re-queues and charges a copper cell again.** That is also fixed.
- `RoadBuilder.refundOf` (through `matches`).
- `Sites.evidence`'s block-id test (the startup settle's evidence).
- `Journal.reactivate`'s plain `equals` is left: it compares recorded values, not the world.

### 4. Refunds: what the refund pays

**Proposed: the current block, as a `REFUND`.** A weathered, waxed or scraped copper cell whose canonical form matches the
queued target is `asPlaced`, so it is a `REFUND` (credited to the stockpile like any other), and it pays the items of the block
**standing** (`Cells.cost(now)`: an `oxidized_copper`, a `waxed_exposed_cut_copper_stairs`). That is VOC item 11's and C29's
rule ("refunded what actually stood"): the refund never mints an unweathered block the world no longer holds, and a player's
honeycomb comes back inside the waxed block.
- The ledger's charge stays the original block's (the plan's), so the stockpile records `charged copper_block, refunded
  oxidized_copper` for that cell. Accounting tests compare per-item, so they see it.
- The alternative (pay the original block) is S-CU-2.
- Delta refunds (CONTRACT "refund removed or changed cells only if paid and still ours") follow from §2: a weathered cell is
  still ours, so a delta that removes it refunds it (the standing block's items).
- PT2 adopted sites: the "snapshot block equals the current block" rule (Builder.java:1854-1856) compares canonically, so an
  adopted copper roof that weathered after adoption is still NONE (it was the player's to begin with).

### 5. The other drift kinds (VOC's `metrics.drift`)

VOC's `drifts(state)` lists unwaxed copper, farmland, ice, snow, saplings and propagules, and non-persistent leaves.

| Drift | Becomes | Ours after CU? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| copper (weathering, waxing, scraping) | another stage of its chain | **yes** | §1 |
| farmland drying or trampled | dirt | **yes, proposed** (farmland joins the `spread` set, both ways) | the same kind of drift as grass to dirt, which is ours today; a field undo then restores it |
| non-persistent leaves decaying | air | no (as today) | air is also what a player's mining leaves; undo can't tell them apart |
| sapling or propagule growing | a tree | no (as today) | a tree is new blocks over many cells; it is growth |
| snow layers, ice melting (not a body's ice) | other layers, water | no (as today) | M17's concern; a body's ice is H's `fluidHolds` |

Farmland is S-CU-3. Everything else stays as today and is recorded in §8 item 5.

### 6. API and versions

- **Placeholders:** mod 0.40.0, API 1.37.0 (one feature string, `weatheringOurs` under `journal`, so Steward can tell which
  removal it gets; no record, method or enum changes), kit unchanged (no kit output moves: the dump already exists).
- **Behaviour:** fewer `kept` cells in `Removed` / `RemoveResult` / `keptCells` after a region or site removal over copper; a
  weathered copper refund moves from `PLAYER_DROP` (at the site) to `REFUND` (to the stockpile).
- api-compat clean; apijars over the HY jar and the two before it.

### 7. Steward's side

Nothing to write: Steward reads `kept` counts and refund rows already. **What changes for Steward:** a removal of a region with
copper parts that weathered now comes back with fewer kept cells, and a survival removal credits the stockpile with the
weathered items instead of dropping them. Steward's pre-release check (S-CU-4) confirms both on its own copper build.

## Phase 6c slice IRR: farm irrigation (FROZEN 2026-10-20, Steward reviewed)

Working farms: a water source in every 9x9 of a farm lot's field, so all of its farmland is hydrated. Each source is an H body
(contained, drained first on undo), and the region owns it, not the lot design: **lot designs never own fluids** (Steward's
S-HY-2, binding). Set by one Architect member on the farm lot. PLAN "Queued (coordinator, 2026-10-19): Farm irrigation".
Over HY and KC.

- **Branch:** `slice/IRR`, worktree `../architect-mc-IRR`. **Spend:** $0.
- **Scope:** the member (§1), the field and its grid (§2), the source body (§3), the lot box exception and its order (§4), the
  lot design's side (§5), villagers and crops (§6), survival (§7), the gate (§10).
- **Not in scope:** crops (the lot design's, or the villagers'); water anywhere else in a lot box; mechanisms (hoppers, water
  streams for harvest); terraced or multi-level fields (one level per lot); district lots in Steward's own districts (D2, not
  started on Steward's side); survival building (RS).
- **Depends on:** H (bodies, the farm pond's lot detection), HY (one frozen volume per part shared by its bodies' guards, the
  ordered fluids stage), KC (the footprint registry and `M25:clear`).

### 0. Facts (main plus HY)

- **No field exists anywhere.** No kit op, template or sidecar brief writes farmland or crops; a farm lot's field comes only from
  the library entry bound to the lot (`asks/farm_village` notes "no field part exists in the catalogue"). `BuildKind.FARM`
  classifies existing builds only.
- **The lot box:** `r.lot` (`program.mjs:2013-2097`) cuts air over the footprint from `floorY` to the box top, writes the pad's
  top at `floorY - 1` (role `surface`), its foundation and a 1-column apron. The box starts at `floorY`, so **the pad's top is the
  region's and stands just under the box.** A lot's entry is fitted into the box (`LotFitting.fit`) and placed as a **LAYER, BOX
  site item after the stage's tiles and roads** (RegionsImpl.java:1277-1300, 1430-1452); with no entry the lot is a pad.
- **K5:** "a region never writes CELL over BOX; region tiles skip cells that site entries own" (SETTLEMENTS §8.4). H's
  `M25:keep` keeps every body clear of a lot box + 1 in x, y and z (`checkFluids.mjs:61`, `place.mjs:395`).
- **The farm pond (H-a)** is the template for detection: `farmPondZones` (`pond.mjs:400-413`) reads a lot's `farmPond` or its
  zone's, and a lot is a farm when `(l.villager ?? inferVillager(l.type)) === 'farm'` (`params.mjs:72-79`: farm, field, barn,
  orchard, pasture, garden). It reads `program.lots` and `params.lots` only; Java's `PlanChecks.farmPond` reads district lots too
  (a mismatch IRR fixes for its own member). The pond stands 4 columns outside the box; it is never capped (a freezing biome gets
  none); its stage is `lots`; its guards go to `K.record.guards`. Its shell is not billed.
- **HY:** ditches run outside lot boxes and "hydrate nothing" (§7.6, as built: water 4 from the box). Courses keep off lot boxes
  + 3.
- **Vanilla 26.3** (assumed, probed in §10 item 9): farmland is hydrated by water within 4 horizontally, at its own level or one
  above (`FarmBlock.isNearWater`: `pos.offset(-4, 0, -4)` to `pos.offset(4, 1, 4)`); a source at the centre of a 9x9 hydrates
  all 80 cells around it. A source on farmland's level in a 1x1 hole is the vanilla farm.

### 1. The member: `irrigate: true`

- **On a lot** (`$defs.lot`, beside `farmPond`) and on `zone.standard` (every farm lot of the zone), exactly as `farmPond`:
  `irrigate: true` asks, `false` on a lot overrides its zone, absent is off. Added to `validateLots`' allowlist (the compiler's,
  never the layout's lot). No catalogue id (a member, as `farmPond`); a catalogue note on `form.pond` is not needed.
- **Read from every place a lot can be** (`program.lots`, `params.lots`, `program.districts[].lots`), kit and Java alike.
- On a lot that is not a farm: the zone's note `irrigate: <lot> is not a farm lot`, nothing written (as `farmPond`).
- **Why a boolean:** the grid is vanilla's one useful pattern (a source per 9x9). A later pattern (rows, a centre channel) would
  be a string value then; `true` stays its meaning. The alternative name `irrigation: "9x9"` is N-IRR-1.
- With both `farmPond` and `irrigate`, both are placed (the pond outside the box, the sources inside); they don't interact.

### 2. The field and the grid

- **The field** is the lot's footprint less a 1-column border (the design's fence or path) and less the front row (the entrance
  side), at the pad's level: farmland level `floorY`.
- **The grid:** sources along each axis, `n = ceil(L / 9)` for a field side of `L`, spaced evenly (ties toward the back-left
  corner, integer), so **every field column is within 4 of a source** in both axes (Chebyshev). A 13 x 11 farm (v49's f1) gets
  2 x 1 sources; a 9 x 9 field 1; a 64 x 64 lot (field 62 x 61) 7 x 7.
- A field side under 3 asks nothing (`irrigate: <lot>'s field is too small`, a note).
- **Level:** the field must be level (the pad is). A lot on a terraced or sloped pad keeps its pad level, so this always holds.

### 3. The source body

Each source is an H body, `<lot>_irr_<i>_<j>` (kind `irrigation`, a new `waters[].kind`), from `r.fluidBody`:
- **cells:** the one source at `(x, floorY, z)`; open top.
- **shell:** the bed under it (`floorY - 1`, the pad's own cell, rewritten by IRR's part in the bible's `fluids.bed`, which must
  differ from the pad's surface block, H-a's reading) and the 4 side cells at `floorY`, written by IRR's part as **`farmland[moisture=7]`**
  (`fs`, not `g`; farmland is where the field starts, so the design's grid meets it).
- **The edges must survive until the water arrives.** The shells are written in `ground` and the sources only in the last stage;
  dry farmland with no crop turns to dirt on a random tick, and the live check would then find a shell that no longer holds and
  skip the source (`uncontained`). Two guards: the edges are written at `moisture=7` (volatile in StillOurs), and **IRR depends
  on CU's S-CU-3** (farmland and dirt interchangeable in StillOurs), so a dried edge still holds. If Steward declines S-CU-3, IRR
  writes the edges as `dirt` instead (vanilla hydrates the field around them all the same; only the four edge cells are not
  farmland) and says so in the lot's note.
- **No notch** (1 deep: a mob steps out). M25:trap and M25:exit hold by construction; the gate measures them.
- **Ice:** a freezing biome caps sources (N-H-4), which stops hydration. **Proposed:** the lot gets no irrigation and a note
  (`irrigate: the biome freezes the sources`), as the farm pond does. Lit fields (a lamp in the design) are not counted on.
- **One frozen volume per lot,** shared by its sources' guards (HY batch's rule under the 16-volume limit): the box's footprint
  from `floorY - 2` to `floorY + 2`.
- **Stage:** the shells in `ground` (before the lot item); the sources in `fluids` (last), as every body.
- **KC:** each source registers its footprint at resolve (step 2); every later writer keeps clear; `M25:clear` judges it.

### 4. The lot box exception, and the realise order

IRR is the first region write inside a lot box. The exception is narrow and named:
- **The irrigation cells** of a lot are the sources, their side shells and the cell above each source (`floorY + 1`, kept open).
  They are recorded on the lot (`lots[].irrigation {cells: runs, sources: n}` in the IR and the plan-check artifact).
- **K5, amended:** a region never writes in a lot box, **except its own lot's irrigation cells**. `M25:keep` and the M1 lot-box
  rule exempt exactly those cells for exactly that lot's irrigation bodies; every other lot, build and keep-out stays kept.
- **The breach.** A single breach of a side shell lets the source run into the field (at most 7 over farmland, washing crops).
  **Proposed:** the breach may reach **its own lot's box** (the field), never another lot, build, protected area or keep-out.
  A breach is a player's act (breaking farmland beside the water), as in any vanilla farm (S-IRR-3).
- **The lot's site never writes an irrigation cell.** `LotFitting.fit` takes the lot's irrigation cells as a mask: the entry's
  blocks there are dropped (reported `irrigationDropped: n` on the lot's site ext). The site's BOX entry then excludes those
  cells, so the lot's own removal, an undo, a `versionOf` replacement ("add a floor"), PT2's adopt and Steward's claim and
  release never touch them. The region owns them until the region is removed.
- **Realise order:** region tiles (the shells, `ground`), then the lot items (masked), then the fluids stage (the sources). The
  live check at the fluids stage needs each shell to hold the region's own top entry, which the mask guarantees.
- **Removal:** the region's removal drains the sources first (H's drain), then the shells go back to their befores. A lot removed
  alone leaves the sources standing in the region (the field around them is the site's and goes); the sources stay contained by
  their own shells. Removing the region with the lot still standing drains the sources and restores the shells; the lot's
  design keeps its cells.

### 5. The lot design's side

- **The brief:** the plan-check artifact's `lots[]` gains `irrigation {cells, sources}`, and the lot's design request carries
  it (`fitBox` plus `reserved`), so the design leaves those cells and lays farmland on the field's level around them. The mask in
  §4 is the guarantee; the brief is what makes the design look right.
- **`Entry.cells()`** (C37b) and `lotProblem`: an entry's cells at irrigation cells are not counted (they are dropped), so the
  pre-check's count is the count placed.
- **Sidecar:** the lot design prompt gains one line when `reserved` is present ("these cells are water and its edge, keep them;
  farmland around them is hydrated"). Not tuned against eval briefs.

### 6. Villagers, crops and the farm pond

- **Villager farmers** till, plant and harvest farmland with a composter in reach; the sources and their farmland don't change
  their job. Paths never cross a 1x1 hole (vanilla avoids water).
- **Crops:** the design's or the villagers'. The side shells are farmland, so a crop above them is the design's to write (the
  cell above a side shell is not reserved; above the source is).
- **`farmPond`** is unchanged and independent (decorative, outside the box; S-H-2).
- **HY's ditches** stay outside the box and hydrate nothing; IRR is the in-field block S-H-2 deferred.

### 7. Survival, API and wire

- **Survival:** INSTANT only (N-K1-3; regions refuse survival worlds today). `cost.bom` on the zone's answer: water free (N-H-1),
  the bed blocks and the farmland priced as `dirt` (vocab survival map). RS builds it later.
- **Plan check:** `PlanChecks.hasH` gains `irrigate` (any depth, districts included), so the plan takes the two-plan flow.
- **API** (placeholders): API 1.38.0, mod 0.41.0, kit 0.38.0. Feature `farmIrrigation` (`region.fluids`). Additive: the lot def's
  `irrigate`; the artifact's and IR's `lots[].irrigation`; `siteplan.waters[].kind` `irrigation`; the realise report's
  `architect_mc:fluids` rows (one per source); the lot site's ext `irrigationDropped`. `LotFitting`'s mask is internal.
  api-compat clean.
- **Catalogue:** unchanged (a member). `plan/0`'s def gains the member, so Steward's plan writer sees it there.
- **Byte identity:** every plan without `irrigate` is byte-identical (the member is absent; `plan_v0.mjs` is not edited).

### 11. Size and split

One owner, about **2-2.5 days**: the member, detection and grid (0.5 day); the body, the volume and KC's registry (0.25 day);
the mask in `LotFitting` and the site's BOX entry, the K5/M25 exemption (0.5 day); the design brief line and the artifact

## Phase 6c slice VOC-c: `rule.palette` measured (FROZEN 2026-10-20, Steward reviewed)

"Only copper" and "no wood": `rule.palette` goes from reserved to supported. The plan check measures a family's share over the
parts in the rule's scope and over the lots in scope, using their bound entries, and `realiseApproved` refuses a required rule
that an approved entry breaks. Steward's S-VOC-2 (binding: "its own slice after VOC-a and VOC-b ... 'Only copper' and 'no
wood' are the target asks"); PLAN "Queued (coordinator, 2026-10-19): VOC-c". Over HY (catalogue 8) and whatever else of this
batch merges first.

- **Branch:** `slice/VOCc`, worktree `../architect-mc-VOCc`. **Spend:** $0.
- **Scope:** the strict def and its lenient read (§1); the measure (§2); the plan-time answers and the re-plan for an upper bound
  of 0 (§3); lots from bound entries and the `realiseApproved` refusal (§4); the catalogue (§5); how the plan writer and Claude
  learn it (§6); the gate (§9).
- **Not in scope:** every other `rule.*` (RC); `gradient` and colour rules ("bright at centre", "family colours"); a palette as a
  design constraint inside Architect's own design jobs (§6, a note only); `palette()` over generated families (VOC §10).
- **Steward's RC check before release** (a new `realiseApproved` refusal, GATES policy 4).

### 0. Facts (main 0d665136 plus HY)

- **Catalogue:** `rule.palette` is `{sinceApi 1.23.0, schemaVersion 0, state reserved, until RC}` (`plan-catalogue.golden.json:628`),
  no limits, no note. HY's catalogue 8 leaves every `rule.*` as it is, and **HY already archived catalogue 7 as
  `catalogue-h.json`**, so VOC §11's sketch ("catalogue 8, archive 7") is stale: VOC-c archives HY's 8.
- **The def** (`plan.json:836`, x-state reserved): `{family: string, share: [a, b] in 0..1, exempt: [terrain | support]}` over
  `rule.common` (`id`, `kind`, `required`, `scope` <= 32 part ids, absent = the whole plan). R11: "a required rule that can't be
  verified blocks readiness". Reserved kinds answer `unsupported {block, until}` (`schema.mjs:420-432`); `overallOf` makes a
  required unsupported part `REQUIRED_BLOCKED` (`finish.mjs:40-46`).
- **`partAnswer` is closed** (`additionalProperties: false`, plan.json:891-910): a measured value needs an additive member.
- **No rule is enforced anywhere today.**
- **Families** (`kit/lib/vocab.mjs` `familyOf`; generated `fam` in `blocks.mjs`): 450, 83 with more than one member. `copper` is 120
  blocks (every stage, waxed or not, of 15 forms); `stone` 23 (cobblestone included). **There is no `wood` family:** each wood is
  its own (`oak`'s 18 members: planks, logs, wood, stripped, doors, signs, ...; leaves and saplings outside). The hand lists
  `WOODS` (13, `kit.mjs:107`) and the vanilla tags (`blocks.mjs` `hasTag`/`tagBlocks`) exist. Mind the name clash:
  `blocks.mjs:2653` also exports a `familyOf` (the Java family).
- **Measured cells** (VOC as built): written, not air, not a fluid source, not a common natural block. Per-part histograms come from
  `vocabCells` (`checkVocab.mjs:237`), built today only when the bible opts in or a precious or creative-only block is written.
  A realised world's lot children are skipped (`checkVocab.mjs:90`).
- **Lots and entries:** a plan lot's `entry` (`id` or `id@version`; absent = provisional) goes to the artifact's `lots[]`
  (`finish.mjs:117-135`). **The kit never reads a library entry during a check**, so no cost or rarity covers a lot's building.
  Java's `Library.Entry.cells()` is a non-air count (C37b); no API gives an entry's block histogram.
- **`realiseApproved`** (`PlanChecks.java:883-959`): entries merge (the artifact's, then `r.lotEntries()`); `lotProblem`
  (:1211-1245) checks **provisional** lots only (exists, fits the fitBox, `cells` within `costRange`). Codes today:
  `NOT_LOADED`, `ARTIFACT_UNAPPROVED`, `ARTIFACT_STALE`. `Reason` ends at `ADOPT_REFUSED` (Reason.java:93-111).
- **`vocab/1`** (`kit/schemas/vocab-1.json`, systemRef `vocab/1` with `#compact`; `sidecar/src/jobs/systemrefs.ts:45`): families,
  tiers, colours, survival; the word "palette" appears nowhere. Steward hasn't adopted it yet ("`vocab/1` for the plan writer
  once VOC-c lands", STEWARD-SYNC). Architect's own design prompts don't use it.
- **Steward's recorded palette rules (7):**

| Ask / rule | required | Members | Today |
|---|---|---|---|
| one_block / copper_only | yes, scope `reach` | `params {family: copper, share: [1, 1], exempt: [terrain, support], gradient}` | unsupported (required: the plan is REQUIRED_BLOCKED) |
| mage_exiles / shared_stone_base | no | `params {family: stone, exempt: [terrain, support]}` | unsupported |
| hidden_village / mossy_palette | no | top-level `family: moss_stone_spruce_oak` (no such family) | unsupported |
| rival_families / family_colours | no, scope `estates` | top-level `family: family_colours`, `exempt` | unsupported |
| old_new_town / two_styles | **yes** | prose only | unsupported (REQUIRED_BLOCKED) |

### 1. The def (strict, additive) and its lenient read

```
rule.palette: {id, kind: "palette", required?, scope?, label?, notes?,
               family: string,                 // a vocab/1 family, or a group (§1.1)
               share?: [min, max],             // the family's share of measured cells; default [1, 1] ("only")
               exempt?: ["terrain" | "support"],  // default both
               params?}
```
- **"Only copper"** is `{family: copper}` (share defaults to [1, 1]). **"No wood"** is `{family: wood, share: [0, 0]}`. "Mostly
  stone" is `{family: stone, share: [0.6, 1]}`.
- **Lenient read (S-K1-3):** `family`, `share` and `exempt` are read from `params` when the top level doesn't give them (Steward
  writes both). `gradient`, `colours`, `material` and other `params` keys are noted ("noted, not read"), never read.

**1.1 Groups.** A `family` value may name a **group**, a fixed union of families, listed in `vocab/1` (§6):
- `wood`: the 13 woods of `WOODS` (`kit.mjs:107`: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark_oak, mangrove, cherry, pale_oak,
  poplar, bamboo, crimson, warped), every member of their families; leaves and saplings are outside those families already,
  and logs written as a tree are terrain (exempt).
- No other group in VOC-c. A group is a closed list in the kit (`kit/lib/vocab/groups.mjs`), generated into `vocab/1`; a new
  group is a later additive change (N-VOCc-1).

### 2. The measure

- **Cells:** VOC's measured cells (written, not air, not a fluid source, not a common natural block), less the exempt ones:
  - `terrain`: cells written in the role `terrain` and by terrain ops (brushes, scatter, relief, a zone's ground and pads'
    batter), **not by stage**: H's and HY's forms emit in `ground` and `forms` too, and a body's shell, a fountain's rim, a
    terrace's walls and every other part's cells **count**;
  - `support`: foundations, footings, piers and pads (the roles `foundation` and `support`, and a lot's pad).
- **Over parts:** the IR parts whose plan part is in `scope` (or all, with no scope), from `vocabCells`, which now runs whenever
  the plan holds a `rule.palette`.
- **Over lots:** the lots of the zones and districts in scope, from their **bound entries** (§4). A provisional lot is not
  measured at check time (§3).
- **The share:** `family cells / measured cells`, by cell count, parts and bound lots together. Integer counts, exact.
- **Recorded per rule:** `{cells, family, share, parts: {id: [family, cells]}, lots: {id: [family, cells]}, pendingLots: [ids]}`.

### 3. Answers at plan time

- **A rule whose family resolves**, measured within `share` over parts and bound lots: `fits`, with the new optional
  `partAnswer.measured` member (above, capped at 16 parts and 16 lots, the worst first).
- **An upper bound of 0** ("no wood"): the compile pass **plans again with the family excluded** from every role chain of the
  parts in scope (a new `ctx.paletteExclude`, a set of block ids; VOC-a's re-plan loop pattern, at most 3 passes in all; note
  that VOC-a's `ctx.vocabRefuse` refuses whole parts, so it is not reused), and materials fall to the next block of their role's
  chain. If it then measures 0: `adjusted`,
  with the substitutions as deviations. If a part still writes the family (a role with no other block): `refused VOCAB`
  (`evidence {rule, block, cells}`, VOC's code), naming the part.
- **A share missed with no fix** (only copper, and a stone wall in scope): `refused TOLERANCE {kind: "palette", family, share,
  measured, worst: [parts and lots]}`; `wouldFit`: the rule with `share` widened to the measured value, re-checked alone.
- **An unknown family or group** (`moss_stone_spruce_oak`, `family_colours`): `refused NO_FEATURE {kind: "family", family}`;
  `wouldFit`: the nearest family by name if one resolves, else the rule with `required: false`.
- **No family at all** (the prose rules): `refused NO_FEATURE {kind: "family"}`, note "palette guidance only: give a family to
  measure it"; `wouldFit`: the rule with `required: false` (a non-required rule never blocks).
- **Provisional lots in scope.** A required rule can't be verified for a lot without an entry. **R11 is amended:** such a rule
  answers by the parts and bound lots, lists `pendingLots`, and is **verified at `realiseApproved`** for each lot the realise
  binds (§4). Without that, every required palette rule over a provisional village would block readiness forever.
- S-K1-6 and S-K1-7 bind: a newly refused pending part is a repair; unknown codes and kinds pass through.

### 4. Lots from bound entries, and the `realiseApproved` refusal (Java)

- **The artifact carries what Java needs, so Java needs no vocabulary:** each rule with lots in scope becomes
  `palette: [{rule, required, lots: [ids], blocks: [ids in the family], natural: [ids not measured], share: [a, b]}]` in the
  plan-check artifact (sorted, deduplicated; `natural` is VOC's common-natural list). The plan check's sha covers it.
- **At check time,** for a lot whose entry is named in the plan, the mod reads the entry's blueprint and passes its block
  histogram to the kit with the check request (`lotBlocks: {lot: {block: n}}`), so §2 measures it then. Its counts become part
  of the artifact.
- **At `realiseApproved`,** after `lotProblem` and before the protection check: for every **required** palette rule, each lot it
  binds now (named in the artifact or supplied in `lotEntries`) is measured from its blueprint (non-air, not in `natural`, the
  pad excluded), and the rule's share is recomputed from the artifact's parts count plus every bound lot. A share outside
  `share` refuses the realise:
  - **code `PALETTE`** (a new `Reason`, appended at the end of the enum; `$defs/reason.code` gains it), with evidence `{rule, lot,
    entry, family, share, measured, cells}`, naming the worst lot.
  - Nothing is written. The caller re-binds a lot (another entry) or drops `required`.
- A non-required rule never refuses; the realise report notes its measured share (`architect_mc:palette` ext rows).
- A lot entry replaced later (`versionOf`, "add a floor") is a site operation, not a realise: it is not re-judged (S-VOCc-3).

### 10. Size and split

One owner, about **1.5-2 days**: the def, groups and measure (0.5 day); the answers and the `paletteExclude` re-plan (0.25 day);
the artifact rows, `lotBlocks` and the Java refusal (0.5 day); the catalogue, `vocab/1` and fixtures (0.25 day); the in-game round
(0.25-0.5 day). If smaller is wanted: plan-time only (parts and named entries), with the `realiseApproved` refusal deferred,
saves about half a day and the RC check, but then "only copper" over provisional lots is never enforced.

**IRR's breach sweep (the verifier's finding 2, fixed before the RC; safety).** The removal drain followed every same-fluid cell
connected to an irrigation body within its lot's box grown by 8, sources included, so a breach's flow that joined a pond or a
player's water there took them too: only the watch sets' water from before the realise was spared.
- **The fix** (`RegionFluids.breachFlow` -> `breachTake`, pure). The drain now judges the breach's flow before it writes anything
  (once the source is air, its flow has no feeder left to tell it from anyone else's water). It takes the flowing water connected
  to the body's cells, shell and watch, inside the same bounds: never a source (a pond's, a player's bucket, a waterlogged block),
  never water there before the realise, never another body's cell. Then every cell with a feeder outside that set is dropped, and
  what it fed after it: a feeder is the same fluid over the cell or beside it at a higher amount, and the body's own sources count
  as inside. What remains is the flow only this body's source can have made.
- **Deviation from "cells recorded as escaped", stated.** The coordinator asked for the sweep to be limited to cells recorded as
  escaped from the body, as H's strays fix is. A breach comes after the body settled, when no census runs, so nothing records the
  flow as it runs. The record is made at the drain from the fluid levels instead, and used for that one pass, never saved: a later
  drain (a resumed removal, the region's after the lot's) would otherwise take what a player poured there since. A periodic shell
  check that re-opens a census would record it as it runs, at a per-tick cost, and would record a player's water that touches the
  flow as escaped. **Limit:** where a foreign flow meets the breach's flow the joint cells are spared, so a few cells of joint
  water can stay outside the lot after its removal (queued in PLAN).
- **Tests.** `RegionFluidsBreachTest` (7): a bare flow with its falling column and spread, all taken; a foreign source joining it
  (the joint cells and everything downstream of them spared); a pond; a waterlogged neighbour; water from before and another
  body's cells; the source already drained (a resumed removal: the flow still taken); the box. In game, irr-ingame's new section
  `spare`: v62 with its field entries; a 2 x 2 pond and a player's 1 x 1 well sunk one under the ground just outside f2's box on the
  side nearest its source (placed after the realise: before it, the plan check would plan round them); the source's side broken and
  a trench dug through the field to the box edge, so the flow (7 cells, 3 outside the box) runs over both and touches them. f2's
  site removed: the pond 4/4 sources, the well a source, 0 water in f2's box, 0 flow cells left outside; then `Regions.remove`:
  REMOVED, the pond and the well still standing, **E-flat over f2's own box 0** (its own snapshot: the world round it was changed
  on purpose). **Against the pre-fix sweep** (the batch's head with c97519cf's RegionFluids, a local commit never pushed:
  `artifacts/gate-runs-int-cu-prefix/20261020-173522-change`): the same case FAILS, the pond 0/4 and the well taken at the lot's
  removal; with the fix (`artifacts/gate-runs-int-cu/20261020-173522-change`, head c170b161) it passes 4/0.

- **Verifier (the fix only; gate-verifier, scoped):** **PASS** at 4354ddca: the diff c97519cf..c170b161 reviewed (never a source,

**Build order and parallelism.**
1. **FL-core and F3-a start together.** They share no module: FL lives in `kit/lib/plan/compile.mjs`'s zone dispatcher plus new

   points:** `compile.mjs` (FL's zone dispatch and `locatorOf`; F3's `resolveForm` dispatch), `kit/schemas/plan.json` and the catalogue
   golden (FL's flips; F3's flip and four added ids), `KIT_VERSION`/`IrStale`, `ArchitectApi.features()`, sidecar `FEATURES`,
   `gate-chains.json`. Each core freezes its interface at the end of its first day (FL: the zone mask and `frontage()` shapes; F3:
   the forms' column footprint and the catalogue stubs), and the later sub-slices branch from it.
2. **FL-a (ring, spiral), FL-b (grid), FL-c (organic) in parallel** over FL-core. **F3-b (mushrooms, stalactites, roots under
   ceilings) and F3-c (coral, M19)** in parallel over F3-a.
3. **The joint fixture** (`around_my_tree` as a ring round a giant oak at the hub, §FL 9 and §F3 9) runs once both are merged:
   on the integration branch, not in either slice's gate.
- **Releases:** FL and F3 can be **one batch** (one release tier, one tag, one publish: GATES policy 5), or FL alone first if F3
  runs late; the agreed order (FL before F3) holds either way. **FL needs no RC** by GATES policy 4 (plan answers
  and lot layouts only; S-FL-6 asks whether Steward wants one anyway). **F3 needs Steward's RC** (S-F3-5): its coral writes a new

## Phase 6c slice FL: free layouts (FROZEN 2026-10-20, Steward reviewed)

Lots laid out other than along one straight street: a **ring** round an open hub, a **spiral**, a **grid** of blocks, and an
**organic** web of crooked lanes; a zone (or a form) laid **around** a feature; and a zone fitted to a sketched **outline**.
COMPOSITION v2 §4 ("zones plus a path network fitted to locators and sketches", Architect's), P0's "Free layouts" at the freeze
(R4b), and Steward's strange asks (ARCHITECT-ASKS "Free layouts have no reserved name"). Over the CU/IRR/VOC-c batch (API 1.37.0,
mod 0.40.0, kit 0.38.0, catalogue 9).

- **Branch:** `slice/FL` (FL-core), then `slice/FL-a`, `slice/FL-b`, `slice/FL-c` over `fl/core`; worktrees
  `../architect-mc-FL*`. **Spend:** $0, sim and stub only.
- **Scope:** the zone mask and the frontage engine (§2), the four layouts (§3), `around` for zones and forms (§4.1), `outline`
  (§4.2), KC's rows (§5), answers and geometry (§6), the catalogue (§7), byte identity (§8), Steward's recorded plans (§9), the gate
  (§10).
- **Not in scope:**
  - **Lots on a wall's line** (towers, gatehouses, wall walks as lots: K1's open question, `castle_city`): deferred to **7a**. A
    lot on a wall line is a joined lot whose box would cut the wall (K5), and the tower or gatehouse is the wall's own structure,
    which 7a's typed connectors own. FL zones may stand *inside* a `wall.around` ring as today.
  - `layout.elevated` (treetop and ledge lots: 7b). Rotated lots: every lot stays an axis-aligned rect with a cardinal front
    (siteplan/1, `Entry.cells`, Steward's designer).
  - `rule.shape` ("no right angles", "mirrored banks", spiral_town's `spiral_shape`): RC. A street that curves is FL's; a rule
    that judges shapes is not.
  - Steward's own districts on these layouts (STEWARD-SYNC "Not started"), and districts programs whose districts pick a free
    layout (`$defs/district` has no layout member; additive later).
- **Depends on:** V (`layoutStreet`, props, lamps), C37/C37b (orientation, fronts EAST/WEST, `Entry.cells`), D1/D2 (masks,
  `followLots`), T2 (routing), K1 (`wall.around`'s meaning), KC (the footprint registry), P0 (the compiler).

### 0. Facts (integrate/batch-cu, 631f89c0)

**How a reserved layout answers today.** `schema.mjs` `nestedUnsupported()` (:168): for a lots program it runs
`reserved('program.lots')`, then `reserved('layout.<layout ?? street>', '$.program.layout')` (:200-205), then `whereCheck` (:176,
`locator.<kind>`) and `sketchCheck` (:187, `outline === true` -> `sketch.outline`); forms the same at :240. `compile.mjs:837`
answers `{class: unsupported, code UNSUPPORTED, block, until, path}`. Lighting a block is a catalogue flip plus a compile path.

**The zone path.** `compile.mjs:896-938` dispatches: `where.along` or `kind: outpost` to D2 (`resolveFollowZone`,
`resolveOutpostZone`), a districts program to `resolveDistrictsZone`, everything else to `resolveZone` (:443-535) after the cache
(:913-921). `resolveZone`:
- lots from `lotSpecs()` (`validateLots`: sizes 5..96, at most 40 lots; placements `central`, `edge`, `near_water`,
  `high_ground`), the shared space from `sharedOf()` (:394: **`shared: none` maps to a 7x7 well today**);
- `locatorOf` (:222-274): `inside`, `near`, `adjacent`; **`along` and `around` fall through to `NO_FEATURE "not compiled in v0"`**
  (:271-272) behind the reserved answer;
- `zoneSizes` (:409) from `programMinimum()` grown by quarters (presets S32, M48, L64, XL96), shrinks by a soft size tolerance;
  `searchAll` (:474) over every size (and its rotation) keeps the top `EVAL_K` 12 rects by `scan()` (:346) and evaluates each with
  `layoutStreet`; best = fewest unplaced, then size deviation, then unrotated, then score (4096 move + 8 sketch + 4 rough +
  water + aim);
- `judge()` (:204) against `TOL_DEFAULTS` (:51: move 16/64, size 25%/50%, count 0, sketch 8/32); `MARGIN` 2;
- the overlap pass (:923-933) re-resolves against earlier zones' rects only: **forms and H footprints are not zone obstacles**;
- `sketchPoint` (:329) is the sketch's centroid (q64 over the claim, or blocks from the anchor).

**V's street** (`village.mjs`): `STREET_RULES {streetWidth 5 (road 3 + a verge each side), lotGap 3, maxSlope 3, claimMargin 2}`,
`PAD_MAX` 2; `layoutStreet` (:101) searches the street line per orientation, `placeShared` (:144), `tryStreetSkipping` (:181),
`fitLot` (:199: margin, gap, keep-out + 1, dry, slope 3, pad 2; entrance the cell outside the front edge's middle),
`streetCheck` (:320), `hintScore` (:345: near_water, central, edge, high_ground; **placement and landmark are read here already**).
`streetLayout` (:523) writes pads, the square or green, verges, lanes (`lane()` :490, which throws on entering a lot box) and two
`road()` items `street_w`/`street_e` with lanterns. Props (`props.mjs planProps` :55) work in the shared space's `sh` frame.

**D2's following street** (`followEmit.mjs`) is already "a street line with lots on both sides": `placeFollow` (:27) gives
`{rect, mask, line, ends}`; the street is a T2 dry route kept within 2 of the line (`FOLLOW_WITHIN`); `followLots` (:147) walks it,
alternating sides, the front edge `FOLLOW_SETBACK` 3 off the centre (pushed up to `FOLLOW_PUSH` 4 more), a slope pad within
`FOLLOW_PAD` 6, at least 4/5 of a lot in the mask, lots 2 apart, the front the cardinal facing the street; `emitFollowLots` (:204)
writes pads, 1-wide lanes and graph nodes.

**Lots.** `program.mjs lot()` (:2055): box = footprint x [floorY, floorY + 31] for plan zones, a 1-column apron, entrance at the
front edge's middle; `front` takes a cardinal or `toward:<anchor|part>` (the dominant cardinal, :2113-2121). K5: no region op
writes inside a lot box (M1, `check.mjs:924-935`). The artifact's `lots[]` (`finish.mjs:131`): `{id, zone, box, role, label, ext,
front, entrance, entry, provisional, costRange, fitBox, ...}`; the mod's `lotProblem` (`PlanChecks.java:1251`) checks a bound entry
against `fitBox` in either rotation and `Entry.cells` against `costRange`. Nothing there reads the layout.

**Routing and walls.** Route hard rects (`program.mjs _routeObstacles` :291): lot boxes + 1, form bounds, kept columns. The wall grid
(`wall.mjs gridOf` :100) has `OB.OVERLAP` for zone rects, lots + 1 and forms, and `OB.BODY` from `keptColumns(K.keep)`.
`line.mjs` `placeRing`/`ringCells` (:137/:186) search a wall ring round a footprint inside a band.

**KC.** H footprints are reserved at resolve (`compile.mjs:889-891`) but **zones and lots never read the registry**:
`layoutStreet` sees `ctx.keepOut` and zone obstacles only. The backstop (`checkFluids.mjs clearRefusals` :252) refuses, for a
zone's writer (its lots, pads, streets, props) found in an H body's sets, **the body's part** `NO_ROOM {kind: clear}` (S-KC-1 read
as "never the zone", because zones were always placed first). `EARLY_FORMS` (:240) are relief, terrace, rock_spire, ice_spike.

**Schema** (`plan.json`, plan/0 frozen, additive only): `$defs/program.lots` `{lots 1..40, layout street|ring|spiral|grid|organic|
elevated, shared square|well|none, orientation ew|ns|auto}`, `additionalProperties: false`; `where.around {feature (required), ring:
intRange, closed: bool}`; `sketch {frame claim|anchor, anchor, unit q64|block, shape point|polyline|polygon, points <= 64, outline:
bool}`. The strict `$defs/lot` accepts `landmark`, `placement`, `villager`, `brief`. **FL needs no new member** (§7).

**Tests that pin the reserved state** (each moves, by name, in FL-core): `kit/test/builds-pt.test.mjs:39-50` (`around` unsupported),
`tools/gate6cpt.mjs:1064-1077` (pt-ingame item 14: `ring` answers `unsupported locator.around`), `kit/test/districts-d2.test.mjs:159`,
`plan-p0.test.mjs` (the catalogue diff), `catalogue-since`, `extension/e07_ring_layout`, `e14_sketch_outline`, `e15_every_reserved_a`
and `e16_every_reserved_b` (the reserved lists), `plan-p0-asks.test.mjs`'s tally (the five waiting zones now answer).

### 1. The rule in one line

**A free layout is a zone mask, a street line (or a street grid) inside it, and lots on that line**, every lot an axis-aligned rect
facing the street with a cardinal front, every street a V street (road 3 plus verges, W's lanterns), every lot box + 1 kept as V
keeps it. Only the street's shape is new.

### 2. FL-core: the zone mask and the frontage engine

**2.1 The mask.** Every FL zone resolves to `{rect, mask, line | grid, hub?, ends}`, D2's shape (`placeFollow`) generalised:
- `rect` the mask's bounds; `mask` a cell set (rect for ring/spiral/grid/organic inside a locator; an annulus for `around`, §4.1;
  the outline's raster for `outline`, §4.2);
- obstacles: the claim margin, `ctx.keepOut` (C17, PT builds + 1), earlier zones' rects, **earlier forms' bounds and every
  registered H footprint** (§5: new for zones), standing regions' footprints (D1 `standing`), natural water;
- size search as `resolveZone` (programMinimum by quarters, presets, tolerances), each candidate evaluated by its layout, best by
  the same order (fewest unplaced, size deviation, score).

**2.2 The frontage engine** (`kit/lib/region/frontage.mjs`, new; D2's `followLots` and `emitFollowLots` are its model and stay
unchanged for byte identity): given a street centre line (an 8-connected polyline, open or closed), a mask and lot specs:
- the street is a T2 dry route kept within 2 of the line (as D2), graded as V's `streetCheck` (steps of 1, within 3);
- lots are taken in V's `orderOf` (central, landmark, rest, edge), placed on the chosen side(s) with their front edge
  `setback` off the centre line (3, as D2; organic varies it, §3.4), at least `lotGap` 3 apart, wholly inside the mask, dry, slope 3,
  pad 2 (V's `fitLot` rules);
- each lot's **front is the cardinal of its nearest street cell** (`toward:` resolution, `program.mjs:2113`), so lots on a ring
  face N, E, S or W by quadrant; its entrance the cell outside its front edge's middle, joined to the street by a lane (V's
  `lane()`, 1 wide, never through a lot box);
- `placement` hints scored as V's `hintScore` (near_water, central, edge, high_ground), plus **central -> the hub** where the layout
  has one (§3.1);
- returns V's shape (`lots`, `unplaced`, `lanes`, `graph`), so pads, props, lamps, the bell, golems, M23/M24 and the siteplan run
  unchanged downstream.

**2.3 The hub.** Ring and spiral leave an open centre; organic grows from a green. The hub replaces V's shared space and gives
props a compatible `sh` frame:
- `shared: square` -> V's square at the hub centre; `well` -> the 7x7 well green; **`none` -> nothing written**: the hub's ground
  stays as it is (a planted oak, a fire pit the lot design brings, a giant tree from F3). V's mapping of `none` to a well is
  unchanged for street layouts.
- The bell and the golem cells go in the hub (or beside the hub's central lot when `none` leaves it bare).
- Port `hub` (the hub's centre cell) joins the zone's ports (lots, `bell`, `start`, `end`).

**2.4 Ports and joins.** A closed ring or a grid has no street ends. `start` is the street cell nearest the claim's centre and
`end` the one farthest; a connector to the zone ends on the nearest street cell to its other end (a junction node is added there),
as a road ends on V's street end today.

**2.5 Determinism.** Every choice is seeded from `fnv64(plan seed, zone id)` and ties break by id, then min x, then min z (P0's
rule). No floating point reaches the IR: lines are integer polylines.

### 3. The four layouts

**3.1 `ring` (FL-a).** A closed street round the hub, lots on its outer side facing in, and on its inner side facing out when the
hub is wide enough.
- **The line:** a rasterised circle (or, inside a non-square mask, the mask's inset contour) about the zone's centre (the
  locator's aim: an anchor, a feature's centre, the sketch point). Radius the smallest whose outer frontage holds the lots
  (sum of lot widths + gaps), searched by 2 up to the mask's inradius; the hub's radius = the radius minus half the street.
- **Central lots** (`placement: central`, the council tent, the gathering fire, the warden's hall) stand **in the hub**, facing
  the street's nearest cell; at most as many as the hub holds with `lotGap` round each; the rest join the ring.
- **Edge lots** (`placement: edge`) take the outer side; `near_water` the ring's cells nearest water; `high_ground` the highest.
- **Fits** when every lot places; `adjusted` (count) within the count tolerance; else `NO_ROOM` with `wouldFit` the size or
  ring radius that holds them, re-checked alone.

**3.2 `spiral` (FL-a).** An open street winding out from the hub, lots on its outer side, up to 3 turns.
- **The line:** an integer Archimedean spiral about the centre, pitch = 2 x (deepest lot + setback) + street, so turns never meet
  lots; ends `start` (inner, by the hub) and `end` (outer).
- **On a hill** (the mask's ground rises toward a summit inside it by at least 8): the centre is the summit, so the spiral climbs
  to it, landmark lots at the top (spiral_town's "spirals up a hill to a temple at the top"); each turn's grade within V's
  `streetCheck` (steps of 1, within 3). Too steep: fewer turns (`adjusted`), else `NO_ROOM {why: grade}` with `wouldFit` the
  ring at the hill's foot.

**3.3 `grid` (FL-b).** Blocks of V streets: avenues along one axis and cross streets along the other, lots back to back in each
block facing its two avenues.
- **Axis:** the zone's C37 `orientation` names the avenues' axis (`ew`: avenues run east-west); `auto` the longer side. This is
  the only free layout that reads `orientation`.
- **Blocks:** block depth = 2 x the deepest lot of the block + `lotGap`; block length fits k lots (k from 2 to 6, the best fill);
  avenues and cross streets 5 wide (V's street), junctions as graph nodes, each street segment its own `road()` item.
- **The plaza:** the central block is the shared space (`square` -> V's square filling the block; `well` the green; `none` an
  ordinary block). Central and landmark lots face it; edge lots take the outer blocks.
- **Names:** avenues numbered from the side nearest `start` (`<prefix>street_a1`, `a2`, ...; cross streets `c1`, ...), echoed in
  the geometry so a bible or card can sign them (grid_city's "numbered avenues": the signs are the bible's).

**3.4 `organic` (FL-c).** A green with lanes growing out of it like a hamlet that grew: lots of mixed setbacks along lanes that
bend.
- **The lanes:** from the green, 2 to 4 lanes (one per 4 lots, rounded), each a seeded walk in 8 headings that turns by at most
  45 degrees every 6 to 12 cells, prefers T2's cheap ground (along contours on a slope), never closer than 6 to another lane
  except where it joins one; a lane that reaches the mask's edge or another lane stops. Lanes are 3 wide (the road; verges where
  they fit, else none).
- **Irregular lots:** setback from 1 to 5 by the seed, gaps from 3 to 6, fronts by the nearest lane cell; the green's lots
  first (central, landmark), edge lots at the lanes' ends.
- **Never a grid by accident:** an axis-run share of the lanes' cells over 0.6 re-seeds once (recorded; the organic read).

### 4. Locators and sketches

**4.1 `around` (FL-a) for zones and forms.** `where: {around: {feature, ring: [r0, r1], closed}}` (the P0 shape, unchanged):
- **The feature** may be a `part` (a zone, a form, an H body), `water` (a natural lake or pond), a `build` (PT's C32 ask: "around
  a build") or `protected`; its footprint the part's resolved cells, the water body's cells, the build's rect, the area's rect.
  `feature.region` stays D1's reserved id (a district round a standing town is D1's `beside` today).
- **A zone around a feature** is laid as a **ring street following the feature's footprint**, offset into the band (`ring`
  default **[6, 32]**: the street's centre line at the smallest offset in the band where every lot places, searched by 2), lots on
  the outer side facing the feature, the feature itself the hub (nothing written in it). `closed: false` leaves out the arc
  nearest the claim's centre (K1's meaning for walls). The mask is the annulus.
- **The layout under `around`:** `ring` or `street` (or none) is read as the ring round the feature; `grid`, `spiral` or
  `organic` with `around` answers `adjusted` with deviation `{what: layout, asked, got: ring}` (S-FL-2).
- **A form around a feature** (`ice_spike`, `rock_spire`, and F3's forms when F3 lands): its `count` sites are taken from the
  annulus, evenly by angle when `count` is at least 3 (a ring of spires round a keep), `closed: false` leaving the gap.
- **On a wall** `where.around` stays the wall's own member (`wall.around`, K1): unchanged. `locator.around`'s catalogue note keeps
  that sentence.

**4.2 `outline` (FL-c).** `sketch: {shape: polygon | polyline, outline: true, ...}` (the P0 shape):
- **A polygon outline** is the zone's mask: the polygon rasterised (cells whose centre lies inside) in the claim's q64 frame or the
  anchor's block frame. The layout (`street`, `ring`, `grid`, `organic`) runs inside it; lots wholly inside it.
- **A polyline outline** is the street's line: the frontage engine lays the street along it (within 2) and lots on both sides,
  the mask the line grown by the deepest lot + setback + 2 (a street that follows the drawing).
- **Fit:** the outline is placed as drawn; when it meets an obstacle or the claim's edge, the mask is the drawn one minus those
  cells, then moved within `move`. **The deviation** is the largest distance from a drawn cell to the used mask (polygon) or from a
  drawn vertex to the routed street (polyline), judged against the part's `sketch` tolerance (soft 8, ceiling 32, in the sketch's
  unit). Past it: `refused TOLERANCE` with `wouldFit` the sketch scaled to fit, re-checked alone.

### 5. KC: every new writer keeps clear

FL's rows for KC's §4 table. The rule is KC's: a body's cells are its own, the part placed later keeps clear (S-KC-1), watch cells
strict (S-KC-2).

| Writer | Placed (vs H resolve and emit) | KC rule | Refused as |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A zone that depends on a body** (`around`, `near` or `adjacent` a `form.pond`/`fountain`/`waterfall`/`quay` or a `channel.moat`) | **after** the body's reservation (the locator target is an implicit dependency, so the body resolves first) | the zone's mask, lots + 1, streets, lanes, hub props and lamps treat the body's reserved footprint as hard (KC §2's `keptColumns`) | the zone: `adjusted` (a wider band) or `OVERLAP {kind: body, body, part}` with `wouldFit` the band that clears it |
| **Any FL zone not depending on a body** | before (as today's zones) | unchanged: the body keeps clear (H's `M25:keep` off lot box + 1) | the body: H's answers |
| Ring, spiral, grid and organic streets and lanes | with their zone | as their zone's row | as their zone |
| Hub props, lamps and the bell area | with their zone | never on a hard cell, never a non-shell-grade block in a watch cell (KC's lamp row) | the prop or lamp is skipped (M5 still judged) |
| A form `around` a body | after the body | its sites keep off the footprint + 2 | the form: `adjusted` (count) or `NO_ROOM` |

**The backstop changes in one place.** `clearRefusals` today refuses the **body** for any zone writer in its sets. FL makes "later"
follow the plan's dependency order: **when the zone depends on the body (directly or through its locator), the zone is the later part
and is refused `OVERLAP {kind: body}`; otherwise the body is refused as today.** **Checked:** none of the 187 committed plans
(integrate/batch-cu, every fixture dir and the asks) has a zone whose `where` targets an H part, so no committed answer is predicted
to change by it; §8 measures it. The footprint becomes an obstacle for **street** zones `near` or `adjacent` a body too (the same
dependency), not only for FL's.

### 6. Answers, geometry and Steward's flow

- **Classes and codes:** as V's zones. No new reason code. New deviation `what` values: `layout` (§4.1), `outline` (§4.2).
- **Geometry** (additive): `{rect, bell, shared, orientation, unplaced, lots: [...]}` gains `layout` (`ring | spiral | grid |
  organic | street`), `streets` (`[{name, points: [[x, z], ...], closed}]`), `hub` (`{rect, centre}` or absent) and `mask` (row
  runs, only for `around` and `outline`). siteplan/1 is unchanged in format: streets are `road` paths, junctions and the hub are
  `junction` and `plaza` nodes, lots carry a cardinal `front`.
- **Lots in the artifact** are unchanged in shape (`box`, `front`, `entrance`, `fitBox`, `costRange`): plan v1's design within the
  box and C37b's `Entry.cells` pre-check apply as they are. Fronts mix all four cardinals in one zone (Steward's plan v1 designs
  every front since C37's EAST/WEST).
- **`orientation`:** read by `grid` only; noted (`notes: orientation not read by layout ring`) and never refused on ring, spiral
  and organic. Steward's Start re-check sets `ew` with rotate off on its street zones: on a grid that sets the avenues east-west;
  on the others it is noted (S-FL-1).
- **Street keys:** each street is a `road()` item keyed `road:<prefix>street_<name>` (ring `street_ring`, spiral
  `street_spiral`, grid `street_a1`..., organic `street_l1`...), keeping V's `street_` stem (S-FL-5).
- **`KIT_VERSION`** moves (0.39.0), so older approved artifacts answer `PLAN_STALE` and Steward re-checks.

The rest of SETTLEMENTS §9.2's generator library as **plan forms**: giant trees, giant mushrooms, coral, roots and stalactites,
with **M18** (leaf decay) and **M19** (dead coral) from §11, and the **forest-heavy `mega_bench` variant** the 6c close-out
measures. Supersedes the 2026-10-11 draft (now marked superseded where it stands), which predates plan/0, the catalogue, H, KC and CU:
that draft's generators, rules and forest variant stand; its API, its "no Java" and its gate are replaced here. Over the CU/IRR/
VOC-c batch (API 1.37.0, mod 0.40.0, kit 0.38.0, catalogue 9) and, for `around`, FL.

- **Branch:** `slice/F3` (F3-a), then `slice/F3-b`, `slice/F3-c` over `f3/core`; worktrees `../architect-mc-F3*`. **Spend:** $0.
- **Scope:** the generators (§2), their footprint and placement in a plan (§3), M18 and M19 (§4), KC's rows (§5), StillOurs (§6),
  the catalogue and API (§7), byte identity (§8), the forest variant (§10.3), the gate (§10).
- **Not in scope:**
  - **Lots in or on forms:** treehouses, canopy huts, houses inside giant mushrooms (`layout.elevated`, S5: 7b), cave cities (S6:
    7b), `form.hidden_room` (7b). F3's forms are standalone landscape.
  - Coral, kelp or seagrass in **natural** water (the seabed and under-water slice, `form.seabed_site`); kelp and seagrass
    anywhere (kelp grows by random tick into its body's cells; deferred with F2's water scatter).
  - Streets under canopies (§3.2: a canopy's columns are hard); lanterns hung in trees (style, later).
  - `form.scatter` (still reserved `until: F2` although F2 shipped scatter as a region op: a stale entry noted for the coordinator,
    not F3's to flip).
- **Depends on:** F1 (generator rules, `voxels`, `settleForm`), F2 (stamps' block rows), H (bodies), KC (the registry,
  `M25:clear`), CU (`StillOurs`' canonical chains), FL (`around` for forms; F3 builds without it, §11).

### 0. Facts (integrate/batch-cu, 631f89c0)

**F1's rules** (`kit/lib/forms/rules.mjs`): `MAX_PRIMITIVES` 32 per op (:15), `BAKE_OPS` 400 ops per form (:20), `SKIRT` 6 (:21);
`bakeOps` (:84) bakes to one `voxels` op (cond `IF_NATURAL`); `settleForm` (:173) trims ungrounded fragments and adds 45-degree
supports for overhangs over 4. `r.form(id, gen, {stage, bake: 'auto'})` (`program.mjs:880`) records `ir.forms[]` and marks the part
`kind: form`.

**F1 in a plan** (`compile.mjs`): `resolveSpikes` (:589) scans for `count` sites (1..32) skipping water, roughness over 3, sites
closer than 8 and frozen survey columns; `resolveForm` (:956) treats accepted zones and forms as obstacles (gap 2) and re-places
on a clash (`adjusted`); emit (:1138-1170) calls `r.iceSpike`/`r.rockSpire` per site; forms past the claim roll back (`refused
OUT_OF_CLAIM`). In a plan `keepNatural` is a note only (:614). Schema: `form` kinds `ice_spike | rock_spire` (`plan.json:745`).

**The checker** (`check.mjs:23`): RULES M1-M14, M17, M20, M22-M27. **No M18 or M19.** Errors M1, M13, M14, M20, M25, M27:state and
M27:convert. M3 support with `M3:overhang` for forms (limit 4). `vocab/budget.mjs:194-201` approximates leaf reach for
`M27:drift` by **offset** (`LEAF_REACH` 6), not vanilla's path through leaves.

**How the mod writes.** `Sites.FLAGS` = CLIENTS | SUPPRESS_DROPS | SKIP_BE_SIDEEFFECTS (`Sites.java:108`): **no neighbour updates**.
So a written block keeps the exact state the kit wrote (leaves' `distance`, mushroom faces, dripstone `thickness`) until something
next to it changes. **The kit never writes `persistent=true`** today; only the mod's held leaves do (`LeafGuard`, `TileCheck`
stage 4, C31's felling).

**Trees in the survey.** `FLAG_TREE` (`pack.mjs:54`); routes keep 6 off trees (`TREE_REACH`, `route.mjs:39`); `clearTrees` rects
(`program.mjs:289-306`); C31 fells a trunk whole and stops at owned cells.

**Blocks** (`blocks.mjs`): leaves `distance 1..7`, `persistent`, `waterlogged`, class LEAVES; logs and wood `axis`, class LOG;
`mushroom_stem` 6 faces, class LOG; `brown_`/`red_mushroom_block` 6 faces, **class LEAVES**; `pointed_dripstone` `thickness`
(tip_merge, tip, frustum, middle, base) and `vertical_direction`, class PLANT, random-ticked; `dripstone_block` ROCK; `rooted_dirt`
SOIL; `hanging_roots` PLANT (ceiling); `mangrove_roots` waterlogged, no voxel class; live coral plants and fans PLANT,
**waterlogged by default**; live coral blocks ROCK. **No coral row is random-ticked** (coral dies by a scheduled tick), so
`drifts()` never catches it.

**Bodies and coral** (KC as built, `checkFluids.mjs`): `clearScan` (:153) makes any write by another part into a body's hard sets
(cells, ice, shell, lining, grate, spill) an `M25:clear` error, and a water or ice cell holding anything but its fluid **whoever wrote
it**, the body's own part included (:208-212). "Water" is water, a bubble column or any `waterlogged=true` state (`vworld.mjs:49`):
so a waterlogged coral fan written by the body's own part passes, a coral **block** in a water cell fails. M27:state already refuses
`waterlogged=true` outside body cells and natural water.

**The removal.** CU's `StillOurs.holds` treats `distance`, `waterlogged`, `age`, ... as volatile and adds copper's canonical chain;
**mushroom faces, dripstone `thickness` and coral death are not in it**: a live coral block that dies when its pond drains (removal
drains first) fails "same block", so `Regions.remove` would leave it standing as a player's edit.

**Volumes.** `r.needVolume(box)` (`program.mjs:759`) takes the two-plan flow (the first plan returns null); classes AIR, ROCK, SOIL,
LOOSE, ICE, SNOW, WATER, LAVA, LOG, LEAVES, PLANT, ...; T3b's caps (`tunnelGeom.mjs:29`): 4M cells per edge, 16M per plan. Scatter
already finds ceilings (`scatter.mjs:372`: an air cell under a solid one).

**Survival.** Forms carry no BOM (`finish.mjs:106-146`: regions are INSTANT); `cost.rarity` and `cost.creativeOnly` apply to any part.

**What is missing for the close-out.** `kit/regions/mega_bench.mjs` has params `lots` and `scale` only: **no forms or forest
variant** exists; the close-out's `mega_bench A --forms` and its per-tile figures on "F3's forest variant" wait on this slice.

### 1. The rule in one line

**A form is landscape the region owns:** written exactly, kept by its own drift rules, removed exactly, clear of every lot, street and
body, never a write in a lot box, and never a cell that vanilla would change on its own (decay, death, growth) unless the change
is named and still ours.

### 2. The generators

All follow F1's rules (§0): one bounded op per cluster (at most 32 primitives), baked to `voxels` past 400 ops, absolute y with
skirts to 6 under the plan ground, species presets plus a bible's own within the param schema, seeded `fnv64(seed, generator, id)`.

| Generator (block id) | Skeleton | Materials | Drift handled at write |
|---|---|---|---|
| `giantTree` (`form.giant_tree`, F3-a) | trunk `capsuleChain` tapering with height; branches by integer space colonisation toward canopy attractors; buttress roots bending into the ground (its own `roots`, §2.1) | bark (`log`, `axis` from the segment's direction), `wood` core, leaves in noise-holed `ellipsoid` lobes | every leaf `persistent=true`, `distance` written as vanilla would compute it (path through leaves from the tree's own logs, capped 7) |
| `giantMushroom` (`form.giant_mushroom`, F3-b) | stem `capsuleChain`, cap `ellipsoid` cut by `clipY` (flat brown, domed red), gills under | `mushroom_stem`, the cap block, gills | the six faces from the op's own cells (a face is false where the neighbour is the same block), as vanilla's `updateShape` would set them |
| `coral` (`form.coral`, F3-c) | branching `capsuleChain`s and fans on a body's bed | live coral plants, fans and wall fans (waterlogged), sea pickles (waterlogged, 1-4), live coral blocks on the bed only | written only inside a plan body as the body's own cells (§3.4); dead variants never chosen by the generator |
| `roots` (`form.roots`, F3-b) | `capsuleChain`s down a steep face (a bank or cliff) or from a cave ceiling | `rooted_dirt` in the face, `hanging_roots` under it; `mangrove_roots` for the mangrove preset | hanging roots only under a solid cell the form writes or the volume shows |
| `stalactites` (`form.stalactites`, F3-b) | cones from a ceiling and from the floor under it, merged into columns where they meet | `dripstone_block` roots, `pointed_dripstone` with `vertical_direction` and `thickness` from the cone (tip, frustum, middle, base; `tip_merge` where two meet) | never under a root whose block above holds or touches a fluid source (vanilla's growth needs water over the root block), so none grows |

**Presets:** trees oak, spruce, birch, jungle, dark oak, cherry, mangrove, pale oak, and the nether's crimson and warped (stems and
wart blocks, shroomlight: no leaves, no M18); mushrooms brown, red; coral tube, brain, bubble, fire, horn (mixed by default);
roots dirt, mangrove; dripstone small, large. **Sizes:** giant trees 16 to 64 high (default by preset), canopies up to 32 across;
giant mushrooms 8 to 32; stalactites 2 to 16 long.

**2.1 A tree's own roots** are part of the tree's op set (buttresses into the ground, `IF_NATURAL`, at most the skirt's 6 below);
`form.roots` is the standalone form (exposed roots down a bank, hanging roots in a cave).

### 3. In a plan: placement, footprint and the volume

**3.1 Placement** (resolve, as `resolveSpikes` with these changes):
- **Sites:** `count` (giant trees and mushrooms 1..16, coral 1..8 patches, roots and stalactites 1..8 clusters) in the part's
  `where` (`inside`, `near`, `adjacent`, and `around` once FL is in: FL §4.1), never on water, roughness at the trunk or stem base
  at most 3 within its radius + 2.
- **Clear of natural trees:** a giant tree's or mushroom's column footprint grown by **8** holds no natural log or leaf column
  (the survey's `FLAG_TREE`, the volume's LOG/LEAVES/mushroom cells). Our logs never sit within a natural leaf's reach, so no
  natural leaf's `distance` or decay changes because of us (§10 item 5's E-normal depends on it). Natural trees are never felled
  by a form.
- **`inside {part: <zone>}`** (F3's kinds only; F1's unchanged): the zone's **open land**, its rect minus its layout's lots + 1,
  streets and verges, lanes, shared space and props, each grown by 2. A ring's hub (FL §2.3) is such land: the giant oak at the
  centre of a ring.
- **Obstacles** as F1's (accepted zones and forms, gap 2) plus every registered body footprint (§5).

**3.2 The footprint other writers see.** A form's 2.5D footprint for routes, walls, lots and later forms is its **column mask**
(trunk, roots and canopy projected), not its bounds rect: F3 forms register `columns` beside `bounds` in `ir.forms[]`, and
`_routeObstacles`, the wall grid (`OB.OVERLAP`) and `resolveForm` read the mask when it is there (F1's forms have none: unchanged).
- Lot boxes + 1 never meet a form's columns (K5: a canopy over a lot box would be a write in it).
- Streets and paths never pass under a canopy (S-F3-4); walls never under one.
- The mask is the tree's own projection, so a 32-wide canopy does not block a 32 x 32 rect.

**3.3 The cave forms' volume.** `stalactites` and `roots` from a ceiling need a frozen volume over their search box: the `where`
rect x [the ground - 48, the ground]. They take the two-plan flow (`PlanChecks.hasVolume` gains them), within T3b's caps; a plan
past the caps answers `refused VOLUME` as a tunnel does. No ceiling of at least 4 headroom in the box: `refused NO_FEATURE {why:
no ceiling}`. Ceilings are the volume's AIR cells under ROCK, SOIL or LOOSE; floors the solid cells under them (stalagmites).
S-F3-3 asks whether Steward's `load` rule for tunnel plans extends here.

**3.4 Coral is its body's.** `form.coral` must name a plan body: `where: {inside: {part: <form.pond | form.fountain | form.quay |
channel.moat>}}`; anything else answers `refused NO_FEATURE {why: no plan water}` (natural water is the seabed slice's).
- It **compiles into the body**: its cells are a new body set `decor` (the body's own writes, `part` = the body's part), written in
  the fluids stage's body order **after the body's water stands** (bed, then water, then decor), so no live coral ever waits dry for
  its water (vanilla's death tick): coral blocks replace bed cells (shell-grade full blocks, solid to solid), plants, fans, wall fans
  and sea pickles (all waterlogged) replace water cells at least 2 below the surface. Removal: drain, then decor and bed restored.
- **Light under ice:** four waterlogged sea pickles give light 15. In a body with N-H-4's ice cap (a freezing biome) pickles are 1
  per cluster (light 6), and M17 guards the cap; a frozen-site case is in `f3/` (`c01_cold_coral`).
- **H's census and prediction** count a waterlogged decor cell as a source cell (as HY's grate bars are); `predicted` includes
  them. The flow model treats them as sources; the breach as H's.
- KC's registry records `decor` in the body's hard set; `M25:clear`'s water check passes them (waterlogged, the body's own part).
  So coral never needs an exception to KC.

### 4. M18 and M19 (checker, warnings; bars 0 in F3's gate)

- **M18 decay:** every leaf cell a plan part writes is `persistent=true`, **or** lies within 6 of a log by vanilla's rule
  (`distance` propagated through leaves and logs from logs, 6-neighbour). On the virtual world. Findings per part: the cells and
  their distance. F2's stamps (harvested `persistent=false` leaves) are judged by the same rule. M27:drift's offset approximation
  (`budget.mjs`) is left as it is and queued to read M18's rule (kit only).
- **M19 dead coral:** no live coral block without a water cell beside it, and no live coral plant, fan or wall fan that is not
  waterlogged. On the virtual world and on the realised world's dump. Findings per part.
- Both are warnings in RULES (`M18`, `M19`), as the 2026-10-11 draft had them; F3's gate holds them at 0 on every fixture, and the
  6c close-out at 0 on the forest variant.

### 5. KC: every new writer keeps clear

| Writer | Placed (vs H resolve and emit) | KC rule | Refused as |
|---|---|---|---|
| Giant trees, giant mushrooms, roots, stalactites | after H resolve (they resolve with forms, after the bodies' reservations at step 2) | **the later part:** sites keep off every registered footprint grown by 2, and no cell (canopy included) in a hard or watch cell | the form: `adjusted` (fewer, moved) or `NO_ROOM`; never the body. They are **not** added to `EARLY_FORMS` (relief, terrace, spikes keep their row) |
| Coral | inside its body | the body's own cells (`decor`, §3.4): no exception needed | `NO_FEATURE` when no body; `NO_ROOM` when the bed holds no room 2 under the surface |
| Lamps, routes, walls near a form | after | the form's column mask (§3.2) is hard, as forms' bounds are today | as today |

`_unsafe.treeInPond` (a canopy over a pond's water) and `_unsafe.coralOtherPart` (coral written as a separate part's op) are
`M25:clear`'s broken variants; the backstop refuses the tree, never the pond.

### 6. StillOurs: the new blocks' drift (Java)

What vanilla changes on our blocks without anyone placing anything, so that undo, removal, deltas and PT2's counts keep them ours
(CU's rule, extended):
- **Volatile properties** (added to `StillOurs`' list): the six faces of `brown_mushroom_block`, `red_mushroom_block` and
  `mushroom_stem`; `pointed_dripstone`'s `thickness` (`vertical_direction` stays shape-defining). Leaves' `distance` and
  `waterlogged` are volatile already; `persistent` stays compared (a player can't flip it).
- **A coral chain** beside copper's: `Coral.canonical(block)` maps every dead coral block, plant, fan and wall fan to its live
  form, read from vanilla at class load (each live coral block's dead block), never a hand table; a unit test pins it against
  `blocks.mjs`. `holds` compares canonical forms first, so a coral that died in a drained pond is ours.
- **Undo order.** The fluids stage writes the bed, then decor, then water; removal drains, then restores decor and bed (H's
  order). The forms stage writes supports before dependants (logs before leaves, dripstone roots before tips, the face before
  hanging roots); removal is the journal's reverse. With `Sites.FLAGS` no neighbour update runs, so no dependant drops mid-removal;
  the order is still stated so a later flag change can't break it.
- **Refunds** don't apply (forms are instant and free, below). PT's records win first, as CU's §2.3.
- **Survival (binding, Noah):** grown natural forms are free and instant (the RS draft's table, "Noah: grown natural forms are
  free"). F3 keeps that. A giant tree is a lot of wood in a Supplied world (N-F3-1 asks once, with the measured counts).

### 7. Catalogue 11, API and versions

| Block id | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `form.giant_tree` | reserved, until F3 | supported, sinceApi 1.39.0 (placeholder), its own `$defs/form.giant_tree` |
| `form.giant_mushroom`, `form.coral`, `form.roots`, `form.stalactites` | absent | **added** supported (one id per idea, P0's freeze rule), each its own lean def |

- **Defs** (strict, lenient params by S-K1-3): `kind`, `count`, `preset`, `height` (or `size`), `where`, and per kind one member at
  most (`roots: bool` on giant_tree, default by preset; `cover` 0..1 on coral). Unread params are noted. The compact plan/0's
  delta predicted 3,000-4,500 characters, measured (S-FL-8).
- **Coverage:** no catalogue entry says `until: F3` after the slice. Catalogue 10 (FL's) archived as `fixtures/plan/catalogue-fl.json`
  (or catalogue 9 as `catalogue-vocc.json` if F3 merges first); the diff is exactly one flip and four added ids.

ground 62-180 (mean 117.6), biomes frozen peaks 32%, cherry grove 26%, sunflower plains 22%, snowy slopes 11%, river 6%. Its

golden and no monastery bible**. Nothing in kit, tools or mod is named monastery.

**The site drifts, and its own fluids move.** Three worldgen fluids on the claim start after a fresh copy's chunks tick:

  it; when a relief fill covered its feeder (3671-3672, 123, -972), the undo left the falling column dry until `site/FluidRearm`
  (fix/relief-flow, edf879f4) gave restored flowing water a fluid tick. HY-b's run also saw 13 unwritten cells beside the stream
  (grass turned to flowing water) that a re-tick can't undo: no class was added;
- a cave stream (x 3752-3760, y 37-48, z -924..-914) and a lava spring (x 3787-3789, y -2, z -995..-990), 90 and 122 from the
  nearest written cell of voc-natural's plan. `fix/voc-natural` classes these `farfluid` in voc-natural's item 9 only
  (`tools/lib/gate6cvoc-b.mjs` `farFluidOf`: air or non-source fluid on both sides, unwritten, in no lot box, at least 8 Manhattan
  from every written cell; a source and every other kind stay unclassified). `tools/scenarios.mjs` has no `farfluid`;

  T1 as built). S2 held its golden the same way.
