## Phase 6d slice RV: region revisions, the core (DRAFT v2 for Steward review, after GPT-6.1's review)

A standing region can be **revised**: parts added, changed or removed, written as new journal layers over the region's own cells,
undone last-in-first-out, and removed with the region exactly. Every later reader sees the region as revised. The plan/0 path answers a
revision of a realised plan part by part and realises it through `realiseApproved`. This is the outline's "region delta (A5B N7)",
redesigned on the facts in §0. v2 settles what v1 left open (GPT-6.1's review, "Review responses" in the batch summary): the patch is
**changed intent** composed over every writer (§3), the region's **realised record** is kept per tile (§3.1), every `before` is the
world as it stands at the write (§3.4), and the **head**, its transactions and recovery are defined (§4).

**RV changes what `Regions.remove` undoes** (a region's group now holds its revisions), and Steward's history and give-up read
removals. So Steward's RC check comes before release (GATES policy 4's exception), and the verifier re-runs the undo, removal, crash and
accounting items (policy 3).

- **Branch:** `slice/RV`, worktree `../architect-mc-RV` (lanes RV-a, RV-b, RV-c and RV-d, §13). **Spend:** $0, sim and stub only.
- **Scope:**
  - the revision IR, its ids and the part diff (§2);
  - the realised record, the composed intent, the patch and its write (§3);
  - the head, the revision states, transactions and recovery (§4), and the effective IR (§4.5);
  - keep-clear: covered, held, protected, road and unfinished cells (§5);
  - undo and removal in every order (§6), fluids (§7), survival (§8);
  - the plan/0 path (§9), byte identity (§10), the API (§11), product limits (§12) and the gate (§14).
- **Not in scope:**
  - growing a street, and lots on free frontage (GR);
  - changing or removing a standing road, zone, lot box or fluid body (S-RV-6), and writing under a standing lot (S-RV-5);
  - revisions over unfinished tiles or unbuilt survival targets (§5.4, §8);
  - re-planning against changed land (LC's replan, deferred);
  - typed links (7a).
- **Depends on:** 6a (frozen heights, tile items, region undo), 5b (deltas, D5 LIFO, D6 KEEP, the before capture), C36 (artifact pins and
  tombstones), H and IRR (drain-first removal), KC, D3 (the held set, hold columns, `reach`, side joins; RV builds after D3 merges), RS (§8).

### Binding answers carried over

- **5b D3, D5, D6, D7:** a delta is plan against plan; undo is LIFO; a player's edit is kept (`KEEP`) and reported; covered cells refuse
  `COVERED`. RV applies each to regions.
- **5b's before capture** (`SiteDeltas.applyChecked`, `SiteDeltas.java` :1013-1020, from code): the delta entry's `before` is the world
  read at the write boundary (state, block entity, PT record), not the journal's earlier `after`. RV does the same (§3.4).
- **6a D3:** the pre-region heightfield is frozen at first touch; a revision is evaluated against the same frozen heights, and columns
  never touched are frozen at the revision's first touch.
- **6a D7 and phase 6 "invariant (iii) narrowed":** a region never puts CELL over BOX. A revision never writes a cell that a lot, a
  delta, a road, another site or another owner holds above the region's own cells (§5.1).
- **Journal (`journal/Journal.java` :32-44, :258-390, from code):** cells at one position stack by layer; undo takes entries out top-down;
  a cell under one that stays hands its `before` down ("ownership passes down"). A CELL cell restores only if the world still holds its
  `after` under the match. RV relies on both (§6.2).
- **D3, Steward's finding:** `PLACED`, `PARTIAL`, and `FAILED` with cells standing are standing regions; in-flight ones refuse
  `OVERLAP_BUSY`.
- **COMPOSITION §2.7:** "a shipped op's semantics never change". RV checks it per tile against the recorded intent sha (§3.6).

### 0. Facts (main f3f41d43, from code unless marked)

**Why "re-plan, then diff by part id" does not work.** The outline proposed re-running the program and diffing the IRs by part id. On
today's programs that diff is everything:
- **Parts aggregate lots.** A village has one `pads` part holding every lot's pad ops, and one `verges`, `lanes` and `street` part
  (`village.mjs` :541-601). One more lot rewrites all four.
- **The layout is a global search** (`layoutStreet`, :101-138): one more lot can move every lot; the street span follows the outer lots
  (`streetCheck` :320-342), moving `streetY` and every junction's y.
- **Ids are ordinals:** junctions `${rid}_j${k}` (:619-623); plan_v0 zone prefixes `''`, `z2_`, ... (`compile.mjs` :1071).
- **The seed follows the params** (`plan.mjs` :187-191); PlanChecks passes a null seed (`PlanChecks.java` :302).
- So **RV never re-plans the standing parts.** A revision is the standing IR kept byte for byte, plus explicit edits (§2).

**What the IR's tiles are, and what they aren't.**
- `evalTile(ir, key, window, {stage, set})` evaluates **parts** (ops: shape, columns, voxels, relief, scatter, stamp, fluid;
  `realise.mjs` :19). **Ground roads aren't parts:** they are `ir.roads`, compiled to 4e road items and placed as road sites `r<N>`
  (`RegionsImpl.java` :1274-1280, :1405-1412) whose cells come from 4e's road planner at placement. Lots are `ir.lots`, placed as sites.
- Tiles are per stage and per set (terrain, path); realise writes a stage's terrain tiles, then its path tiles, then its roads, then its
  lots (`RegionsImpl.java` :1254-1305), each a new layer over the earlier.

**What realise actually writes differs from the IR's intent.** `TileCheck` (:36-56) checks every intended cell against the live world and
**skips** cells whose condition fails, cells any site, delta, road or other owner holds, cells in a PT build, fluid-gated cells
(`RegionItems.java` :179) and **no-op cells** (the world already holds the state); it **adds** felled worldgen trees and the leaves held
on them (a `leaves` entry). The PLACING entry holds only what passed. Nothing records the skips: the tile entry is the only record. A
`PARTIAL` or `FAILED` region may also have tiles never written.

**What a region is, on disk and in the journal.**
- `<world>/architect-regions/<regionId>/`: `region.json`, `ir.json`, `heights/`, `after/`, `fluids.json` (`RegionStore.java` :14-50,
  `RegionFluids.java` :1662).
- RegionRec stores no tile list and no road ids. Each tile is its own cell site `c<N>` (CELL); roads `r<N>`; lots `s<N>` (BOX); all join
  one ordinary group `g<N>` with a StageRec per stage (`SiteGroupRec.java` :55). **There is no `region:<id>` group.** A journal entry
  names its site, not its group (`Journal.java` :176); membership lives on site records and the group's stage lists.
- `Regions.remove` cancels a running batch, then `Groups.removeGroup` (last placed first), then `finishRemoval`. **The fluid drain runs only
  for a whole-group removal** (`Groups.java` :587: `r.stage == null`); a stage undo drains irrigation only (:590-595).
- Stack depth: `SiteJournal.MAX_DEPTH = 8` (`LAYER_DEPTH`). The kit allows at most 64 stages per IR (`plan.mjs` :31, :421).
- `Sites.remove(lotSiteId)` removes a lot alone (`SitesImpl.java` :214-250); RegionRec keeps it `placed` with a stale site id.

**Plans and artifacts.** `revision {n, parent, parentArtifact, reason}` is in `kit/schemas/plan.json` and read by nothing. Steward
writes no `revision` (steward-mc 6d54540: `parentArtifact` only in its schema copy). `realiseApproved` re-surveys every column of the
artifact's tiles (`PlanChecks.java` :1185-1222).

**Corrections to the old docs.** SETTLEMENTS §14's `SITE_DRIFTED` doesn't exist (`Reason.java` :98-118 has `DRIFTED` only). RV adds no
Reason.

### 1. The rule in one line

**A revision writes only where its intent differs from the parent's intent, composed over every writer in write order, and only where
the parent's write actually stands as recorded; it captures the world as it is at each write, never writes a cell anything else holds,
publishes itself as the region's head in one durable step, and its undo is checked whole before anything moves.**

### 2. The revision IR

#### 2.1 Ids and positions

- **`rid`:** each revision's id, monotonic per region, never reused (`1, 2, 3, ...`; an undone revision's id stays retired). Files live
  under `rev/<rid>/`; part ids use `rv<rid>_`; stages `rv<rid>:<stage>`.
- **`position`:** the revision's place in the head chain (1 for the first revision over the realised plan). After `undoRevision` to
  position `k`, the next accepted revision takes position `k + 1` with a new `rid`.
- **`parent`:** the `rid` (0 for the realised plan) and irSha it was planned on.

#### 2.2 Shape

A revision IR is a full region IR (the effective IR after it) with one added member:

```json
"revision": {
  "rid": 5, "position": 3,
  "base": "<irSha of the realised plan>",
  "parent": {"rid": 4, "irSha": "<sha>"},
  "edits": [
    {"op": "add", "part": "rv5_pond"},
    {"op": "change", "part": "relief_east", "was": "<sha of the part's canonical JSON before>"},
    {"op": "remove", "part": "spire_2", "was": "<sha>"}
  ],
  "lots": {"add": ["inn"], "refill": [{"lot": "bakery", "box": [..]}]},
  "roads": {"add": []},
  "graph": {"nodes": ["lot:inn"], "edges": ["lane_inn"]},
  "dirty": {"<stage>": {"terrain": ["tx,tz"], "path": ["tx,tz"]}},
  "seed": "<fnv64(base seed, rid)>"
}
```

- **Kept parts, lots, roads, paths, anchors, nodes and edges** are byte-identical to the parent's, in the parent's order.
- **Added parts** take the stage they belong to (an existing stage name of the parent, or a new one appended once); within a stage they
  come after every kept part. The IR's stage list grows only when a revision adds a new stage name (§12's limit).
- **Changed parts** keep their id and place; `was` is the parent part's sha (a stale parent fails, `REVISION_PARENT`).
- **Removed parts** are gone. A removed part may not hold a fluid body (§7), a road or a lot's pad under a standing lot.
- **Lots:** added lots are new `ir.lots` entries; `refill` re-activates a lot whose site was removed alone (§4.6). A standing lot's box
  never changes.
- **Roads:** added roads only (4e road items); a standing road is never changed or removed (S-RV-6).
- **Graph:** nodes and edges may be added; a standing node may gain edges. Nothing standing is removed or moved.
- **`dirty`:** the tiles of every added, changed or removed part's op bounds, before and after, plus their 8-column windows.
- **`seed`:** added and changed parts draw from `fnv64(base seed, rid)` keyed by part id.

#### 2.3 Who writes the edits

- **`Regions.planRevision(regionId, RevisionRequest)`** (§11), program `revise` (`kit/regions/revise.mjs`, bundled, deterministic,
  `catalogue = false`): `params.parts: [{op, id, call}]` with `call` one of the region primitives (forms, relief, terrace, carve, pond and
  the plan/0 form kinds), `params.remove: [partId]`, `params.refill: [lotId]`. GR adds `params.grow`.
- **`Regions.checkPlan` of a plan with `revision.parentArtifact`** (§9).
- The standing program never re-runs.

#### 2.4 The kit side (`kit/lib/region/revise.mjs`, RV-a)

`reviseIR(parentIR, edits, ctx)`: checks every `was`; builds added and changed parts against `ctx.standing` (§5.3); assembles the IR,
`dirty`, `tiles`, `budget`, `requires`; runs `check` on the whole revised IR plus **`M29:revision`** (new; error):
- a kept part, lot, road, node or edge differs from the parent's;
- a standing road, lot box or fluid body changed or removed;
- an added or changed part's intent reaches a standing road's cells, a standing lot box plus 1, a held column or a beside region's `reach`
  or hold column (§5);
- an edit names a part that isn't in the parent.
Broken variants, each caught: `_unsafe.rewriteKept`, `_unsafe.underLot`, `_unsafe.ignoreHeld`, `_unsafe.removeRoad`, `_unsafe.overRoad`.

### 3. The patch

#### 3.1 The realised record (new; written by every tile from RV on)

At every region tile's commit (a realise's and a revision's), before its entry goes `ACTIVE`, the mod writes
`<regionId>/realised/<stage>.<set>.<tx>.<tz>.bin` (fsync and rename, as the heights shards):
- the tile's **intent sha** (the sha `evalTile` gave, the artifact's tile sha);
- a **code per intended cell**, in `evalTile`'s cell order: `WRITTEN`, `NOOP` (the world already held it), `HELD` (another entry held it),
  `BUILD` (a PT build), `COND` (its condition failed), `FLUID` (the fluids gate kept it out), `CLIP` (outside the claim or window);
- the **extra cells** the tile wrote beyond its intent (felled trunks, held leaves), as a list of positions.

A tile with no file is **unfinished** (never written, or written by a region realised before RV; §3.7 says how old regions are read).
Roads and lots need no file: their sites' entries are their record.

#### 3.2 The composed intent

For a dirty tile, `I_P(c)` and `I_R(c)` are the parent's and the revision's intended block at `c`, over **every part writer**, in write
order: stages in IR order; within a stage, terrain before path; within a stage and set, `evalTile`'s own op order (kept parts first, then
added). **The last writer in that order wins** (that is what realise's layering leaves standing). Roads and lots are not in the composed
intent; they are protected (§5.2).

The **patch** is the set of cells where `I_P(c) != I_R(c)` (absent counts as a value). Nothing outside the patch is ever written, so a
revision never repairs a kept part's skipped cells, never builds unfinished work, and never touches a road or a later stage's surface it
didn't change.

#### 3.3 Per patch cell

Let `w` be the parent's writer of `I_P(c)` (a tile of stage `s`, set `t`) and `code` its realised code at `c` (§3.1).
- **`I_P(c)` absent, or `code` is `WRITTEN` or `NOOP`, or `c` is an extra cell:** the cell is the region's to change.
  - **target:** `I_R(c)` if the revision writes `c`; else the land before the region at `c`: the `before` of the region's lowest active
    entry at `c` if the region holds `c`, else the world now (a `NOOP` cell the region never journaled).
  - **ownership:** if the region holds `c` and the world isn't its top `after` under StillOurs, the cell is **kept** (a player's or the
    world's change; 5b D6): not written, listed (at most 2,000 listed, the count exact), with PT's record when there is one.
  - **held above:** any active entry above the region's top at `c` that isn't the region's tile, revision or road entry: refuse (§5.1).
- **`code` is `HELD`, `BUILD` or `FLUID`:** the parent never wrote `c` because something else stood there. If it still stands (the
  journal or PT says so), the revision refuses as §5.1; if it has gone, the cell is treated as `I_P(c)` absent.
- **`code` is `COND`:** the cell is treated as `I_P(c)` absent; the revision's own write at `c` is checked with its own condition (the
  same TileCheck path), and fails the same way if it fails.
- **`code` is `CLIP`:** never written.
- **The tile is unfinished:** the revision refuses `NOT_ALLOWED {why: unfinished, tiles}` (§5.4).
- **Write** when `target != world(c)`.

#### 3.4 The write

- **One CELL entry per (revision, dirty tile, set)**, kind `architect:terrain` or `architect:path` (so 6a D8's walk-surface marks see
  revised paths), meta `{rid, region, tile, set}`, its own cell site `c<N>` through `InfraPlace.beginTile`, in the region's group, stage
  `rv<rid>:<stage>`, on a new layer.
- **`before` is captured at the write boundary**, as `SiteDeltas.applyChecked` does: the block state in the world at the tick the entry
  is created, its block-entity data, and its PT record. The ownership predicate (StillOurs) decides only whether a cell is written or kept;
  it never supplies the `before`. So a revision over weathered copper (CU) undoes to that weathered copper, and farmland that became dirt
  undoes to dirt.
- The entry runs the tile path's P1-P8 cycle (6a D4), so a cell that changed between the check and the write is re-checked.
- **Its realised record** is written as §3.1, with the patch's cells only (the code `WRITTEN`, `NOOP` or `KEPT`).
- **Depth:** a written cell whose stack would exceed `MAX_DEPTH` 8 refuses the revision before any write: `LAYER_DEPTH` with the columns
  (at most 16 listed).
- **Added lots and roads** queue in the revision's stages as a realise queues them (roads after the stage's tiles, lots after roads).

#### 3.5 The patch record

`rev/<rid>/patch.json`: per dirty tile and set, the parent's and the revision's intent shas, the patch cell count, the kept count, and the
tile entry id once written. It is written before the revision is accepted (§4.3) and completed as tiles commit.

#### 3.6 The kept-intent check

For each dirty tile, the revising kit's `I_P` (re-evaluated) must hash to the parent's recorded intent sha (§3.1). A difference means the
current kit evaluates a standing op differently (a broken COMPOSITION §2.7 promise): `PLAN_STALE {why: kept_differs, part, tile}`, nothing
written. This compares two kit evaluations, never the world, so skips can't trip it. Expected: never (item 2).

#### 3.7 Regions realised before RV

They have no realised record. On a revision's first touch of such a tile, the mod derives one, read-only: `WRITTEN` where the region's
top entry at `c` holds `I_P(c)` under StillOurs; `NOOP` where the region holds nothing at `c` and the world equals `I_P(c)`; `HELD` where
another entry holds `c`; otherwise `UNKNOWN`. A patch cell at an `UNKNOWN` cell refuses `NOT_ALLOWED {why: unrecorded, cells}` (at most
16): RV never guesses whether the region wrote a cell. The derived record is saved, marked `derived`. The intent sha comes from the
region's own artifact tiles when it has one (plan/0 regions), else from the current kit (and §3.6 then can't catch a drift there: named).

### 4. The head, states, transactions and recovery

#### 4.1 States

| State | Meaning | Head? |
|---|---|---|
| `CANDIDATE` | planned (`planRevision`, or a check's artifact), not realised; any number may exist on one parent | no |
| `ACCEPTED` | its realise has begun: published as the head | yes |
| `PLACING`, `PLACED`, `PARTIAL`, `FAILED` | as a region's | yes |
| `UNDOING` | inside an undo of its suffix | yes, until done |
| `UNDONE` | taken away | no |
| `STALE` | a candidate whose parent is no longer the head | no |

- **The head** is the accepted revision with the highest position (or the realised plan, position 0). **The effective IR** is the
  head's IR. Planning never moves the head.
- **The region's busy state** (`RegionView.busy`: `null`, `revising <rid>`, `undoing [rids]`): while busy, every write-side call on the
  region refuses `OVERLAP_BUSY` (another revision's realise, `undoRevision`, D3 beside plans and realises, C38 offers; `Regions.remove`
  still works as for any placing region: it cancels the revision's batch, then removes the group),
  and the region's state reads `PLACING` while a revision writes (S-RV-10). Reads (`get`, `view`, `landCheck`, checks of other plans) work.

#### 4.2 Competing candidates

Several candidates may name one parent. Realising one **accepts** it by compare-and-set on the head (its parent must equal the head, under
the region's lock); every other candidate on that parent becomes `STALE`, and its realise refuses `PLAN_STALE {why: parent_moved}`
(`planRevision`) or `ARTIFACT_STALE {why: parent_moved}` (`realiseApproved`), nothing written. A candidate is never re-based silently.

#### 4.3 Realise: the durable order

1. **Files:** `rev/<rid>/ir.json` and `rev/<rid>/patch.json` (fsync, rename). A crash here leaves a candidate.
2. **Accept:** under the lock, the head CAS; then `region.json` with the revision `ACCEPTED`, the new head and `busy: revising` in one
   atomic rename. **This is the publication point.** Readers see the new effective IR from here on.
3. **Queue:** the revision's stages are appended to the region's group as StageRecs and its items to the region's batch (the queue
   persists tile keys and the IR hash, 6a D5).
4. **Per tile:** the PLACING entry with its captured befores, the writes, the realised record, then `ACTIVE` (the tile path's crash rules,
   unchanged).
5. **Lots and roads** as a realise's.
6. **End:** the revision `PLACED`, `PARTIAL` or `FAILED` (as a region's rule), `busy` cleared, in one save.
- **Recovery:** at world start, a region with `busy: revising` resumes its queue (as a region resumes); a candidate's orphan files with
  no record are swept after 7 days; a tile entry left `PLACING` rolls back as 4e's (its planned `after`).

#### 4.4 `undoRevision`: preflight, then one operation

```java
default CompletableFuture<RemoveResult> undoRevision(String regionId, int toPosition, String actor)
```

1. **Preflight**, under the lock, over the **whole suffix** (positions `toPosition + 1` .. head), before any write. Any failure refuses the
   call with every reason found, and nothing is written:
   - the region busy, or in flight: `OVERLAP_BUSY`;
   - `toPosition` not below the head: `NOT_ALLOWED`;
   - a lot site added or refilled by a suffix revision covered by a site that isn't the suffix's own: `COVERED`, naming it;
   - a **dependency**: a standing region whose graph targets a node, road or port the suffix added (D3's `<region>:<node>.<port>` ends and
     `<region>:<roadId>` side joins), or whose `reach` or hold cells sit on suffix cells: `NOT_ALLOWED {why: joined, region}` (§6.4);
   - survival: §8's barriers;
   - fluids: §7's precondition.
2. **Begin:** `region.json` with each suffix revision `UNDOING`, `busy: undoing [rids]` and the undo plan (the suffix's sites in removal
   order), one atomic save.
3. **Drain:** the suffix's fluid bodies (§7), recorded per body.
4. **One removal operation** over the suffix's members as one group-stage removal, top position first (`Groups` removal with its persisted
   cursor, unchanged code). The revisions' own lots go in it, with their deltas.
5. **End:** each revision `UNDONE`, the head at `toPosition`, `busy` cleared, the artifacts tombstoned (§9.5), one save.
- **Recovery:** a restart inside 3 or 4 resumes them (the removal resumes as a group removal does, `reconcileRemovals`). A refusal can only
  come from step 1.

#### 4.5 The effective IR: every reader

Every reader of a region's IR reads the head's IR from RV on, and the gate checks each (item 12): `RegionsImpl.view` and `get`/`list`;
the beside data and `besidePorts`; D3's footprint, bodies, held set, `reach` and `architect_mc:land`; plan/0's `standing` and `regions`
inputs and C38's `wall.around {feature: {region}}`; `Drift.checkStage`; previews; `architect_mc:fluids`; C36's pins; and 7a's link pass and
`nav.json` when they land (named for `docs/7a`).

#### 4.6 Lots removed alone, and refills

- `Sites.remove` of a region's lot site marks the lot `removed` (with the old site id and `removedAt`) in RegionRec and `RegionView.lots`.
  Its pad stays the region's.
- **A refill** re-activates that lot id in a revision (`lots.refill`, the same box): its revision record keeps the lot's previous state
  `{state: removed, siteId, removedAt}`; the new site joins the region's group in the revision's lot stage. Undoing the revision removes the
  new site and restores the lot's `removed` state exactly.
- **Placing a lot by hand** (`Sites.place` into a removed lot's box) is not a refill: the site isn't the region's and `Regions.remove`
  doesn't take it. Steward refills through a revision.

### 5. Keep-clear

#### 5.1 Covered and held cells: refuse, never skip

A patch cell whose target differs and which anything other than the region's tile, revision or road entries holds above the region:
- a lot site or its deltas: **`COVERED`**, naming the sites (at most 16) and cells (at most 16, the count exact);
- another site, another owner's region, a beside region's `reach` or hold column, a PT build or a Steward addition: **`OVERLAP`**, naming
  the holder (`PLAYER_BUILD` evidence for a build);
- the owner's C17 area: **`PROTECTED`**.
At plan time (the kit, `M29:revision`, on the held set) and again at realise (the mod, on the journal). Through `realiseApproved` each
answers `ARTIFACT_STALE`. The remedy for a covered lot is to remove it, revise, and refill it (§4.6). The pad delta under a cover stays
deferred (S-RV-5).

#### 5.2 Roads and lots are never patch targets

A standing road's cells (its site's active entry) and a standing lot's box plus 1 are hard to every added or changed part
(`M29:revision`), and the mod refuses any patch cell in them (`OVERLAP {kind: road}` / `COVERED`). A removed part's cells under a standing
road can't occur (the road was placed after the part's tiles and holds the cells above them; the removed part's target there is held, so
§5.1 refuses).

#### 5.3 What the kit keeps off at plan time

`ctx.standing` (sent by the mod, recorded in the revision's sidecar plan directory so it replays offline): the parent's footprint (lots
plus 1, roads plus 1, paths, path-set parts), its bodies' hard and watch sets (KC), `held` (every claim column with an active journal cell
of an entry outside the region's group, D3 §5.1's reader), every beside region's `reach` and hold columns, the owner's C17 areas, and
the parent's unfinished tiles (§5.4). A body a revision adds keeps clear of everything standing (KC: the revision is the later writer).

#### 5.4 Unfinished work

A revision whose dirty tiles include an **unfinished** parent tile (no realised record: never written, a failed tile item, a stage not
reached) refuses `NOT_ALLOWED {why: unfinished, tiles}`. A `PARTIAL` region whose failures are lots only (Steward's usual case) has no
unfinished tile and can be revised; a lot that failed is a lot to remove or refill. The fixture `rv_partial_tile` exercises both.

### 6. Undo and removal

#### 6.1 What undo does

`undoRevision` (§4.4) takes away whole revisions, top first; there is no way to undo a middle revision alone (5b D5). Its own lots go with
it; other sites placed later over its cells don't block it (§6.2).

#### 6.2 Why it is exact, and its stated exceptions

- A revision's cells sit on new layers above every region cell at their positions, and below nothing when written (§5.1 refuses
  otherwise). Each cell's `before` is the world at its write (§3.4).
- **Undone while on top:** each cell restores its `before`, the world just before the revision.
- **Undone after a later site was placed over a cell:** the journal hands the revision's `before` down to that site's cell and the world
  isn't written there; that site's removal later restores it. The journal's rule, unchanged.
- **`Regions.remove` with revisions standing:** the whole group, last placed first (the fluid drain first, H). Every cell ends at the land
  before the region: each revision's `before` at `c` is the world after the layer below it, and the bottom layer's `before` is the land.
- **Exceptions, stated:** a cell a player changed is kept by policy (CELL restores only if the world still holds its `after`), with its PT
  record; and an operation blocked by a dependency, a cover, survival or fluids refuses at preflight, before any write.

#### 6.3 Removal, every order (the gate's rows)

| Case | What happens | Bar (§14) |
|---|---|---|
| **The head undone** | its entries undone | 0 changed cells against the world just before the revision (ARWD over the claim) |
| **Undo to 0 after 5 revisions** | top first, one operation | the world before revision 1, cell for cell |
| **Undo to 1 when revision 3's lot is covered** | refused at preflight (`COVERED` naming the cover), nothing written | hash unchanged |
| **Undo, then a new revision** | the new one gets a new `rid` and the freed position | its files under its own `rid`; undo of it exact |
| **`Regions.remove` with revisions standing** | the group, last placed first | E-flat 0 over the claim against the world before the region |
| **A revision's lot with Steward's `applyDelta`, then undo** | the lot and its delta go in the operation | as the first row |
| **A Steward site over a revision cell, undo, then the site removed** | handed down, then restored | the world before the revision, after both |
| **The same, the site removed first** | the site restores the revision's block; the undo the earlier one | as above |
| **A player's block on a revision cell** | kept, reported, PT intact | the block stands; all else as the first row |
| **Weathered copper under a revision** (CU) | the revision writes over it; its undo restores the weathered state | the exact state before the revision |
| **The region removed while a revision is `PLACING`** | the revision's batch cancelled, then the group removed (today's path for a placing region) | E-flat 0; a save, leave and reopen between |
| **A town revision with a beside district, each removal order** | D3's rows with the revision standing and after its undo | D3 §4.2's bars |

#### 6.4 Dependencies

The region keeps `dependents`: for each standing beside region, the nodes, roads and ports of this region its graph targets (end joins
and side joins) and the columns its `reach` and hold cells cover (from D3's records, refreshed when a beside region is realised or
removed). Preflight refuses an undo whose suffix added any of them. `Regions.remove` of the town is unaffected (D3's `dangling`).

### 7. Fluids

- **Added bodies:** a revision may add bodies (a pond, a fountain, a course). They are written in the revision's fluids stage with H's
  settle and census, and recorded in `fluids.json` with `rid`.
- **Changing or removing a standing body** is refused in 6d (`M29:revision`, `NOT_ALLOWED {why: body}`; S-RV-6).
- **Undo of a suffix with added bodies:** step 3 of §4.4 drains exactly the suffix's bodies before their solids go, by H's drain-first
  protocol scoped to those bodies: their census and escaped cells, their sources, upstream bodies that feed them (HY's closure) if those are
  the suffix's too (a standing body upstream of a suffix body refuses at preflight: `NOT_ALLOWED {why: upstream, body}`). The base region's
  bodies and later holders are untouched.
- **Recovery:** each body's drain state is saved in `fluids.json` (`drained: rid`); a restart resumes the drain. If the removal then can't
  complete, the bodies stay drained and the revision stays `UNDOING`, reported in `RegionView` (as IRR's failure note), and a retried undo
  continues; the sources are rewritten if the undo is abandoned by `Regions.remove` failing (IRR's queued fix applied here).
- `Groups.java` :587's gate gains the suffix case (today it runs only when `r.stage == null`).

### 8. Survival (RS), first version: additive only

- A revision in a survival world builds as RS builds: land free, built blocks construction targets from the owner's stockpile, RS's
  waits, part ids the revision's.
- **Allowed:** patch cells whose current occupant is land (free under RS) or nothing the region wrote. **Refused**
  (`NOT_ALLOWED {why: survival_paid | survival_unfinished}`, at plan and at realise): a patch cell over a paid built block of the region,
  or over an RS target not yet built (RS can report a region `PLACED` while targets remain; those targets are never changed by a
  revision).
- **`undoRevision` in survival:** preflight checks that every suffix revision is still additive (nothing paid or reserved of another
  revision sits under it). Then its unbuilt targets are cancelled first (RS's cancellation, reservations released), its built paid blocks
  are refunded once per key (`rev:<region>:<rid>:<entry>`), and the land comes back free.
- **Whole-region removal:** RS's rule over every entry; since no revision replaced a paid cell, each paid block has one owner and one
  refund.
- The check reports `survival.allowed` per revision.

### 9. The plan/0 path

#### 9.1 A revision of a realised plan

A plan with `revision: {n, parent, parentArtifact}` naming an artifact a standing region was realised from (its own or an accepted
revision's) is checked **as a candidate revision** of that region (§4.1):
- the region is found through C36's artifact record; none, or another owner's: `NO_FEATURE {why: parent}`;
- the parent artifact must be the head's: otherwise every part is answered as usual but the overall state is `NEEDS_REPAIR` with
  `parent_moved` and the head's artifact sha;
- `revision.n` is Steward's own counter, recorded, never compared with `rid` or `position`;
- a plan without `parentArtifact` is today's plan, byte for byte (§10).

#### 9.2 Per-part answers

Parts are matched against the parent artifact's own `plan` member (the plan as checked and approved), and only against parts the parent
**built**: a part in its `dropped` list, or answered `unsupported` or `blocked` there, was never built, so the same id is checked as an
added part (C38's waiting part, asked as a revision). Matching never uses Steward's kept copy (Steward rewrites lot ext and `required` at
Start).

| Part in the revision plan | Answer | Catalogue |
|---|---|---|
| same id, same canonical part JSON as the parent's plan | `fits`, `standing: true`, the parent's geometry, cost 0 | `revision.keep` (supported) |
| a new id, or an id the parent didn't build | checked against the standing region (§5.3): every usual answer | `revision.add` (supported) |
| an id gone, a form or a non-street connector with no body, nothing covering its cells | `removed`, a new answer class, with the cells it frees | `revision.remove` (supported) |
| an id gone, a zone, street, road or body | `refused NOT_ALLOWED {why: remove_zone | remove_road | body}` | — |
| same id, a zone whose `program.lots` only gains lots | `unsupported {block: revision.grow}` until GR | `revision.grow` (reserved, until GR) |
| same id, any other change | `unsupported {block: revision.change}` | `revision.change` (reserved) |

Added parts stay inside the standing claim (S-RV-8). Dependencies may name standing parts (satisfied).

#### 9.3 The revision artifact

`region` gains `revisionOf: {region, parentRid, parentArtifact, parentIrSha}` and `dirty`; `tiles` lists the dirty tiles' intent shas;
`inputs.surveySha` is the dirty windows' survey, `inputs.held` the held set's sha; `$.lots[]` lists added and refilled lots only. The cost
counts the patch.

#### 9.4 `realiseApproved` of a revision artifact

Today's checks, then: the head CAS (§4.2, `ARTIFACT_STALE parent_moved`); the held set over the dirty tiles unchanged (`ARTIFACT_STALE
held`); `terrainDiff` over the dirty tiles only; then §4.3 under the call's opKey. One stale retry under a second key works as for a plan.

#### 9.5 Pins and tombstones (C36)

A revision's artifact is kept while it is the head or below it; `undoRevision` tombstones each undone revision's (unless pinned);
`Regions.remove` tombstones all. A tombstoned or stale artifact can't be a parent.

### 10. Byte identity

- **Unrevised regions, plans without `parentArtifact`, programs without `params.grow`** give today's IRs, tiles and answers (D2's
  kitVersion-only golden rule). Pinned: `scenarios/goldens/*`, plan fixtures `valid/*`, the 59 asks' answers, tile goldens S1, S2, S3, S7
  and mega_bench, D3's pinned set.
- **Journal entries of a plain realise are unchanged;** the realised record (§3.1) is a new file beside them, never inside an entry.
- **Catalogue 12:** `revision.keep`, `revision.add`, `revision.remove` (supported), `revision.grow`, `revision.change` (reserved).
- **`RegionView`** gains trailing `int position`, `@Nullable String busy`, `List<RevisionView> revisions` (old constructors kept).
- **KIT_VERSION** moves; old IRs go `PLAN_STALE` on a new realise as with every kit bump. A region realised under an older kit can be
  revised; §3.6 and §3.7 say what is checked.

### 11. API (binary compatible)

```java
// Regions (defaults throw UnsupportedOperationException; feature "regionRevisions")
default CompletableFuture<RegionPlan> planRevision(String regionId, RevisionRequest r)
default CompletableFuture<RemoveResult> undoRevision(String regionId, int toPosition, String actor)

record RevisionRequest(String program, com.google.gson.JsonObject params, @Nullable String opKey, @Nullable String actor)
record RevisionView(int rid, int position, int parentRid, String planId, String irSha, String state, long createdAt,
    List<String> stages, List<String> lotsAdded, List<String> lotsRefilled, long cells, long kept, @Nullable String artifact,
    boolean survivalAllowed)
```

- `Regions.realise(planId, ...)` of a revision plan realises it; `realiseByKey` finds it. `RegionPlan` gains trailing `revisionOf`.
- **No new Reason, no new event.** Refusals: `COVERED`, `OVERLAP`, `OVERLAP_BUSY`, `PROTECTED`, `LAYER_DEPTH`, `REGION_LIMIT`,
  `NOT_ALLOWED`, `PLAN_STALE`, `ARTIFACT_STALE`. Region events carry revision stages (`rv<rid>:<stage>`).
- **Features:** `regionRevisions`, `planRevisions`; sidecar `region.revise`, `plan.revision`. api-compat clean; apijars on the previous
  three.

### 12. Product limits (bounded settlement lifetime, stated)

No fold in 6d (S-RV-2), so these bound how long a settlement can keep evolving in place:
- **Depth 8 per cell.** A region tile is depth 1 (a D3 contact column already 2, a lot over a pad 2). Each revision that **writes** a cell
  adds one, so one cell can be rewritten at most 7 times (6 in a D3 contact column) in the region's life. Revisions that don't touch a
  cell add nothing there. The 8th rewrite refuses `LAYER_DEPTH`.
- **64 accepted revisions** per region in its head chain (undone ones don't count; `rid` runs to 9,999): `REGION_LIMIT` past it.
- **64 stages per IR** (the kit's limit): a revision adds a stage only when it brings a new stage name, so most revisions add none; the
  group's StageRecs grow by the revision's stages (bounded by the 64 revisions).
- A settlement past a limit can still be removed whole and re-planned. A fold (5b D9's) is the later lever if Steward's worlds reach them.

### 13. Size, split and the shared interface

## Phase 6d slice GR: growing a standing region (D-S2, `growDistrict`) (DRAFT for Steward review)

New lots are added to a standing town or district as a revision (RV): first on free frontage along its standing streets, then on a
street extended from an end that nothing else uses. Standing lots, streets and junctions never move. This is Steward's D-S2 (steward-mc
`docs/DISTRICTS.md` §7: "Lots added to a standing district region (its street extended), so along districts and outposts can grow"),
V's "additions to a realised village", and Noah's Q1 for beside districts ("built at its first accepted building, then grown along
its street"). D3 §11 reserved the feature `growDistrict`, `architect_mc:land.v` 2 and terminal street ends; GR uses all three.

**GR changes what stands in a district's land and what a building's undo takes away**, which Steward's district give-up and history
read. So Steward's RC check comes before release, shared with RV's if they ship together (S-GR-7).

- **Branch:** `slice/GR`, worktree `../architect-mc-GR` (lanes GR-a and GR-b, §10). **Spend:** $0, sim and stub only.
- **Scope:** the growth search (§2), frontage (§3), street extension (§4), along districts (§5), ids and the graph (§6), the land v 2
  (§7), plan/0's `revision.grow` (§8), the API (§9) and the gate (§11).
- **Not in scope:** turning or branching an extension, growth past the claim (a new district, S-RV-8), growth along FL's ring and
  spiral ends (§2.4), re-laying standing lots, a second square.
- **Depends on:** RV (merged first; GR's in-game items need it), D1, D2, D3 (the held set, hold columns, `reach`, `land`), FL (the
  street flag), KC, T2 (routing, for along districts).

### Binding answers carried over

- **RV, all of it:** a growth is a revision: kept parts byte for byte, `rv<n>_` ids, `rv<n>:` stages, the tile delta, LIFO undo, the
  effective IR. A growth is undone by `undoRevision`, one building at a time.
- **D3 §11:** a district's street ends stay terminal junctions in its graph; `land.v` moves to 2 when 6d adds grown parts.
- **D3 S-D3-1:** Steward's own street extensions in a V town are held cells to route around. GR's extensions are Architect's, in the
  region's graph, so later districts may join them.
- **S-FL-5:** every street road a region writes carries `architect_mc:street {zone, district?}` and keeps the `street_` stem.
- **Steward DISTRICTS.md §4:** "a reserved beside district owns its reservation ... and keeps it once built, so its street has room
  to grow"; `District.growable()` is true for `beside` while its street runs east-west, and Steward never routes a building into a
  district that can't grow. GR answers which can.

### 0. Facts (main f3f41d43 plus D3 as frozen, from code unless marked)

- **V's street** spans its outer street lots and the square ±4, clamped to the claim margin 2 (`village.mjs` :320-328), width 5 (road 3
  plus a verge each side), `lotGap` 3 (:23), cut/fill ±3 with steps of 1, no water (:332-340). Its height is the survey at the span's
  midpoint (:341). Lots alternate sides outward from the square (:251, :269).
- **One side free.** D3 measured both of its towns: each street run has lots on one side only; along the lot-free side the verge row
  is held by `path:verges` alone and the row past it holds nothing (D3 §0). So V towns have free frontage on the lot-free side.
- **Ends.** A street end is a `junction` node `${rid}_end` with one non-external edge (`besidePorts`, `districtsEmit.mjs` :146-170);
  its past-end cell faces outward. Junction ids are ordinals along the street (`village.mjs` :619-623), so GR never renumbers them: new
  junctions get new ids (§6).
- **Districts.** A plain district and an outpost have their own V street (`districtsEmit.mjs` :191, prefix `<d>_`, lots `<d>_<k>`
  :78). A following district's street is a T2 route along its band's middle, its lots on both sides with one-cell lanes
  (`followEmit.mjs` :1-4, :142-189); its window is a slice of the traced boundary's spine (:40-50), which the IR doesn't keep.
- **The join.** A district's join leaves from one of its own street ends (`ends.get(d.id)`); a town street end a D3 district joined
  stands under D3's hold cells (stack depth 2 in the contact columns). Neither end may be extended (§4.1).
- **Meta isn't kept.** A region keeps its IR, frozen heights and drift shards (`RegionStore.java` :14-50), not the plan's `meta`
  (village, districts, route). GR reads the effective IR only.

### 1. The rule in one line

**A growth places each new lot on the cheapest free frontage of the standing streets, then on one straight extension from an end
nobody uses, inside the claim, around everything that stands, and never moves a standing cell, lot, street or junction.**

### 2. The growth search (`kit/lib/region/grow.mjs`, GR-a)

#### 2.1 The request

`params.grow` on a revision of a `flat_village`, `districts` or plan_v0 region (the region's own program id; RV's `planRevision`):

```json
"grow": {
  "lots": [{"id": "smithy", "type": "smithy", "size": [9, 11], "villager": true, "ext": {}}],
  "district": "quay",
  "prefer": "frontage",
  "extend": "auto"
}
```

- `lots`: V's `LotSpec` (D1's for a district: a lot list; a count `n` gives `<d>_<k>` ids continuing the district's numbering).
- `district`: which district of a districts region grows (required there; absent for a town).
- `prefer`: `frontage` (default: free frontage first, then extension) or `extend` (extension first).
- `extend`: `auto` (the cheapest extendable end), an end node id, or `none` (frontage only).

#### 2.2 Order and choice

1. **Specs** in V's order (`orderOf`: central, landmark, the rest, edge; then input order). A `central` or `landmark` lot in a growth
   takes the best frontage slot nearest the square (or the district's shared space), never displacing a standing lot.
2. **Frontage slots** (§3), cheapest first: nearest the square along the street, then the lot-free side before a gap between lots,
   then by street id and `u`.
3. **Then one extension** (§4), if lots remain and `extend` allows.
4. **A lot that fits nowhere** is listed in `unplaced` with its reason (`NO_ROOM {kind: frontage | street | claim | held | body}`),
   as V lists them. A growth with no lot placed fails `NO_ROOM` and plans nothing.
- The search is deterministic over the effective IR, the frozen heights, the held set and the revision seed (RV §2.1).

#### 2.3 Obstacles

Everything RV §5.2 lists, plus: every standing lot box plus its apron (`lotGap` 3 to a new lot), every standing lane, prop, lamp and
square cell, every beside region's `reach` and hold columns, and a beside district's land (D3's `land.union`) when the town grows.
A town's growth never takes a district's land; a district's growth never takes town land except its own join's cells (it doesn't write
them, §4.1).

#### 2.4 Which streets grow

| Region kind | Frontage | Extension |
|---|---|---|
| V town (`flat_village`, plan_v0 street zone) | yes | yes |
| plain district, outpost (their V street) | yes | yes, from the end that isn't the join's |
| along district (a following street) | yes, both sides | along the boundary (§5) |
| FL grid (blocks of V streets) | yes | yes, from a block street's outer end |
| FL ring, spiral, organic | yes, on straight runs of at least 9 | no (`NO_ROOM {kind: layout}`; S-GR-4) |

### 3. Frontage

On a straight street run along axis `a`, centre line `v = c`, side `s` (±1), the street's footprint is `|v - c| <= 2`:
- **The lot:** its front edge on `v = c + s (2 + 1 + L)`, where `L` is the lane length (V's: the lot's apron row then the lane, at
  least 1), facing the street. Its box plus 1 misses every obstacle (§2.3) and is at least `lotGap` from every standing lot box.
- **The lane:** from the lot's entrance to the verge, as V's lanes, ending at the verge row `c + 2s`; it **never writes** a verge or
  road cell (D3 §3.2's verge contact: the verge cell it meets is held by the street's road or verge only).
- **The pad:** V's pad ops (`surfaceOps`, `PAD_MAX` 2) on the frozen heights; its batter must not reach a held column or a standing
  lot box plus 1.
- **Junction:** a new junction node on the street at the lane's foot (§6).
- **Lamps:** the town's lamp rule for the new lot's apron (W), skipping spots within 6 of a standing lamp (N-D3-2's rule).
- Slots are tried every 2 cells along each run, from the square outward.

### 4. Extension

#### 4.1 Which ends can be extended

An end node is extendable when all hold:
- it is a terminal junction of a street (`architect_mc:street`, or the `street_` stem before FL) with exactly one edge in the region's
  graph, and that edge is the street's own;
- no join, route, lane, external edge or D3 junction meets it (not the district's join end; not a town end a district joined);
- its past-end cell and the 3 cells past it, 5 wide, hold no cell of another entry (no D3 hold cell, no site, no PT build);
- its past-end cell lies at least 9 cells inside the claim margin along the street's axis (room for one lot).

#### 4.2 The new street

- **Straight**, continuing the street's line from the past-end cell, the street's width (road 3 plus verges) and its look: the same
  road blocks, verges and W's lanterns (`lanterns: true` when the standing road has it) (N-GR-1).
- **Length:** the lots it carries, sides alternating as V's `tryStreet` (outward from the old end), plus 4 past the last lot, clamped
  to the claim margin 2. At most one extension per growth.
- **Grade:** V's street check per cell (cut/fill ±3, steps of 1, no water) against the frozen heights. The extension's height starts at
  the end node's y and may step by 1 per 4 cells (V's road rule); a run that can't meet it ends where it fails, and the lots that don't
  fit are `unplaced` (`NO_ROOM {kind: street}`).
- **The road:** a new 4e road item `<roadId>_g<n>` (`street_e_g2`), flag `architect_mc:street {zone, district?}`, joined end to end
  with the standing road at the past-end cell (4e's handover; the standing road is never rewritten).
- **The verges and lanes** as new parts (§6). The standing `verges` part is unchanged; the new verges start at the past-end cell.
- **Lots** on both sides of the extension, V's placement on its run.

### 5. Along districts (GR-b)

A following district's street is a route on its boundary line. Its growth:
- **Frontage:** new lots on both sides of the standing route where free (§3's rule with `FOLLOW_SETBACK` 3 and `FOLLOW_PAD` 6, the
  district's own lot geometry, `followEmit.mjs` :142-189).
- **Extension:** the boundary is traced again (`traceBoundary`, the same `follow` and side) over a fresh survey of the claim (loaded
  chunks, resolution 1, recorded with the revision's inputs as RV §5.2's files) from the standing route's free end along the spine,
  outside the standing band. The new band continues the standing mask; its street is a T2 route from the end node along the new
  band's middle, and its lots are placed as D2's.
- **Its mask grows:** `meta.districts.follow[id].mask` isn't kept, so the revision records the new band's mask as its own
  (`revision.follow {district, mask}`), and `land` reads it (§7).
- **Where the boundary ends** inside the claim, or turns back into the band: `NO_ROOM {kind: boundary}` for the rest.
- An outpost grows on its own V street (§3, §4); its corridor (`architect_mc:corridor`) doesn't change.

### 6. Ids, parts and the graph

- **Parts:** `rv<n>_pads`, `rv<n>_lanes`, `rv<n>_props` and, for an extension, `rv<n>_verges` and `rv<n>_street` (for a district:
  `rv<n>_<d>_pads` and so on), in `rv<n>:` stages after the parent's.
- **Lots:** the caller's ids, unique across the region (M14).
- **Joined nodes (an RV §6.1 refusal):** a revision that added a node a beside region's `join_external` now targets can't be undone while that
  region stands: `undoRevision` refuses `NOT_ALLOWED {why: joined, region}`. The town's removal is unaffected (D3's `dangling`).
- **Roads:** `<roadId>_g<n>`.
- **Graph:**
  - frontage: a new junction `<roadId>_g<n>_j<k>` on the street at each lane's foot, splitting no standing edge: the junction is
    recorded with `on: <roadId>` and `u` (as D3's side junction, so the standing edge isn't re-cut), plus the lane edge and the lot node;
  - extension: a new edge from the standing end node to the new end node `<roadId>_g<n>_end`, the extension's junctions, lanes and lot
    nodes. The standing end node gains one edge and stops being terminal; the new end is terminal, so a later district (D3) or a later
    growth can use it.
- **Byte identity:** a program run without `params.grow` is unchanged (item 2); a growth's kept parts are RV's (byte for byte, checked
  per tile, RV §3.4). `KIT_VERSION` moves.
- **The town's square and bell** are unchanged; M22, M23 and M24 are judged on the whole revised IR (a new trading hall must sit
  within 12 of the bell, or it is placed where it is and M23 warns as today).

### 7. The land: `architect_mc:land` v 2

For a districts region (D3 §6), `v` becomes 2 at the first growth:
- each grown lot and street is a new `parts[]` entry `{kind: "grown", id: "rv<n>", district, revision: n, runs, rect, cells,
  insideCells}`; an along district's new band is `{kind: "district", id, shape: "mask", revision: n, ...}`;
- `union`, `outside` and `inside` are recomputed from all parts (D3's rules), so `outside` holds the grown land Steward now owns;
- `undoRevision` recomputes `land` (the revision's parts leave; `v` stays 2);
- every part carries `revision` (0 for the realised plan's parts), so a reader can tell which building took which land.
- A V town gains no `land` key (D3 gives it none); its growth stays inside its claim.

### 8. plan/0: `revision.grow`

In a revision plan (RV §9), a zone with the same id whose `program.lots` only gains lots (every standing lot spec equal, in any order;
no other member changed) is a growth:
- the added lots are checked by §2 with the zone's own streets, and each gets its usual answer (`fits` with geometry, `refused
  NO_ROOM` with `wouldFit` where a smaller size fits, or listed `unplaced` with the zone's other answers);
- the zone answers `fits` with `standing: true` and `grown: [lot ids]`;
- catalogue: `revision.grow` reserved -> supported (catalogue 13).
- A districts zone (`program.districts`) gaining lots in one district grows that district.

- **Placeholders:** API **1.44.0**, mod **0.47.0**, kit **0.45.0**, catalogue **13**.

## Phase 6d slice FS: updates follow the source (DRAFT for Steward review)

When a source design gets a new version, each of its copies can be re-made from that version by its own recipe, at $0, and then each
lot that stands at the old copy is updated by the existing delta path. This is 0b's deferral ("a source's new version applied to its
COPY and SITE followers, by recipe"; CONTRACT 0b §2.4: "That is 6d's update path, so there's no migration") and Steward round 3's
"updates follow the source" ("a new version of a source design is offered to its variants and site-adapted copies as one update,
applied per lot, keeping each lot's adaptation").

FS uses only existing placement paths (`outdated`, `checkDelta`, `applyDelta`, `revert`), so it needs no RC (GATES policy 4); the
verifier re-runs the delta and revert items (policy 3).

- **Branch:** `slice/FS`, worktree `../architect-mc-FS`. **Spend:** $0 (no Claude call: a recipe is deterministic kit work).
- **Scope:** `Library.followers`, `Designs.follow` and `followAll`, the sidecar's follow job, the copy's next version, and the per-lot
  update through the existing delta path; region lots included.
- **Not in scope:** SITE followers (7b's `fitToSite` adaptations: `follow` of a SITE entry answers `NOT_ALLOWED {why: until_7b}`);
  VARIANT and RESKIN entries (they don't follow, 0b §2.4); copies of an adopted entry (PT2's N-PT2-2: its own ask); applying deltas
  automatically.
- **Depends on:** 0b (copies, `Derivation`), 5b (deltas), C13 (`versionOf`), PT2 (adopted entries refuse), RV only for item 6's region.

### 0. Facts (main f3f41d43, from code)

- `Library.Derivation(source, sourceVersion, Kind {VARIANT, RESKIN, COPY, SITE}, recipe)` (`Library.java` :281-299); its javadoc says
  "Only COPY and SITE follow their source (6d)".
- A COPY's recipe is written by `variants.ts` :624 (`recipeRecord` :47-49): `{shift, param, values, mirror, roles, bible, group,
  itemKey, archetype, ordinal, attempt, levers?, changed?, bar?}`. It is chosen by `kit/tools/copy-recipe.mjs` (`chooseRecipe` in
  `lib/variation.mjs`), up to `COPY_RECIPES` 3 attempts (`variants.ts` :365, :582).
- **Nothing re-applies a recipe to a later source version.** The only reader of `derivation.recipe` is `checkChangeable`, which refuses
  `versionOf` and polish of a COPY (`VERSION_REFUSED copy`, `versions.ts` :188-192).
- New versions carry `derivation` forward (`polish.ts` :969, `sidecar.ts` :1009).
- `Sites.outdated` lists standing sites whose pinned version is below their entry's head (`SiteDeltas.java` :1499-1512), building sites
  only, region lots included (RV §0).
- Deltas refuse a frame change (5b D2, `FRAME_CHANGED`).

### 1. The rule in one line

**A copy follows its source by re-running its own recorded recipe on the source's new version, exactly, and becomes its own next
version only if that result still passes everything a copy had to pass; each lot then updates by the ordinary delta.**

### 2. Followers

```java
// Library (default throws; feature "followSource")
default List<Follower> followers(String sourceEntryId)
record Follower(String entryId, Library.Derivation.Kind kind, int sourceVersion, int headVersion, int sourceHead, boolean behind)
```

- Every entry whose head's `derivation.source` is the source, any kind, with `behind` true for a COPY whose `sourceVersion` is below
  the source's head. VARIANT and RESKIN are listed (never `behind`), so a caller sees the family.

### 3. Following

```java
// Designs (defaults throw; feature "followSource")
default CompletableFuture<FollowResult> follow(String copyEntryId, int toSourceVersion /* 0 = head */, @Nullable String opKey)
default CompletableFuture<List<FollowResult>> followAll(String sourceEntryId, int toSourceVersion, @Nullable String opKey)
record FollowResult(String entryId, boolean followed, int fromVersion, int newVersion, int sourceVersion,
    @Nullable String refused /* null | frame | check | bar | fit | bible_gone | source_gone */, String message)
```

- **The job** (sidecar `entry.follow`): load the source at `toSourceVersion`, apply the copy's recipe exactly (its `shift`, `param`,
  `values`, `mirror`, `roles` and bible pin; `attempt` fixed, no new choice), build the copy, then:
  - the pristine-kit check (as `VariantRunner` runs it for every copy);
  - the 0b variation bar against the source's new version (2 of 3 levers, at least 10% of cells changed), so a follower is still a
    copy and not the source;
  - the frame: front and the entrance's feet row equal to the copy's head (else `frame`: its lots couldn't take the delta);
  - the copy's own size bounds (the archetype's `max`, the lot's fit box if the group recorded one: `fit`).
- **Installed** as the copy's head + 1, `by: 'follow'`, `derivation.sourceVersion` = the new source version, recipe unchanged;
  `ENTRY_VERSIONED` fires as for any version.
- **Refused** (any check failing): nothing installs; `FollowResult.refused` names why; the copy stays at its version. No fallback
  design is made (N-FS-1).
- **opKey:** the same key and request return the same result; `followAll` keys each follower `<key>:<entryId>`.
- `versionOf` and polish of a COPY stay refused (`VERSION_REFUSED copy`): following is how a copy changes.
- An entry whose source is gone (deleted, never GC'd while pinned) refuses `source_gone`.

### 4. The lots

Nothing new. The caller lists `Sites.outdated()` (the followed copies' lots now show `headVersion` above their pin) and runs
`checkDelta` then `applyDelta` per lot, keeping the player's edits (`KEEP`) as 5b. Each lot's own adaptation is its copy's recipe,
so "keeping each lot's adaptation" holds by construction. A region's lot updates as any lot (RV §0); a lot under a revision's cells is
unaffected (a lot is BOX above its pads).

- **Survival:** a construction delta (5b D8, Y1's stockpile), unchanged.
- **Revert:** `Sites.revert(siteId, oldVersion)` as 5b (LIFO; in survival a paid forward delta).

### 5. Byte identity, KC and Steward's asks

- **Byte identity:** no IR, tile, plan answer or blueprint changes for anything not followed; a followed copy's blocks equal a fresh
  copy made by the same recipe from the new source version (item 1). Kit unchanged, so no `PLAN_STALE`.
- **KC:** FS adds no region writer; a lot's delta stays inside its lot box (5b), which bodies already keep clear of (H's `M25:keep`).
- **Steward's asks:** round 3's "updates follow the source" is answered for COPY (C1's copies); SITE waits for 7b. The 59 asks are
  unaffected (no plan path changes).

### 6. Gate (slice tier, $0)

| # | Check | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Unit (sidecar, kit) | the follow job on the bundled cabin and tavern sources: a recipe re-applied to v2 gives the same blocks as a fresh copy made with that recipe from v2 (byte-identical NBT); each refusal (frame, check, bar, fit, source_gone); opKey replay |
| 2 | Followers | a group with an archetype and 3 copies, plus a VARIANT: `followers` lists 4; `behind` true for the 3 copies after the source's `versionOf` (stub) |
| 3 | followAll | the 3 copies followed: 3 new versions, each passing the check and the bar; `ENTRY_VERSIONED` 3 times |
| 4 | Lots (verifier re-runs) | the 3 copies placed as lots of a `flat_village` realised through `checkPlan` then `realiseApproved` (Steward's plan v1 shape); `outdated` lists them; `applyDelta` on each, a player's block on one lot kept (`KEEP`); `revert` of each to the old version: the world before the delta, cell for cell |
| 5 | Refused | a source v3 with a moved front: every follower `frame`, nothing installed, lots unchanged |
| 6 | With RV | one lot's site removed alone (RV §4.4), the region revised to re-add it at the new copy version; then `Regions.remove`: E-flat 0 |
| 7 | Unchanged, API, spend | 0b's copy units, 5b's delta suite, pt2-ingame's adopt items; api-compat clean; apijars; $0.00 |

**Tier:** slice plus `sidecar/**` and `api/**`: the units, apijars, 5b-deltas; FS's own `fs-unit`, `fs-ingame` (driver
`tools/gate6dfs.mjs`). The verifier re-runs item 4.

**Size:** 2-2.5 days, one builder (the sidecar job 1 day; the Java surface and api-compat 0.5; the gate 1).

**Placeholders:** API **1.45.0**, mod **0.48.0**, kit unchanged (the recipe tool is reused as is), catalogue unchanged.

### Open questions for Steward

- **S-FS-1. Who triggers.** Steward calls `followAll` after it hears `ENTRY_VERSIONED` on a source (or finds a `behind` follower at
  world load), shows "3 buildings can take the new design", and applies per lot. Architect never applies by itself. Default: yes.
- **S-FS-2. All or some.** `followAll` follows every copy; a copy that fails is listed and left. Do you want `follow` per copy only?
  Default: both.
- **S-FS-3. Variants.** VARIANT and RESKIN entries never follow (they were made to differ). Fine? Default: yes.
- **S-FS-4. SITE copies.** 7b's site-adapted entries follow in 7b, with their fit parameters. Until then `NOT_ALLOWED until_7b`.
  Default: yes.

### Open questions for Noah

- **N-FS-1. When a copy can't follow.** Proposed: it stays at its version, says why, and nothing is spent. The alternative designs a
  fresh copy with Claude (paid). Default: stays, $0.

### Deferred

- SITE followers (7b). Copies of an adopted entry (PT2's N-PT2-2, its own ask). Automatic application.

### Coordinator decisions (2026-10-20, on Noah's behalf)

- **N-FS-1:** a copy that can't follow stays as it is, at $0, with no paid redesign.


## Phase 6d slice LC: land change in a standing region (DRAFT for Steward review)

A standing region can say what has changed in it since it was built, part by part and lot by lot, with the player's cells apart. And a
region held `DRIFTED` before a later stage can re-plan just the stages not yet placed, keeping everything placed. This is
SETTLEMENTS §14 ("incremental replanning on land change"), PT's S-PT-1 ("to 6d with replanning on land change"), and §14's "drift at
realise ... offer replan affected stages".

LC adds a read-only report and an opt-in call on a waiting region; it changes no removal, so no RC (GATES policy 4).

- **Branch:** `slice/LC`, worktree `../architect-mc-LC`. **Spend:** $0.
- **Scope:** `Regions.landCheck` (§2), `Regions.replanStages` (§3), the stage wait's action, and wiring T2's route hysteresis
  (`routePrefer`) through the mod for the first time.
- **Not in scope:** SETTLEMENTS §14's incremental passes over dirty tiles with old fields as boundary conditions (a kit rewrite of
  every pass; later, if a measured need appears, S-LC-3); re-fitting damaged buildings (C13's `versionOf` does that); repairing damage
  automatically.
- **Depends on:** RV (the effective IR, revisions as the repair path), PT (player records), CU and F3's StillOurs rows, T2.

### 0. Facts (main f3f41d43, from code)

- `Drift.check` at realise and `Drift.checkStage` before each later stage (`Drift.java` :17-36, :56+): a failed stage shows as
  `drift["held: ..."]`, surfaced as `waiting = DRIFTED` (`RegionsImpl.java` :1852-1857). There is no `SITE_DRIFTED` reason
  (SETTLEMENTS §14 names one; it doesn't exist).
- Frozen heights exist only for columns a written tile touched (6a D3); unplaced stages' tiles may have none.
- `ctx.routePrefer` (T2's hysteresis: cells of an earlier route cost a third, `route.mjs` :328-340, `program.mjs` :360-371) is set only
  by gate tools (`gate6ct2.mjs`, `scenario-route.mjs`); the mod and sidecar never pass it.
- PT keeps who placed a cell per chunk (`Placed`, `Sites.playerPlaced`), and the journal keeps a `Pt` per cell (`journal/Pt.java`).

### 1. The rule in one line

**A land check reads, never writes; a stage re-plan changes only stages that have written nothing, and refuses if any placed part
would come out different.**

### 2. `landCheck`

```java
// Regions (default throws; feature "landCheck")
default CompletableFuture<LandReport> landCheck(String regionId, @Nullable String part /* null: every part */)
record LandReport(String region, int revision, List<PartLand> parts, List<LotLand> lots, long cellsChecked, long ms)
record PartLand(String part, long cells, long changed, long player, long natural, Map<String, Long> kinds, List<BlockPos> sample)
record LotLand(String lot, String siteId, String state, double standing /* Reconcile's score */, long changed, long player)
```

- For each cell the region holds on top (tile, revision and road entries): the world against the entry's `after` (StillOurs, with CU's
  and F3's rows). Changed cells are split by PT's record: `player` (a player placed what's there), `natural` (air, fluid, leaves, snow,
  grown plants: the volatile kinds), else counted by block kind in `kinds`.
- Lots: each lot site's `Reconcile` standing score (`STANDING` 0.8, `RESTORED` 0.9, as world start) and its changed and player cells.
- Bounded: at most 4M cells per call, over ticks at the queue's budget (recorded); a larger region answers per part.
- $0, read-only, no ticket (unloaded chunks are counted `unloaded`, not loaded).
- **Use:** Steward shows "the east field was dug up (120 cells, by players)"; a repair is a revision (RV) or a lot delta (5b).

### 3. `replanStages`

```java
// Regions (default throws; feature "replanStages")
default CompletableFuture<RegionPlan> replanStages(String regionId, @Nullable String opKey)
```

- **When:** the region is `PLACING`, waiting `DRIFTED` at a stage gate (no tile of that stage or later written), or `PARTIAL` with
  stages never started.
- **What runs:** the region's program again with its **recorded** params and seed (the ones its plan ran with, kept in the sidecar's
  plan directory; for plan_v0 regions that includes the `regions`, `builds`, `protected.areas` and `standing` inputs as they were),
  over the claim, with the new land and the held set passed as separate inputs:
  - the frozen heights where they exist (placed tiles' windows), and a fresh resolution-1 survey elsewhere (loaded chunks);
  - `ctx.routePrefer` from the effective IR's route and road cells (T2's hysteresis), so routes stay where they were where the land
    allows;
  - the held set as obstacles (RV §5.2).
- **The acceptance rule:** every part, lot, road, node and edge of the **placed** stages comes out byte-identical. If any differs, the
  call refuses `DRIFTED {why: placed_parts_changed, parts}` and nothing changes (the region keeps waiting; the caller may `force` as
  today, or remove it).
- **When accepted:** the region's IR for the unplaced stages is replaced by the new one (a revision `n` with `kind: replan`, RV §4.1,
  writing nothing until its stages run; the one revision allowed while the region is `PLACING`, since it touches only stages that
  haven't started), `Drift.checkStage` re-baselines, and the queue continues. Undo and removal are RV's.
- Through `realiseApproved`: a region realised from an artifact gets a new artifact for the replan (`revisionOf`, RV §9.3), so
  Steward approves the changed stages before they run (S-LC-2).

### 4. Byte identity, KC and Steward's asks

- **Byte identity:** a region that never calls `replanStages` is unchanged; a replan keeps every placed part byte for byte (§3's
  rule). Plain plans don't get `routePrefer` (only `replanStages` passes it), so no plan answer moves. Kit unchanged.
- **KC:** the replanned stages are the region's own program; its bodies keep clear as at plan time, and the held set is hard.
- **World classes:** item 3's natural twin classes E-normal by D2's narrowed classes at unwritten cells only (no new class).
- **Steward's asks:** S-PT-1 ("C17 areas are enough until 6d's replanning") is answered by the report plus the stage replan; plan
  v1's stale retry is unchanged. The 59 asks are unaffected.

### 5. Gate (slice tier, $0)

| # | Check | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Unit | the classification (player, natural, kinds) on a synthetic journal; the acceptance rule on synthetic IRs (a placed part changed: refused) |
| 2 | Land check | `rv_town` (RV's fixture): a player digs 40 cells of the square and places 12 blocks on a lane; a creeper-like removal of 20 pad cells (DevBridge); `landCheck` reports each part's counts exactly (against a driver-side diff); 0 cells written (hash) |
| 3 | Replan, accepted | a 3-stage region whose stage 3's tiles are dug by the driver while stage 2 places: `DRIFTED` at stage 3's gate; `replanStages` accepted; stage 3 placed against the new land; then `Regions.remove`: E-flat 0 (verifier re-runs) |
| 4 | Replan, refused | the same, with stage 2's ground changed too: refused `placed_parts_changed`, nothing changed |
| 5 | Steward's shape | the plan v1 path: a region from `realiseApproved` held `DRIFTED`; `replanStages` gives a revision artifact; `realiseApproved` of it continues |
| 6 | Unchanged, API, spend | rv-ingame, 6a drift items; api-compat; apijars; $0.00 |

**Size:** 2.5-3 days, one builder. **Placeholders:** API **1.46.0**, mod **0.49.0**, kit unchanged (the kit already takes
`routePrefer`), catalogue unchanged.

### Open questions for Steward

- **S-LC-1. The report's grain.** Per part and per lot, with player cells apart and a sample of positions (at most 16). Enough for the
  card, or do you need cell lists? Default: counts and samples.
- **S-LC-2. Approving a replan.** A replanned region from an approved artifact gets a new artifact, and its changed stages wait for
  `realiseApproved` of it. Or should a replan whose changed parts are only terrain under no lot continue without a new approval?
  Default: a new approval.
- **S-LC-4. How often a replan is accepted.** Predicted low for layout-searched programs (V's street search and plan_v0's zone search
  read the whole survey, so new land near any placed part can move it), higher for terrain-only stages. The builder records the rate
  on item 3's fixture and on 20 synthetic drifts. Is a mostly-refusing replan still worth shipping, or should LC ship the report only?
  Default: ship both; the refusal names the parts, which is useful by itself.
- **S-LC-3. Incremental passes.** SETTLEMENTS §14's dirty-tile passes (fields re-run over changed tiles with old values as boundaries)
  are not in LC: the stage replan re-runs the program whole and accepts only if placed parts are unchanged. Is that enough for your
  phase 3? Default: yes, until a measured case needs more.

### Open questions for Noah

- **N-LC-1. Damage in the card.** Proposed: Architect reports damage only when asked (`landCheck`), and Steward decides whether to
  mention it. The alternative is an event per damaged part. Default: on request only.

### Coordinator decisions (2026-10-20, on Noah's behalf)

## Phase 6d slice AD: adopting a VillageLayout settlement as a region, the 6d half of C12 (DRAFT for Steward review)

An existing Steward settlement built by VillageLayout (its own street road and lot sites, placed before regions) becomes a region
record **without writing a cell**, so it can grow (GR), revise (RV) and be removed as one region. This is the 6d half of the C12 joint
7a/6d gate (CONTRACT V §10: "The joint 7a/6d gate adds `Regions.adopt` ... then the gate runs a 6d addition (a lot, or the square), a
6d `applyDelta` on one lot, and one exact `Regions.remove` of everything"). The 7a half (the link pass and `nav.json` over adopted lots)
is drafted on `docs/7a`; the two meet at the adopted region's effective IR (§2) and the joint gate's last row (§4).

AD moves Steward's standing sites into a region's group, which Steward's history and migration read: **RC check** before release.

- **Branch:** `slice/AD`, worktree `../architect-mc-AD`. **Spend:** $0.
- **Scope:** `Regions.adopt` (§2), the synthesized IR (§2.2), group membership (§2.3), un-adopt (§3), the gate's 6d rows (§4).
- **Not in scope:** the link pass, `nav.json` and typed links (7a); Steward deleting VillageLayout (after the joint gate and region
  survival, C12); adopting another owner's sites; adopting road networks that aren't one straight street.
- **Depends on:** RV, GR, PT2 (its adopt patterns: an entry with before == after), V (the `street` layout geometry, CONTRACT V §10).

### 0. Facts (main f3f41d43, from code)

- `Sites.adopt` adopts a player's build as a site (PT2, `Adopt.java`), writing one `adopt` journal entry with before == after; it has
  no region references. There is no `Regions.adopt`.
- A V region's lots are sites `s<N>` and its street a road site `r<N>` in one group `g<N>` (RV §0); VillageLayout's are the same kinds
  of sites in Steward's batches' groups.
- V's `street` layout is VillageLayout's geometry; `kit/REGIONS.md` records the mapping (CONTRACT V §10).

### 1. The rule in one line

**Adoption writes no block and no journal cell; it records which standing sites a region is made of and an IR that describes them,
and from then on the region's revisions and removal treat them as its own.**

### 2. `Regions.adopt`

```java
// Regions (default throws; feature "regionAdopt")
default CompletableFuture<RegionView> adopt(AdoptRegionRequest r)
record AdoptRegionRequest(String owner, ResourceKey<Level> dimension, BoundingBox claim, String layout /* "village_layout" */,
    com.google.gson.JsonObject geometry /* {streetZ, xLo, xHi} or {streetX, zLo, zHi} */, List<String> roadSiteIds,
    Map<String, String> lots /* lotId -> siteId */, @Nullable String opKey, com.google.gson.JsonObject ext)
```

#### 2.1 Checks

- Every site is the owner's, standing, inside the claim, in no other region; the roads are 4e roads along the given street line; every
  lot site's box faces the street. Else `NOT_ALLOWED` naming the site.
- The claim overlaps no other region of any owner beyond D1's seam rule, and no C17 area of another owner.
- No write, ticket or prepare.

#### 2.2 The synthesized IR

- Program `adopted_village` (kit, bundled, deterministic, `catalogue = false`): from `geometry`, the road sites' recorded specs and the
  lot boxes, it emits `ir.lots` (each `{id, box, front, entrance, adopted: siteId}`), `ir.roads` (each `{id: street_*, adopted:
  roadSiteId}`, flagged `architect_mc:street`), the graph (V's: lot nodes, junctions along the street, ends), and **no parts** (no ops,
  so no tile). `budget` 0.
- Its street ends are terminal junctions, so GR can extend them and D3 can join them.
- Its IR is revision 0; its frozen heights are taken at first touch by a later revision (6a D3).
- **Its artifact:** adopt writes a synthesized plan/0 artifact for the region (C36-kept, `region.adopted: true`, no tiles, its lots in
  `$.lots[]` with C36's members and the sites' ext), so a plan/0 revision can name it as `parentArtifact` (RV §9) and Steward's plan
  writer can grow the adopted village as any region.

#### 2.3 Group membership

- The region gets a new group `g<N>`. Each adopted site's membership moves to it (`Site.Member(group, batchId, itemKey)`), its old
  membership recorded in the region record (`adopted.from`) so un-adopt can restore it.
- One `adopt` journal entry per site is **not** written (the sites' own entries stand); the region record and the membership change
  are one atomic save.

### 3. Un-adopt and removal

- **`Regions.remove`** of an adopted region removes its group: every adopted site and road, plus every revision's cells, last placed
  first. That is exact as RV §6.2 (the sites' own entries restore their land).
- **`Regions.unadopt(regionId)`** (default throws): allowed only with no revision standing; restores each site's old membership and
  deletes the region record. No cell is written.

### 4. Gate (slice tier, $0): the 6d rows of the joint gate

| # | Check | Bar |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Unit | `adopted_village` IRs from 20 synthetic VillageLayout settlements: lots, roads and graph as V's for the same geometry; no parts |
| 2 | Adopt | a Steward-shaped VillageLayout settlement (Steward's own `VillageLayout` code path driven through its test hook, or the recorded site set of Steward's e2e village), adopted: 0 changed cells (hash), 0 journal entries written; `RegionView` lists its lots and street |
| 3 | A 6d addition | a GR growth of one lot on its street (frontage): through `checkPlan` of a revision plan naming the adopted artifact (Steward's plan writer shape: the adopted zone with one more lot) then `realiseApproved` |
| 4 | A 6d delta | `applyDelta` on one adopted lot (a stub v2) |
| 5 | Remove (verifier re-runs) | `Regions.remove`: E-flat 0 over the claim against the world before the settlement |
| 6 | Un-adopt | a second settlement adopted then un-adopted: memberships as before, Steward's own undo of one of its sites still works |
| 7 | Joint row (with 7a) | once 7a's link pass lands: its link pass over the adopted region, then rows 3-5 again (run on the integration branch) |

**Size:** 3-3.5 days, one builder. **Placeholders:** API **1.47.0**, mod **0.50.0**, kit **0.46.0**, catalogue unchanged.

### Byte identity, KC and Steward's asks

- Adoption writes nothing (hash, item 2); `adopted_village` is a new program, so no existing IR moves. KC: no writer. The 59 asks are
  unaffected. C12's joint gate is answered on the 6d side by rows 2-6; its 7a row waits for 7a.
